descent-lift.classical-record-reproduces.formal: With the record pair in the even mixture $\tfrac12(\ket{00}\bra{00} + \ket{11}\bra{11})$ and the same coupling $C$, the induced map on the pair is again the descent, but the joint output of a pure input has purity $\tfrac12$, against $1$ for the lift. One rung suffices for this: a single rung in the maximally mixed state $\tfrac12(\ket{0}\bra{0} + \ket{1}\bra{1})$, with the coupling $1 - 2P^{R}_{1}N_{0}$, also induces the descent, its joint output commuting with the total parity and again of purity $\tfrac12$. Two rungs are needed only for the coherent lift.
descent-lift.classical-record-reproduces.technical:
Prepare the record pair not in the paired state $\varphi$ but in the even mixture $\tfrac12(\ket{00}\bra{00} + \ket{11}\bra{11})$ and apply the same supplied-class coupling $C$. Since $C$ acts on the two record branches as $1$ and as $\G_{0}$, the induced map on the pair is $\tfrac12(\rho + \G_{0}\rho\G_{0})$, the descent, but the joint output of a pure input is an equal mixture of two orthogonal pure states, of purity $\tfrac12$ rather than the lift's $1$.

A single rung suffices for this classical version: in the maximally mixed state $\tfrac12(\ket{0}\bra{0} + \ket{1}\bra{1})$, with the coupling $1 - 2P^{R}_{1}N_{0}$, it again induces the descent, with a joint output that commutes with the total parity and again has purity $\tfrac12$. Two rungs are needed only for the coherent lift.
descent-lift.classical-record-reproduces.lay: The descent that erases a pair's entanglement can also be produced by coupling the pair to a record that is itself a random classical coin. That has the same effect on the pair, but the combined system ends up in a mixed state, so the erased information is not stored anywhere recoverable. A single extra mode is enough for this classical version; the second one is needed only when the record must keep the information coherently.

descent-lift.classical-shared-bit-reduce.formal:
Let the pair be in the thermofield state $c\ket{00} + s\ket{11}$, $(c, s) = (\tfrac45, \tfrac35)$. Its lift is the pure, even four-mode state
\[
c\,\ket{00} \otimes (\ket{00} + \ket{11}) + s\,\ket{11} \otimes (\ket{00} - \ket{11}),
\]
up to normalisation. The pair's marginal is $\operatorname{diag}(\tfrac{16}{25}, \tfrac{9}{25})$ on $\{\ket{00}, \ket{11}\}$, exactly the descent of the pair, the classical shared bit; each single mode of the pair keeps the thermal marginal $\operatorname{diag}(\tfrac{16}{25}, \tfrac{9}{25})$ of the singularity paper's sample point; and the record's marginal has the same spectrum $(\tfrac{16}{25}, \tfrac{9}{25})$. The entanglement of the pair, with Schmidt coefficients $(c, s)$ across the mode-mode cut, has become entanglement with the same Schmidt coefficients across the pair-record cut.
descent-lift.classical-shared-bit-reduce.technical:
Take the pair in the thermofield state $c\ket{00} + s\ket{11}$ at $(c, s) = (\tfrac45, \tfrac35)$. Applying the two-rung lift gives, up to normalisation, the pure even four-mode state $c\,\ket{00}\otimes(\ket{00} + \ket{11}) + s\,\ket{11}\otimes(\ket{00} - \ket{11})$.

Its marginal on the pair is $\operatorname{diag}(\tfrac{16}{25}, \tfrac{9}{25})$ on $\{\ket{00}, \ket{11}\}$, exactly the descent of the pair, the classical shared bit; each single mode keeps the thermal marginal $\operatorname{diag}(\tfrac{16}{25}, \tfrac{9}{25})$ of the singularity paper's sample point; and the record's marginal has the same spectrum. The pair's entanglement, with Schmidt coefficients $(c, s)$ across the mode-mode cut, reappears with the same Schmidt coefficients across the pair-record cut.
descent-lift.classical-shared-bit-reduce.lay: Take the series' sample entangled pair of modes, with amplitudes four fifths and three fifths. When the descent turns it into a classical shared bit, the lost coherence can be kept, using the two-rung lift, by a record made of two extra modes. The pair and record together are then in a single pure state, and the classical bit is simply what the pair looks like when the record is ignored. The entanglement that was between the two modes is now between the pair and the record, with the same strengths.

__notes__.note.descent-lift.setting-what-does-two-: \textbf{Verdict.} K1 to K4 do not trigger, in the corrected framing: the two-rung count for the pair and the one-rung-per-mode count in general (Theorem \claimref{descent-lift.lift-costs-one-rung-per-mode}(ii)); the necessity of a generator that fails to conserve number, a pairing among quadratic ones (Theorem \claimref{descent-lift.lift-costs-one-rung-per-mode}(v)); the coupling in the supplied class (Theorem \claimref{descent-lift.lift-costs-one-rung-per-mode}(iv)); the stored coherence with the pair's Schmidt coefficients (Corollary \claimref{descent-lift.classical-shared-bit-reduced-view-pure}). K5 triggers, as registered: nothing in the root paper's transport principle forces a map to be lifted, so the step from ``the descent is one-way'' to ``the descent should be lifted'' is a reading of the principle, not a consequence of it. Of the predictions, P3 held as registered; P1, P4, P5 and P6 held with the framing corrected as Remark \claimref{note.descent-lift.departures-registered-wording} records; P2 held as to the two quanta the record must gain and not as to where the pairing acts (item (4) of the remark); P7 held as to K5 and not as to the registered grade (item (5)).

\textbf{What this settles.} Run on the pairing creator, the transport algorithm returns type P at cost zero and hands back the pair annihilation, an element of the singularity paper's vacuum stabiliser (Fact \claimref{descent-lift.imported-descent-modes-univalence-supplied-class}); read through the type-N refinement instead, it returns the obstruction of the adjoined null vectors, which no equivariant element-level repair meets. Under Step 2 it adjoins nothing; under the refinement Step 3 adjoins a plane whose repair acts on points and returns no element from $n$; on neither reading is a rotation produced. The ascent itself contains the pairing and the hop on equal terms, as rotors of its own Spin group built from its own ladder elements, and it has a symmetry exchanging them (iv); that symmetry exchanges the parity sectors too, so it is a symmetry of the algebra and not an operation the univalence rule admits. So the transport principle neither produces nor excludes the pairing generator: what distinguishes a hop from a pairing is the vacuum, which of $f, f^{*}$ annihilates it, together with the parity grading the vacuum fixes, and the singularity paper's exclusion of pairing terms is a premise about that choice, not a consequence of transport. Clause (vi) says where the pairing generator lives: on the even sector of the pair, the creator and its pseudo-inverse are one effective ladder pair, Anderson's pseudospin \cite{Anderson1958}, and the pairing rotation is the rotation of that plane. The registered claim, that the principle produces the generator, is dead at Step 3 as the registration predicted; the kill conditions K1 to K3 of that registration triggered under Step 2, K4 held, every prediction P1 to P6 held, and clause (vii) is outside the registration.
__notes__.note.descent-lift.abstract:
The series' descent, the pinching onto the number-diagonal algebra, is one-way: the root paper proves no homomorphism returns, and the singularity paper shows it sends an entangled pair to a classical shared bit. This note treats the descent as a channel and asks whether it lifts as the transport principle lifts an element without an inverse: reversibly, by adjoining what it discards. It does, at an exact price. On the even (physical) states of $
u$ modes the descent has Kraus rank $2^{
u - 1}$, and an even isometric lift needs that many orthogonal even record states; $k$ rungs of the tower supply $2^{k - 1}$, so the minimal record is $
u$ rungs, one per mode. One lift is explicit: a coupling in the singularity paper's supplied class applied to a record prepared in the Thouless state with all pairing amplitudes one, by a rotation of the family whose member at amplitude $4/3$ is that paper's necessity witness. The pairing may sit on the record or on the pair; no number-conserving dynamics replaces it. The discarded coherence reappears as entanglement across the pair-record cut with the pair's Schmidt coefficients; the classical shared bit is the reduced view of a pure four-mode state. Seen from the two sides of the descent, the one-way door and the exclusion of pairing terms are one fact within the supplied dynamics. The lift does not touch the Hawking angle, and extending the principle from elements to maps is a reading, not a theorem.
__notes__.note.descent-lift.setting-setting-what-i:
The transport principle is a rule for elements: where an element has no inverse, adjoin the minimum that gives it one, and keep the descent that forgets the adjunction \cite[Thm.~4.13, Prop.~7.5, Thm.~7.6]{ButlerT1}. The descent is a conditional expectation, the pinching onto the algebra that commutes with the ladder's occupation projector, and it is one-way: no homomorphism returns from the ascent to the base. The singularity paper reads the same pinching, mode by mode, as the parity average $\EN(x) = \tfrac12(x + \G x\G)$ and, on several modes, as the pinching onto the joint-number-diagonal algebra \cite[Thm.~5.7, Prop.~9.6]{ButlerT5}; applied to an entangled pair $c\ket{00} + s\ket{11}$ it returns the classical shared bit $\operatorname{diag}(c^{2}, s^{2})$.

This note asks the inverted question. A map without an inverse can still be lifted: enlarged to a reversible map on a bigger system, followed by forgetting the enlargement. That is Stinespring's dilation, and it is the exact analogue for maps of what the transport principle does for elements. The question is whether the descent's lift can be built inside the tower, from rungs, by operations the framework's own premises allow, and what it costs. The answer is computed exactly, in the singularity paper's conventions, and the kill conditions of the section “The claim, and the kill conditions fixed before computation” were fixed before the computation.

Three things are fixed on this page. First, the states. The singularity paper's premise (P) says physical states of the modes are even, and its imported univalence rule says the observable algebra is the even subalgebra \cite[Prem.~7.8, Fact~7.9]{ButlerT5}. Everything below is stated on even states, and a single mode then has nothing to lift: its only even pure state is the vacuum, on which the descent is the identity. The descent's first physical action is on the pair. Second, the reduced state. For fermions the reduced state of a subsystem is the restriction of the joint state to the subsystem's algebra; the tensor-product partial trace agrees with it when the complementary factor is even, which is the only case the lift uses, and the script computes the restriction throughout. Third, the vocabulary, for a reader of quantum information who has not read the series: a \emph{rung} is one $(1,1)$ ascent of the tower, which adjoins one fermionic mode \cite[Thm.~4.2]{ButlerT3}; the \emph{descent} is the pinching above; the \emph{supplied class} is the set of generators the singularity paper's completion provides, polynomials in the parity sections $\sigma_{k} = 2N_{k} - 1$, all joint-number-diagonal \cite[Prem.~7.30, Thm.~C.8]{ButlerT5}; a \emph{pairing} generator is $a^{\dagger}_{i}a^{\dagger}_{j}$ or its adjoint, the part of $\mathfrak{so}(2\nu)$ that moves the vacuum \cite[Prop.~13.4]{ButlerT5}; and the two-ledger words \emph{transport-essential}, \emph{convenient} and \emph{absent} grade a result by whether the $(1,1)$ increment does irreplaceable work in it, some work, or none \cite{ButlerT17}.
__notes__.note.descent-lift.setting-machine-verifi:
Every computational identity asserted in this note has been verified in exact arithmetic by the script \texttt{verify\_T05\_dilation.py} \cite{ButlerVerifyT05dilation}, which imports the series' shared library \texttt{GA.py}: its Gaussian rationals and its exact ranks. Irrational normalisations are avoided by working with unnormalised isometries, $W^{\dagger}W = 2^{\nu-1}$, and unnormalised record states; the reduced state of a subsystem is computed as the restriction of the joint state to the subsystem's algebra, with the operators $\ket{Y}\bra{X}_{S}$ built from the system's ladder operators, and the tensor-product partial trace is used only as a cross-check on even records. No floating point is used anywhere; the script exits nonzero on any failure. Thirty-four checks, all passing, in eight parts. The two pre-registrations are deposited beside the script \cite{ButlerPreregT05dilation, ButlerPreregT05pairing}.

\emph{Part A: the channel.} The product of the two parity averages equals the joint-number-diagonal pinching on all sixteen matrix units of the pair and is idempotent on a random matrix; on the even sector it equals $\tfrac12(\rho + \G_{0}\rho\G_{0}) = \tfrac12(\rho + \G_{1}\rho\G_{1})$, with Choi rank $2$ there and $4$ on the full space; the descent of the thermofield pair is $\operatorname{diag}(\tfrac{16}{25}, \tfrac{9}{25})$ with coherence $\tfrac{12}{25}$ removed; on one mode the even sector is the vacuum line and the descent is the identity on it.

\emph{Part B: the record.} The even sector of $k$ rungs has $2^{k-1}$ basis states for $k \leq 4$; Stinespring's one-rung map and the occupation copy both induce the descent on the even sector and both fail evenness, the first producing a parity-mixed joint state from the vacuum, the second an odd joint state from $\ket{11}$.

\emph{Part C: the lift of the pair.} $W = 1 \otimes \ket{00} + \G_{0} \otimes \ket{11}$ is even, has $W^{\dagger}W = 2$ with $W\ket{00} \perp W\ket{11}$, and induces $2\EN$ on the even sector's matrix units; the tensor-product partial trace agrees with the algebraic restriction on the lifted states; $C = 1 - 2P^{R}_{11}N_{0}$ is diagonal, equals $1 - \tfrac14(1-\G_{0})(1-\G_{2})(1-\G_{3})$, commutes with every $N_{k}$ and the total parity, squares to $1$; and $W = C(\,\cdot \otimes \varphi)$ on both even basis states and on the pair.

\emph{Part D: the preparation.} $\varphi$ is even and a Witt vacuum with Thouless amplitude $1$; the hops, the annihilation and the Cartan elements annihilate the record vacuum while the pair creation carries it to $\ket{11}$; the rational pairing rotor is unitary, even, and carries $\ket{00}$ to $\tfrac35\ket{00} + \tfrac45\ket{11}$; ten number-conserving generators commute with the total number, and the enumeration of joint basis states at the required number and parity leaves only the record vacuum for both even system states; a beam splitter between the pair and a rung at $(\tfrac35, \tfrac45)$ moves weight $\tfrac{16}{25}$ out of $\ket{11}$; the system pairing $1 + (a^{\dagger}_{0}a^{\dagger}_{1} - a_{1}a_{0})$, conjugated by the two system-record swaps and followed by $C$, is an even map inducing $2\EN$ on the even sector; the annihilation $a_{2}a_{3}$ kills the record vacuum while its Hermitian completion $a_{2}a_{3} + a^{\dagger}_{3}a^{\dagger}_{2}$ carries it to $\ket{11}$; the quartic element $I_{4}N_{0}(a^{\dagger}_{2}a^{\dagger}_{3} - a_{3}a_{2})$ is Hermitian, even, kills the joint vacuum and fails to commute with the total number, and its rotation at $\pi/2$, entered in closed form, is a unitary, even map carrying $\psi \otimes \ket{00}$ to the two-rung occupation copy, which is even, induces $\EN$, and equals $W$ in the record basis $\ket{00} \pm \ket{11}$.

\emph{Part E: the stored coherence.} The lifted pair is pure and even; its pair marginal is the classical shared bit and equals the descent; the marginal of each of the two modes is $\operatorname{diag}(\tfrac{16}{25}, \tfrac{9}{25})$; the record marginal has trace $1$ and determinant $\tfrac{144}{625}$; the lifted state equals $c\ket{00}\ket{+} + s\ket{11}\ket{-}$; the partial-lift factors $1, \tfrac{7}{25}, 0, -\tfrac{7}{25}$ at $A = 0, \tfrac34, 1, \tfrac43$.

\emph{Part F: the classical records.} The even mixture on the record pair with the coupling $C$ induces the descent exactly and leaves the joint output at purity $\tfrac12$; a single rung in the maximally mixed state with the coupling $1 - 2P^{R}_{1}N_{0}$ does the same, its joint output commuting with the total parity.

\emph{Part G: three modes.} On the even sector of three modes the pinching has Choi rank $4$; the even sector of three rungs has dimension $4$ and of two rungs $2$; the four record states are even and orthonormal (each pair checked); $W$ is even with $W^{\dagger}W = 4$ and induces $4\EN$ on the sixteen even matrix units; the record preparation is an even Witt vacuum with all three amplitudes $1$.

\emph{Part H: the pairing creator under the transport algorithm.} In $\Cl(2,2)$ over the rationals: $n = f_{1}^{*}f_{2}^{*}$ is nonzero, pure grade $2$, square zero, the centre is the scalars, $f_{2}^{*}f_{2}$ and $f_{1}^{*}f_{1}$ are non-central idempotents with $n\,f_{2}^{*}f_{2} = 0$ and $f_{1}f_{1}^{*}n = 0$, and the annihilating idempotents $f_{2}f_{2}^{*}$ and $f_{1}^{*}f_{1}$ are $wv$ and $vw$ for the grade-one null pairs $(f_{2}^{*}, f_{2})$ and $(f_{1}^{*}, f_{1})$ with $vw + wv = 1$; the Fock adjoint is an anti-automorphism exchanging $f_{k}$ and $f_{k}^{*}$, and $n^{\dagger} = f_{2}f_{1}$ satisfies the four Penrose equations with $n$ and kills $P_{00}$; $f \wedge f^{*}$ squares to $\tfrac14$ and commutes with the number operator; the reflection $e_{4} \mapsto -e_{4}$ is an automorphism carrying $h$ to $n$, $X_{h}$ to $X_{p}$, $P_{00}$ to $P_{01}$, $P_{\mathrm{odd}}$ to $P_{\mathrm{even}}$ and the hop rotor to the pairing rotor; $X_{p} = \tfrac12(e_{1}e_{2} + e_{3}e_{4})$ and $X_{h} = \tfrac12(e_{1}e_{2} - e_{3}e_{4})$, $X_{p}^{2} = -P_{\mathrm{even}}$, $X_{h}^{2} = -P_{\mathrm{odd}}$, $X^{3} = -X$, both closed-form exponentials at $(\tfrac35, \tfrac45)$ are even with $R\widetilde{R} = 1 = RR^{\dagger}$, the pairing rotor carries $P_{00}$ to $\tfrac35P_{00} + \tfrac45 nP_{00}$ and the hop rotor fixes it; $nn^{\dagger} + n^{\dagger}n = P_{\mathrm{even}}$ with $P_{\mathrm{even}} + P_{\mathrm{odd}} = 1$; and the pinching of either rung erases $n, h, X_{p}, X_{h}$ and fixes $\sigma_{1}, \sigma_{2}, \sigma_{1}\sigma_{2}$.

What the script does not check: Facts \claimref{descent-lift.imported-pinching-one-way-door} to \claimref{descent-lift.imported-thouless-states-witt-vacua} (imports); clauses (i) to (iii) of Theorem \claimref{descent-lift.lift-costs-one-rung-per-mode} beyond $\nu = 2, 3$ and clauses (iv) and (v) beyond $\nu = 2$ (the proofs are by counting and by Fact \claimref{descent-lift.imported-stinespring-kraus-choi}); the coefficient argument in the proof of Proposition \claimref{descent-lift.within-supplied-dynamics-descent-has-no}, of which the script checks one annihilation and the one quartic exception; and, in Proposition \claimref{descent-lift.pairing-creator-under-transport-algorithm}, the imported taxonomy of Fact \claimref{descent-lift.imported-taxonomy-type-p-rule-algorithm} and the identity $XP = X$, which follows from $X^{3} = -X$.
__notes__.note.descent-lift.setting-claim-kill-con: The kill conditions and predictions below are as registered, in the deposited pre-registration \cite{ButlerPreregT05dilation}; every departure between that wording and what the note does is collected in Remark \claimref{note.descent-lift.departures-registered-wording}.

\textbf{Claim D (the descent lifts, at a price).} The descent has a lift within the tower: an even isometric dilation whose record is a set of rungs, realised by an even unitary that factorises as a coupling in the singularity paper's supplied class composed with a pairing rotation on the record. The coherence the descent discards is stored as system-record entanglement with Schmidt coefficients equal to the system's amplitudes. The only step outside the supplied class is the pairing rotation, so within the dynamics the framework supplies the descent has no lift: the root paper's one-way door and the singularity paper's exclusion of pairing terms are one fact.

\begin{itemize}
\item[K1] (one rung suffices) If an even isometric dilation of the single-mode parity average exists with a one-rung record, the count ``two rungs for one mode'' is dead. Test: the Kraus operators span $\{1, \G\}$, both even and number-diagonal, so an even isometry has the form $P_{0} \otimes r_{0} + P_{1} \otimes r_{1}$ with $r_{0}, r_{1}$ even record states that must be orthogonal ($\EN$ kills the coherence); the even sector of one rung is one-dimensional.
\item[K2] (no pairing needed) If an even unitary generated by number-conserving elements only (hops within the record, hops between system and record, Cartan elements, joint-number-diagonal couplings) realises a lift from the record vacuum, the clause ``the only step outside the supplied class is a pairing rotation'' is dead. Test: such a unitary conserves the total number, the joint state stays in total number $\leq \nu$, and the record's even states there are too few to be orthogonal.
\item[K3] (coupling outside the supplied class) If the controlled coupling $C$ of the factorisation is not joint-number-diagonal (not a polynomial in the parity sections), the factorisation clause is dead.
\item[K4] (coherence not stored) If the lifted state of $c\ket{0} + s\ket{1}$ does not have reduced spectrum $(c^{2}, s^{2})$ on the system and on the record, with the joint state pure, the reading ``the discarded coherence is the system-record entanglement'' is dead.
\item[K5] (the principle) The root paper's transport principle concerns elements without inverses. Applying it to a map without an inverse is an extension. If nothing in the root paper forces a non-invertible map to be lifted, the lift is a reading and the result is transport-convenient at most. Expected to trigger; recorded as such, not as a kill of the mathematics.
\end{itemize}
Predictions, as registered: the minimal even record for one mode is two rungs, in their even sector, and for $\nu$ modes $\nu + 1$ rungs, the per-mode product lift using $2\nu$ and not being minimal (P1); the record must leave its vacuum by two quanta, a pairing creation, and the stabiliser of the record vacuum fixes its ray (P2); $C = 1 - 2P^{R}_{11}P^{S}_{1}$ for one mode (P3); at $(c, s) = (\tfrac45, \tfrac35)$ the lifted state is $c\ket{0}\ket{+} + s\ket{1}\ket{-}$ with reduced spectra $(\tfrac{16}{25}, \tfrac{9}{25})$ on both sides, the system marginal being the thermal marginal at $e^{-\omega/T} = \tfrac{9}{16}$ (P4); the record preparation is the necessity witness rotation at amplitude $1$, and with amplitude $A$ the lift is a partial descent with coherence factor $(1 - A^{2})/(1 + A^{2})$ (P5); a one-rung stochastic version exists and records nothing recoverable (P6); K5 triggers, with ledger entry transport-convenient (P7).
__notes__.note.descent-lift.where-descent-first-ac: On a single mode the descent acts only on the odd-even coherence $\ket{0}\bra{1}$, which (P) declares unphysical: the single-mode descent is the identity on every physical state. The descent's first physical action is on the pair, and what it removes there is the pairing coherence between $\ket{00}$ and $\ket{11}$, the coherence that makes the pair entangled. That is the entangled-pair-to-classical-bit computation of the singularity paper's descent, and it is the object lifted below.
__notes__.note.descent-lift.departures-registered-:
Five, recorded in one place. (1) The registration framed the count on the full Fock space, where the single-mode descent has Kraus rank $2$ and the $
u$-mode descent rank $2^{
u}$, and predicted a minimal record of $
u + 1$ rungs (P1). On the physical, even states, which is where (P) places the framework and where the note is stated, the ranks are $1$ and $2^{
u-1}$ and the minimal record is $
u$ rungs; the single mode has nothing to lift, and the pair is the base case. The full-space count $
u + 1$ is correct for the descent of unphysical coherences and is not the note's result. (2) K1 was framed for one mode, where on even states there is nothing to lift; its test, that the even record states must be orthogonal and one rung has one, applies unchanged to the pair, and Corollary \claimref{descent-lift.parity-alone-forces-second-rung} records that both one-rung maps do induce the descent and fail by parity alone. (3) K4, P4, P5 and P6 were stated for a single mode $c\ket{0} + s\ket{1}$, which is not an even state; the note states them for the pair $c\ket{00} + s\ket{11}$, where every number predicted holds. (4) Claim D, K2 and P2 as registered place the pairing rotation on the record. Theorem \claimref{descent-lift.lift-costs-one-rung-per-mode}(v) shows it may be placed on the system instead and carried to the record by hops; the clause that survives is that no number-conserving dynamics lifts, and the lift of Theorem \claimref{descent-lift.lift-costs-one-rung-per-mode}(iv) places the pairing on the record as registered. (5) P7 as registered named the ledger entry transport-convenient; the grade found is transport-absent, for the reason given below.
__notes__.note.descent-lift.setting-what-does-two-: \textbf{Prior art, and the two ledgers.} The dilation, the Kraus form and the minimal environment are Stinespring, Kraus and Choi; the parity constraint is the univalence rule in its operational form; the Thouless state and the Witt vacuum are imports. What the note proves for itself is the even-state Kraus rank $2^{\nu-1}$, the count of one rung per mode with the second rung forced by parity, the explicit lift and its factorisation into a supplied-class coupling and a pairing rotation, the identification of that rotation with the singularity paper's witness family, the number-conservation obstruction and its indifference to where the pairing acts, the stored-coherence and partial-lift computations, and Proposition \claimref{descent-lift.within-supplied-dynamics-descent-has-no}. Under the two-ledger discipline the result is transport-absent: the rungs are where the record lives and the count matches the tower's one mode per rung, but the lift exists for any $\nu$ fermionic modes adjoined by any means, the univalence rule and Stinespring's theorem fix the count without the $(1,1)$ increment, and the transport principle does not force the lift (K5). The ascent supplies the vocabulary in which the record is counted, not a step the argument needs; and Proposition \claimref{descent-lift.pairing-creator-under-transport-algorithm} shows that the creator from which the one generator the argument needs is built is one the principle classifies as costing nothing.

\textbf{What it does not do.} It does not touch the angle. The amplitudes $(c, s)$ of the pair are inputs to the lift, not outputs; the Hawking temperature enters through the singularity paper's regularity premise exactly as before. The record is an adjoined system, not a spatially separated one, and nothing here is a Bell test, a coupling Hamiltonian between separated regions, a global positive-frequency splitting, a non-Gaussian state, or an invariant measure of entanglement; the lift moves the pair's entanglement one cut outward and calibrates what that costs, and that is all it does.

\textbf{Consequences for the owning papers.} For the root paper: Theorem 7.6 can carry a clause, and Proposition \claimref{descent-lift.pairing-creator-under-transport-algorithm}(i) records a point for it to settle: Step 2 diagnoses a product of two adjoined null vectors by its grade, as type P, while Theorem 3.9(2) refines it to type N by the origin of its annihilating idempotent; the two branches agree that no element is returned, and the root paper should say which diagnosis governs such products. The pinching's kernel, the ladder sector, is recoverable by an even isometry into $\nu$ further rungs, one per pinched mode, so the door is one-way for algebra homomorphisms and for the dynamics the completion supplies, and two-way for the tower if a pairing rotation is admitted. For the singularity paper: Premise 7.30's pairing clause now has a second characterisation beside Proposition 13.4's tangent: among quadratic generators the pairing terms are exactly those whose absence makes the descent irreversible, and Corollary 11.6's witness rotation is the record preparation of the descent's lift at amplitude $\tfrac43$, which overshoots (Corollary \claimref{descent-lift.partial-lifts-witness-overshoots}); the complete lift is its member at amplitude $1$. Successor problems: whether the framework's own tower selects the amplitude $1$, that is, whether anything in the ascent prefers the maximally paired record; whether the lift composes along the tower, the record of the record costing $\nu$ further rungs each time; and the angle, which this note leaves where it found it.

__notes__.note.descent-lift.reading: The tower adjoins one mode per rung and one qubit per rung \cite[Thm.~4.2]{ButlerT3}. The theorem says the descent's reversible lift costs exactly that: one rung per mode of the system, and the count is forced by univalence, not by the dimension of the environment, which Stinespring alone would put at $2^{\nu-1}$ states of any kind, $\nu - 1$ qubits, one rung fewer. What the second rung buys, for the pair, is a two-level record that is the even sector of a mode pair rather than a single mode. __notes__.note.descent-lift.setting-what-does-two-: \textbf{One fact.} The root paper proves that the descent is one-way at the level of algebras: no homomorphism returns. The singularity paper premises that the completion supplies no generator off-diagonal in the joint number basis, and its own envelope corollary shows that one pairing rotation is what the return of its boundary modes needs. Proposition \claimref{descent-lift.within-supplied-dynamics-descent-has-no} joins the two: inside the dynamics the framework supplies, the descent cannot be lifted, and the missing ingredient is a pairing rotation, on the adjoined rungs or on the modes themselves. The one-way door and the pairing exclusion are the same statement seen from the two sides of the descent.

\emph{Proved in this paper, at the standard of \cite{ButlerT1}:} the single-mode modular structure (Proposition \claimref{hawking.modular-structure-completed-pair}); the Gibbs/KMS equivalence with uniqueness in finite dimensions and the restriction lemma (Lemmas \claimref{hawking.gibbs-states-are-kms-conversely-finite}, \claimref{hawking.kms-restricts-invariant-subalgebras}). __notes__.note.hawking.what-now-proved-open-proble: Three levels, stated separately. \emph{Proved here:} within the quasi-free class the state is unique, with gauge invariance and the Fermi-Dirac symbol both forced by the KMS identity (Theorem \claimref{hawking.i-state}); in this sense the I-state is the framework's equilibrium vacuum, and the quasi-free restriction is a convenience of proof, removed at the next level. \emph{Imported:} given the boost dynamics and $\beta$, full uniqueness among all states (Corollary \claimref{hawking.full-uniqueness-given-dynamics}, from Fact \claimref{hawking.imported-ideal-fermi-gas-uniqueness}). \emph{Open, and named:} deriving the dynamics itself, i.e.\ an axiom selecting the boost flow and its temperature from the geometry. T5 has already treated this question at the level of a single factor: its geometric modular condition (G) is formulated and rejected there as over-determining the boundary modes, its premise (R) is proved irreducible, its rate-rigidity theorem shows the temperature is not algebra-intrinsic, and the resulting state class is recorded \cite[Def.~7.12, Thms.~7.16 and 7.28, Cor.~7.32]{ButlerT5}. The question this paper poses is different and remains open: a \emph{net-level} selection in the style of geometric modular action \cite{BDFS2000}, demanding that the modular groups of a net of boundary-mode algebras act geometrically and deriving the boost identification for the whole net rather than assuming it. Within the single atom the algebra already forces the orbits of any rotor-implemented flow, though not its speed (Proposition \claimref{hawking.modular-structure-completed-pair}(5)); the execution for the net is a successor problem (the section “Scope, and successor problems”). \emph{Point of contact:} the I-state on a horizon pair is Israel's thermofield double \cite{Israel1976}, and its GNS representation is the Araki-Wyss doubling; the non-equilibrium state of the descent, the cosmological state problem, is outside this paper's scope (successor problem 5).
__notes__.note.hawking.which-dynamics-what-level: The one-particle Hamiltonian $h$ was supplied by the geometry: the Schwarzschild frequency of each boundary mode, with the temperature's coefficient fixed by the surface gravity (Fact \claimref{hawking.imported-modular-descent-premises-geometric-normalisation}); in rapidity the weights are $\omega/\kappa$ at modular temperature $2\pi$. Two notes on scope. First, the greybody filtering of the section “The four-dimensional lift” does \emph{not} deform $h$ or the KMS structure: transmission through the exterior barrier is a property of the propagation from the horizon to infinity, not of the horizon algebra; conflating the two is what the interface premise (I) of Assembly \claimref{hawking.greybody-inheritance-under-interface-premise} guards against, and it is named in that assembly's statement. Second, the identification of the mode set (which $(\omega, \ell, m)$ channels, with which degeneracies) is a modelling input from the standard near-horizon reduction; the theorems of this section are exact for whatever separable $(\mathfrak{h}, h)$ that input delivers; the algebra supplies the theorems and the physics supplies the input.
__notes__.note.hawking.setting-position-series:
This paper is T7 of the series. \emph{It relies on six predecessors:} the primer T0 \cite{ButlerT0} and the root paper T1 \cite{ButlerT1} for the completed-pair language and the transport principle; the tower paper T3 \cite{ButlerT3} for the CAR limit that makes the boundary modes an algebra (Fact \claimref{hawking.imported-algebra-boundary-modes-car-algebra}); the singularity paper T5 \cite{ButlerT5} for modular descent under its premises (P) and (R), the bosonisation bridge under (Q), and the surface gravity $\kappa = 1/4M$ (Facts \claimref{hawking.imported-modular-descent-premises-geometric-normalisation} and \claimref{hawking.imported-s-wave-bosonic-sector}); the interior paper T6 \cite{ButlerT6} for the exterior exactness that greybody inheritance rests on (Fact \claimref{hawking.imported-exterior-exactly-general-relativity}); and the twistor paper T9 \cite{ButlerT9} for the ordering shift from which Proposition \claimref{hawking.homogeneity-ordering-shift} is promoted.

__notes__.note.hawking.abstract: This paper is a quantum companion to T5: it supplies the state, the continuum, and the four-dimensional lift between T5's single-mode core and the physical Hawking spectrum, each claim at its tier. Tier A: among the quasi-free states of the boundary modes' CAR algebra exactly one is KMS for the geometry's boost at the Hawking temperature, the I-state; existence is window-exact, carried to the full algebra by imported inductive-limit results; the KMS identity itself forces the pairing to vanish and the symbol to be Fermi-Dirac, all modes at once, extending T5's single-mode occupancy theorem; uniqueness beyond the class is the imported ideal-Fermi-gas theorem; and the statements carry to the continuum on a dense core. Tier B, the joints itemised: the helicity lift and greybody inheritance, whose only joint proved in this paper, the homogeneity $-2s-2$, is promoted to a stated result from inside the proof of the twistor paper's dictionary theorem; the exterior coincides with general relativity on the invertible region at $\Lambda = 0$, so the flux prediction equals Hawking's, filtering included. Tier A again: the finite mode space's deviations from the free-boson current algebra are edge-supported by an exact commutator identity; and, on the linear s-wave ladder of T5's premise (Q), an exact Planck factor with proven exponential window tails. The $\ell_P^2/A$ scale of generic corrections is a dimensional reading at modelling level; the per-observable scaling is open. Open and named: axiomatic selection of the dynamics, the lift beyond assembly, the Kerr continuum. Exact-arithmetic checks verify the identities.
__notes__.note.hawking.setting-prior-art: The prior work is acknowledged once, here. Hawking's radiance is \cite{Hawking1975}. The thermofield-double reading of the eternal black hole is Israel's \cite{Israel1976}; the identification of modular flow with the boost for wedge algebras is Bisognano-Wichmann \cite{BisognanoWichmann1976}, with Sewell's black-hole reading \cite{Sewell1982}. Quasi-free states of the CAR algebra and their two-point calculus are Araki's \cite{Araki1971}; KMS theory, the ideal Fermi gas, and the inductive-limit results are standard in Bratteli-Robinson \cite{BratteliRobinson1997}. The geometric-modular-action programme, the candidate axiom for state selection, is Buchholz-Dreyer-Florig-Summers \cite{BDFS2000}. The Penrose transform is \cite{Penrose1969, EPW1981}; greybody filtering through the Regge-Wheeler and Teukolsky barriers is \cite{ReggeWheeler1957, Teukolsky1973, Page1976}. The boson-fermion correspondence and the charge-zero Fock isomorphism are classical two-dimensional field theory \cite{FrenkelKac1980}. Weinberg-Witten is \cite{WeinbergWitten1980} and the soft-graviton universality is \cite{Weinberg1964}. What this paper claims as new is the transport assembly: the I-state theorem at the operator level, all modes at once, with pairing and symbol both forced by the KMS identity (the single-mode occupancy is derived the same way in \cite{ButlerT5}); the exact finite-window continuum statements and the limit with its imports declared; the promotion of the homogeneity computation inside the proof of \cite{ButlerT9}'s dictionary theorem to a stated result the transform can consume; the identification of the lift's remaining joints with theorems of this series (the exterior exactness of \cite{ButlerT6}); and the quantified edge-support of the finite-mode corrections.
__notes__.note.hawking.setting-setting-imports: Units are $G = c = \hbar = k_B = 1$ throughout, so for Schwarzschild the surface gravity is $\kappa = 1/4M$, the Hawking temperature is $\TH = \kappa/2\pi = 1/8\pi M$, the modular period is $\beta := 1/\TH = 8\pi M$, and areas are in Planck units, $\ell_P = 1$. (Two symbols are nonetheless kept visible where they carry the point: $\hbar$ in the section “The four-dimensional lift”, where the ordering shift is a multiple of it, and $\ell_P$ in the section “The finite boundary mode space, and the $\ell_P^2/A$ correction”, where the corrections scale as $\ell_P^2/A$, $A$ the horizon area.)
__notes__.note.hawking.setting-single-mode-self-co: The unit of the boundary mode space is a completed null pair: vectors $v, v^*$ with $v^2 = (v^*)^2 = 0$ and $vv^* + v^*v = 1$, the ladder pair the transport principle adjoins \cite{ButlerT1}. Everything modular about a single mode is elementary and is proved here outright, per the series' standard.
__notes__.note.hawking.setting-successor-problems:
Six problems for the series' list of open directions.

\begin{enumerate}
\item \emph{State selection from geometry.} Formulate the geometric-modular-action axiom for a net of boundary-mode algebras over the horizon and derive the boost dynamics, the temperature entering through the net's geometric normalisation rather than as an algebra-intrinsic quantity, which T5's rate-rigidity theorem shows it cannot be \cite[Thm.~7.16]{ButlerT5}. Proposition \claimref{hawking.modular-structure-completed-pair}(5) fixes the single-atom orbits, and T5's factor-level analysis (its condition (G), rejected as over-determining) records what is already established.
\item \emph{The lift beyond assembly.} Derive joint J3, the partial-wave identification, from the emergent transverse geometry (the fuzzy sphere of the counting programme), converting the helicity lift (Assembly \claimref{hawking.helicity-lift-joints-itemised}) from assembly to theorem; shared with the entropy paper T8 \cite{ButlerT8} and the action paper T10 \cite{ButlerT10}.
\item \emph{The Kerr continuum.} Superradiant channels make the rotating analogue of Theorem \claimref{hawking.i-state-continuum} genuinely different (no global KMS state at fixed angular velocity for all modes); formulate the correct rotating statement.
\item \emph{The $\ell_P^2/A$ correction, per observable.} Refine Remark \claimref{note.hawking.p-2-correction-interpreted} into a table of leading finite-$L$ corrections for named observables (spectrum distortion, correlator deficits), with the $\ell_P^2/A$ scaling proved rather than dimensional.
\item \emph{The cosmological state.} Connect the equilibrium I-state to the non-equilibrium state of the descent.
\item \emph{Helicity counting per boundary mode.} Decide whether one boundary mode of the near-horizon theory carries one helicity channel of the lift or both helicities of a massless species. The two answers differ downstream by a factor of two in the capacity per boundary mode ($\ln 2$ against $2\ln 2$) and so in the entropy paper's calibration residue, $\kappa_c = 1/(4\ln 2)$ against $1/(8\ln 2)$ \cite[Prop.~4.12]{ButlerT8}. In this paper the question sits at joint J3 of Assembly \claimref{hawking.helicity-lift-joints-itemised}, the partial-wave identification of each $(\omega, \ell, m, s)$ channel with a two-dimensional mode, which is modelling; joints J1 and J2 place the two helicities at distinct homogeneities but do not say how many channels one boundary mode registers. T8 takes the one-helicity reading, at the tier of that joint; settling it is part of converting J3 to a theorem (problem 2).
\end{enumerate}
__notes__.note.state-selection.setting-univalence-: Premise \claimref{singularity.p-univalence} is available to the chain for a reason the chain itself supplies: the ledger is a CAR algebra by the tower limit \cite[Thm.~5.6]{ButlerT3}, its grading is the Clifford grading of Definition \claimref{obj.singularity.grading-parity-automorphism}, and by Theorem \claimref{singularity.descent-parity-average} its even part is exactly the metric-level algebra. What the univalence rule asserts is that the odd sector carries no expectation values, and Theorem \claimref{singularity.descent-parity-average} says that this is the same as asserting that the ascended and descended readings agree \emph{per mode}. That is a considerably weaker demand than boost invariance of the whole state, and it is not a choice of state: it is a statement about which elements of the algebra are observables.
__notes__.note.singularity.setting-what-selects-st: The chain is entitled to (P) for a reason it supplies itself: the boundary modes form a CAR algebra, one pair per point of $E$ (Fact \claimref{singularity.imported-one-sided-completion-singularity}; the tower limit \cite[Thm.~5.6]{ButlerT3} is its algebraic model), its grading is the Clifford grading of Definition \claimref{obj.singularity.grading-parity-automorphism}, and by Theorem \claimref{singularity.descent-parity-average} its even part is, mode by mode, exactly the metric-level algebra (the multi-mode metric level is the joint-diagonal algebra, whose licence is Proposition \claimref{singularity.p-reduced-metric-level-reading-many}, one parity per point rather than the product of all of them). What (P) asserts is that the odd sector carries no expectation values, which by that theorem is the same as asserting that the ascended and descended readings agree \emph{mode by mode}. That is a much weaker demand than invariance of the whole state under the boost flow, and it is not a choice of state at all: it is a statement about which elements of the boundary mode space are observables.
__notes__.note.singularity.setting-finite-mode-mod: This section contains the paper's new computation: an exactly solvable model, small enough that every claim is a finite calculation in exact arithmetic, in which the chain's conceptual endpoint can be followed step by step, at both levels. The model is a toy and is offered as one; its role is to exhibit, not to derive. What it exhibits, exactly rather than approximately: every single radiated quantum is thermal; the joint radiation state ends pure; the information is carried by inter-quanta correlations invisible to any single-quantum measurement; the entropy of the radiation rises exactly along $\Sth$, falls under the eviction mechanism of Theorem \claimref{singularity.eviction-window-thermal-product-radiation-entropy}, and returns to zero, with the falling branch strictly inside the envelope by exactly the per-quantum shortfall the theorem quantifies; and, in the section “The descent, applied: the two levels in numbers”, the descent of Definition \claimref{obj.singularity.multi-mode-descent} is applied to the radiation outright, so that the metric-level reading of the same history is also computed rather than described.
__notes__.note.singularity.setting-descent-applied: Everything so far in this section lies at the ascended level: the states, marginals and correlators of the completed description. The chain's conclusion, however, is a comparison of two levels, so the model must also be read in the second one. This subsection does exactly that: it applies the multi-mode descent $\EN$ of Definition \claimref{obj.singularity.multi-mode-descent} to the radiation itself and tabulates both readings side by side; per Remark \claimref{note.singularity.where-descent-acts-hawkings-loss-derived}, this is the counterfactual reading, the one the closure does not perform, and it is where the entire nonzero deficit lies, the window marginal being an $\EN$ fixed point at every stage. Every number below is a rational number, computed and verified exactly.
__notes__.note.one-relation.setting-two-presentati: \textbf{The relation in words.} Multiply two directions in either order, add the results, and what comes back is a number rather than a direction: that is the whole of $\{e_{a}, e_{b}\} = 2g_{ab}\mathbf{1}$. Taken on one direction with itself it says that a displacement squared is its own interval, which along a timelike direction is what a clock carried there reads. The same relation decides which directions have zero interval, because $g$ is what says so, and in the plane spanned by the time direction and any one spatial direction there are two such: the opposite light rays $n_{\pm} = \tfrac12(e_{0} \pm e_{1})$, for which the relation gives $n_{\pm}^{2} = 0$ and $\{n_{+}, n_{-}\} = 1$, the real null pair of the proof above. Those are the relations of a fermionic ladder pair, so $n_{+}^{2} = 0$ is at once the statement that a light ray has no length and the statement that no state holds two identical fermions. The two rays are not yet a creation operator and an annihilation operator, because nothing in the relation says which is which. Both are future directed, so a time orientation does not separate them; what does is the orientation of the plane they span, the sign of the bivector $\sigma = e_{0}e_{1}$, since $n_{-}n_{+} = \tfrac12(1 + \sigma)$ and $n_{+}n_{-} = \tfrac12(1 - \sigma)$ are the two occupation projectors and choosing the sign of $\sigma$ is choosing which of them counts as occupied. Reversing $e_{0}$ alone, or $e_{1}$ alone, swaps the roles; reversing both leaves them fixed. This is the sense in which the flag of Fact \claimref{one-relation.imported-flag-arrow-superselection} is a $\mathbb{Z}_{2}$ orientation and not a frame vector, and $\sigma$ is the boost generator whose rotor flow rescales the pair in Lemma \claimref{one-relation.third-constant-conversion-constant-between-charts}(iii) and which the singularity paper reads as its clock \cite{ButlerT5}. Once the sign is chosen the plane carries the kinematics of one fermionic mode: a two-state system with exclusion built in, and nothing more than that. Dynamics, a Hamiltonian, and the complex structure the usual Fock space needs are not in the relation and are not claimed here; over $\R$ the plane's algebra is $\Cl(1,1) \cong \Mat(2, \R)$, the real form of the one-mode CAR. The script checks the two projector identities, $\sigma n_{\pm} = \mp n_{\pm}$, and the three sign reversals.
__notes__.note.one-relation.measurement-recording-: What the framework can say, under Premise \claimref{one-relation.recording-irreversible-stated-so-it-can}: after a measurement, interference between flag sectors is as inaccessible as inter-tower coherence, the superselection mechanism of the dark-towers paper operating in miniature, at laboratory scale (Fact \claimref{one-relation.imported-flag-arrow-superselection}); the step from unwritten records to inaccessible interference is the decoherence argument \cite{Zeh1970, JoosZeh1985}, and it is the first gap Proposition \claimref{one-relation.record-chain-votes-measurement-without-collapse} names and states with its cost. What it cannot yet say: why one outcome obtains rather than all persisting in parallel record chains. The recording is compatible with both readings empirically, and no present instrument distinguishes them. What the framework's own principles nonetheless say is Proposition \claimref{one-relation.record-chain-votes-measurement-without-collapse}.
__notes__.note.scrambling.abstract:
T5's counting step enters with two conditional inputs, the counted epoch and the per-cell density. This paper is the derivation programme for that count, with the dynamics and observational record of the boundary modes, at declared tiers. Proved: the stretched singularity is scheme-robust; its slice volume per unit Killing time is exactly $8\pi M$ at leading order under the framework's own curvature cutoff; the count $N = 8\pi
u M\Delta t/\lP^2$ reproduces the Bekenstein-Hawking entropy exactly when $
u\Delta t = M/2$; and the internal cutoff's mass scaling is the unique one from which an admissible timescale of order $M$ reaches the area law. Conditional, on the flagged intrinsic-clock premise: the epoch is the modular period $ eta = 8\pi M$, collapsing two unknowns into the single falsifiable density $
u = 1/16\pi$ in the 1-nat convention, equivalently the integer-holographic statement that the boundary mode space registers $\SBH$ fermions per modular period, up to the absorbed $\ln 2$: one per four Planck cells of horizon; the naive reading overshoots by exactly the horizon-area coefficient $16\pi$. The transverse sphere emerges by Kostant's principal embedding with principality forced by the flagged indifference premise, the fuzzy count matching the slice geometry and both naive aggregations refuted. The clocks of the boundary modes run at exactly $2\pi T$, so operator spreading saturates the chaos bound by construction, at free-fermion tier. The observational record: the registered no-echo prediction stands consistent across four gravitational-wave catalogues, one confirmed echo train from refutation. Forty-seven exact-arithmetic checks certify the computational identities.
__notes__.note.scrambling.setting-introduction:
T5 of this series \cite{ButlerT5} uses the singularity's boundary mode space twice: its capacity caps the radiation's fine-grained entropy (the falling branch of the Page curve), and its count is the area law. Both uses rest on a counting formula with two inputs T5 imports conditionally and flags: the counted \emph{epoch} $\Delta t$, and the per-cell mode density $
u$. This paper is the derivation programme for that count, together with the dynamics of the boundary modes (scrambling) and its observational record (echoes). The paper says its level in every section: what is proved is proved at the standard of \cite{ButlerT1}; what is conditional carries its named premise; what is assembled from results proved elsewhere stands in an \emph{Assembly}, its component results and their sources displayed and no proof claimed; and what is observational stands in a \emph{Record}, resting on the cited survey record with the date attached.

Five strands organise the paper. \emph{The count} (the section “The count”): the stretched singularity is scheme-robust at order one, its slice volume per unit Killing time is exactly $8\pi M$ in Planck units to leading order under the framework's own curvature cutoff, the resulting count $N = 8\pi
u M\Delta t/\lP^2$ reproduces the Bekenstein-Hawking entropy exactly when $
u\Delta t = M/2$, and the mass scaling produced by the internal cutoff is the \emph{unique} one for which an admissible timescale of order $M$ reaches the area law. \emph{The epoch} (the section “The epoch is the modular period”): on the flagged premise that the counted epoch is intrinsic to the boundary modes, it can only be the modular period $ eta = 8\pi M$: every intrinsic clock of the boundary modes runs at the modular rate $\kappa$, so every one carries the period $ eta$; the conversion is exact and holds in both directions, collapsing the pair $(\Delta t, 
u)$ into the single falsifiable prediction $
u = 1/16\pi$ in the 1-nat convention, whose integer-holographic equivalent is that the boundary mode space registers $\SBH$ fermions per modular period, up to the absorbed per-mode $\ln 2$: one per four Planck cells of horizon. \emph{The sphere} (the section “The transverse sphere from the boundary modes”): the transverse angular geometry is derived from the correlation structure, by Kostant's principal embedding with principality forced by the indifference principle, and the fuzzy operator count $n^2$ reproduces the slice sphere's Planck-cell scaling exactly; the two naive aggregation rules both fail, in instructive ways, and the failure is quantified. \emph{The dynamics} (the section “Scrambling, and the return delay”): the intrinsic flows of the boundary modes are all bivector-generated and the only ones the geometry converts to Schwarzschild time are the hyperbolic ones, all at the common rate $\kappa$, so operator spreading is boost-hyperbolic and the scrambling time is $( eta/2\pi)\ln S$: the chaos bound is saturated by construction, at free-fermion tier, with genuine chaos beyond it named as open. \emph{The record} (the section “The observational record”): the framework's quantum structure lies at the stretched singularity and nowhere near the horizon, so the registered prediction is an unmodified Kerr ringdown with no echoes, and the catalogue record through GWTC-4.0 is confronted, with the confrontation's openness stated.

__notes__.note.state-selection.setting-gap-stated-:
Step 4d of T5 \cite{ButlerT5} proves the following. Let the completed ladder pair $(v, v^{*})$ of the singular locus carry a state that is (i) pure, (ii) invariant under the boost flow generated by $\sigma$, and (iii) entangling across the two ends of the pair, that is cyclic and separating for the one-sided subalgebra. Then the descended state is KMS for the boost flow at modular temperature $2\pi$ of rapidity, which by the geometric calibration of \cite[Prop.~6.2]{ButlerT5} is
\[
T \;=\; \frac{\kappa}{2\pi} \;=\; \frac{1}{8\pi M} \;=\; \TH ,
\]
with per-mode reduced density matrix the Fermi-Dirac matrix. The theorem is stated with its converse: a state violating (ii) or (iii) reduces non-thermally under the same projector. The status line in the chain table reads \emph{up to a state}, and the paper says in as many words that the projection alone cannot select a temperature and that it does not pretend otherwise.

That admission is the point of departure here. Every derivation of the Hawking effect meets the same wall. Hawking's original calculation \cite{Hawking1975} selects the state by the collapse history and the choice of an ``in'' vacuum; Hartle and Hawking \cite{HartleHawking1976} select it by regularity of a Euclidean path integral; Unruh \cite{Unruh1976} by regularity on the future horizon; Boulware's alternative \cite{Boulware1975} is the same field theory with a different state and radiates nothing; Kay and Wald \cite{KayWald1991} prove, in the rigorous setting, that a stationary nonsingular quasi-free state on a spacetime with a bifurcate Killing horizon is unique when it exists, and is KMS at the Hawking temperature, which is exactly a theorem about the strength of the regularity premise; and Fredenhagen and Haag \cite{FredenhagenHaag1990} localise the input to the short-distance behaviour of the state near the horizon. The wall is not an accident of any one formalism, and it is not a wall this note claims to knock down.

What this note does claim is that the wall stands in a different place than Step 4d's three hypotheses suggest, and that once it is put in the right place, two of the three hypotheses are theorems, the third is an output, and what remains is one real number and one named premise. The results, with statuses, are in the table accompanying \claimref{singularity.descent-parity-average}.

\emph{The results of this note and what each does to Step 4d's hypotheses. (P) is the univalence premise of the section “The descent is the parity map”; (R) the regularity premise of the section “Fixing the rate: one premise, and its habitat inside the framework”; (L$_E$) the ledger locality premise of the section “What equilibrium cannot supply: correlations”.}

The one-sentence summary is this. Thermality of a single fermionic mode is not a property that a state can fail to have, so the state-selection problem in Step 4d is not about the shape of the reduced density matrix at all; it is about one number, the number is a ratio of two clocks, and a ratio of clocks requires a calibration that no amount of algebra can supply. The chain's contribution is that it says exactly which two clocks, and proves that the calibration enters exactly once.
__notes__.note.state-selection.what-was-bought: Theorem \claimref{singularity.ascended-marginals-are-diagonal} replaces hypothesis (ii), a symmetry assumption about the state, with (P), a statement about which elements of the ledger are observable. It is strictly weaker: (ii) constrains the whole state, (P) constrains one complex number per mode. It is also more robust, and this matters for the chain: (ii) is an equilibrium condition, and the evaporating hole is not in equilibrium, while (P) holds throughout an arbitrary non-stationary history. the section “What equilibrium cannot supply: correlations” shows that this robustness is not a luxury but a necessity, because the exact equilibrium condition is provably too strong for what Steps 5 and 6b need.
__notes__.note.state-selection.setting-one-tempera: Theorem \claimref{singularity.ascended-marginals-are-diagonal} leaves a function $k \mapsto \beta_k$. Two questions remain: why is it constant, and what fixes the constant.
__notes__.note.state-selection.why-rescues-rather-:
Read carelessly, Theorem \claimref{singularity.exact-equilibrium-over-determines-boundary-modes} looks like an obstruction: the state that thermality wants is the state that has no information in it. Read carefully, it is the reason the architecture of this note matters. Had per-mode thermality been derived from the exact equilibrium condition, as hypothesis (ii) suggests, then thermality and correlation would have been in direct competition and the chain could not have had both. Theorem \claimref{singularity.ascended-marginals-are-diagonal} shows that per-mode thermality does not rest on equilibrium at all: it rests on parity, which survives an arbitrary non-stationary history. The correct state class for the chain is therefore
\[
\bigl\{\ \text{even states, per-mode populations at } \beta = 2\pi/\kappa, \ \text{correlations free}\ \bigr\},
\]
a class in which every single quantum is exactly thermal and the joint state is free to carry everything the evaporation writes. That is exactly the class the finite-ledger model of \cite[\S 12]{ButlerT5} inhabits, and \cite[Lem.~12.1]{ButlerT5} is the model's proof that it does.

\emph{Step 4d after this note. The status line ``up to a state'' becomes ``proved from (P) and (R)''.}

The proposed status line for the chain table of \cite[Table 1]{ButlerT5} is therefore \emph{proved from (P), (R)} rather than \emph{up to a state}, with the two premises named in the row's own text, in exactly the manner Steps 6a and 6b already name (C1) to (C3) and (U), (C), (F). That is not a cosmetic change: it moves Step 4d from the class of results that await a state to the class of results that hold given premises the reader can inspect, which is the standard the rest of the chain is held to.

What has been relocated rather than removed is this. The chain's residual state dependence is now entirely in the correlations, and the correlations are the business of Step 6b, where the rate model already prices them by (U), (C) and (I). Theorem \claimref{singularity.exact-equilibrium-over-determines-boundary-modes} adds one thing to that pricing which was not previously visible: the correlations cannot be obtained from any equilibrium principle whatsoever, so no sharpening of Step 4d will ever supply them, and the search for a state-selection principle that delivers both thermality and the Page curve is a search for something that provably does not exist in the equilibrium category. Steps 4d and 6b are not two instalments of one problem; they are two different problems, and this note closes the first at the price of showing that the second cannot be closed the same way.
__notes__.note.state-selection.setting-what-remain:
\begin{enumerate}
\item \emph{Premise (R) is not derived, and cannot be, from the singular side.} It is the standard premise, stated in the framework's own algebra (Proposition \claimref{state-selection.euclidean-partner-curvature-selected}), but the transport principle does not entail it, and the reason is structural rather than a shortcoming of the present proof. The only finite rate the geometry supplies to the boost flow is the surface gravity, a horizon quantity: on the singular side the connection rate diverges as $\sqrt{M/2r^{3}}$ and offers no finite period to identify with $2\pi$. The locus at which (R) has purchase is the fixed locus of the boost flow, the bifurcation surface at $r = 2M$, and the Euclidean section on which the periodicity argument runs is the region $r \geq 2M$, which does not contain the singular boundary at all. There, by the chain's own Step 1, the gauge field is invertible and unimodular and division does not fail. A theory of the loci where division fails is therefore silent, by its own diagnosis, at the locus where the temperature is calibrated. In particular, strengthening the rain-finiteness of the chain's null dyad \cite[Prop.~8.23, Rem.~8.24]{ButlerT4} from a statement about the dyad to a statement about admissible states at $E$, which is the question \cite{ButlerT4} itself poses and a reasonable item for the geometry paper (T6), would discharge faithfulness and exclude the endpoints $\beta \to 0$ and $\beta \to \infty$, but would not fix the value: it is a bound, not a calibration.

The live route to a better-placed premise runs through Step 3's landing zone instead. Bisognano-Wichmann does not assume the factor $2\pi$: it derives it, from the spectrum condition together with covariance and locality \cite{BW1976, Sewell1982}. The ascent lands in $\Cl(2,4)$, whose parabolic stabiliser of the adjoined null direction contains exactly the translations such a spectrum condition needs, so the premise could be restated as positivity of the ledger's energy with respect to a generator the ascent itself installed. That would still be an import, positivity of energy being no Clifford fact, but it would be stated in the algebra the chain produces rather than in the metric geometry. Transcribing the theorem needs an action of the relevant subgroup on the ledger, a wedge and locality structure, and analyticity of the state, each of which is real work and any of which could fail; the natural home is the twistor paper, not T6.
\item \emph{Premise (L$_E$) is a statement about available generators.} See Remark \claimref{note.state-selection.status-l-e}. A no-go excluding inter-point hopping generators on $E$, in the manner of the series' other no-go results, would settle it.
\item \emph{The infinite ledger.} Theorems \claimref{singularity.descent-parity-average} to \claimref{singularity.ascended-marginals-are-diagonal} and \claimref{singularity.exact-equilibrium-over-determines-boundary-modes} are stated for the CAR algebra and their proofs do not use finiteness. Theorems \claimref{singularity.kms-uniqueness-factor}, \claimref{singularity.rate-rigidity-temperature-not-algebra-intrinsic} and \claimref{state-selection.partner-purification-are-canonical} are proved here in the matrix factor, which is the setting Step 4d works in; the general versions are the imported Facts \claimref{state-selection.imported-general-statement}, and in the genuine field-theoretic setting the horizon algebra is a type III$_1$ factor, where the Gibbs form is unavailable and the KMS condition must be used directly. Transcribing the section “One temperature, and the rigidity of the number” and the section “Fixing the rate: one premise, and its habitat inside the framework” into that setting is the natural next technical step, and \cite{KayWald1991} is the template.

__notes__.note.state-selection.true-reading-why-it:
Theorem \claimref{singularity.descended-form-state-independent} should be read as deflationary, not triumphant. For a single fermionic mode, ``thermal'' is not a discriminating property: the state space of one mode, after the descent that the chain performs anyway, is one-dimensional, and every point of it is a Gibbs state. It follows that no part of the physical content of Step 4d lies in the \emph{shape} of the reduced density matrix. All of it lies in the number $\beta_k$, in the claim that $\beta_k$ is the same for all modes, and in the claim that its value is $2\pi/\kappa$. The gap is therefore not ``which class of states'', as the status line ``up to a state'' suggests; it is ``which point of a line, and why the same point at every mode''. Everything that follows is about that line.

This is a sharpening of the gap and not a closing of it, and it is worth being explicit that the sharpening cuts against a certain kind of rhetorical comfort: one cannot claim the Fermi-Dirac \emph{form} as a prediction of the chain, because the descent manufactures that form from any input whatsoever. What the chain can claim is the temperature, and only under the premises named below.

__notes__.note.state-selection.abstract: Step 4d of T5 proves thermality at the Hawking temperature for any state that is pure, boost invariant and entangling, and declares its status plainly as ``up to a state''. This note asks what selects the state, and answers in four parts. First, the descent map of the chain is identified: it is exactly the fermion parity average, so the metric level is the parity even level, and for every state whatsoever the descended single mode marginal is diagonal, hence Gibbs at some inverse temperature. Per mode thermality is therefore not a property that can fail; the entire physical content of Step 4d is one number per mode. Second, under the univalence premise the ascended marginals are already diagonal, so the parity protection lemma of the finite ledger model is a theorem about all states and hypothesis (ii) is discharged. Third, the residual number is pinned by a rigidity theorem: for each inverse temperature there is exactly one KMS state, no flow preserving automorphism relates two of them, and the only algebraic relation available is the orientation flip. The temperature is therefore not algebra intrinsic, and no condition stated in the algebra and its flow can fix it. Fourth, one named regularity premise fixes it, and the framework supplies the premise's habitat: the curvature selected eigenplane pair of T5 Theorem 6.1 contains both the Lorentzian boost and its Euclidean partner, whose rotor has period $4\pi$ and whose conjugation action has period $2\pi$, giving $T = \kappa/2\pi$ and, as a by-product, the antiperiodicity responsible for Fermi-Dirac rather than Bose-Einstein statistics. A fifth result cuts the other way: exact KMS for the geometric flow forces a product state, hence no inter-quanta correlations at all, so the correlations carrying the information in Steps 5 and 6b are precisely the deviation from exact stationarity, and they cannot be selected by any equilibrium condition. Purity is shown to be the canonical GNS purification rather than an assumption. Step 4d's status changes from ``up to a state'' to ``proved from univalence and one regularity premise''; the residual state dependence migrates to Step 6b, where the chain already prices it.

The one-way character of the descent \cite[Fact 5.9]{ButlerT5} is then not a separate fact to be imported but the statement that a $\mathbb{Z}_2$ average cannot be undone: the even subalgebra retains no trace of the odd part it averaged away. It also explains, at a glance, why the descent is the \emph{unique} trace-compatible conditional expectation onto the commutant of $P$: it is the unique one compatible with the grading, and the grading is not a choice but the Clifford algebra's own.

The antecedent enters the table accompanying \claimref{singularity.imported-equivalence-einstein-equations} as the residue of (P$_{\mathrm{loc}}$), definitional rather than physical. the section “The metric-level sheaf, and the hopping exclusion” states the residue in structural terms without reducing it: ``the pointwise metric level'' names two algebras, the even part of the mode factor and the even-in-that-mode part of the boundary mode space, and a region can be read by assembling either contravariantly (a sheaf, a limit: survive every point's descent) or covariantly (a net, a colimit: the algebra the points' retained parts generate). The chain adopts the sheaf assembly; that adoption is the antecedent, restated, and Remark \claimref{note.singularity.what-antecedent-stated-plainly} records that the appendix quantifies both and decides neither. The sheaf exists whenever the completed mode bundle does, that is under the standing hypothesis $w_1(\shL) = 0$, and needs nothing further.
