__notes__.note.singularity.setting-metric-level-sh: The body defines the metric level pointwise (Proposition \claimref{singularity.descent-what-it-erases}, Theorem \claimref{singularity.descent-parity-average}) and reads a region of the boundary mode space through $\EN$, the composite of the pointwise descents (Proposition \claimref{singularity.p-reduced-metric-level-reading-many}). This subsection separates what that reading assumes. ``The pointwise metric level at $x$'' names two algebras, and the choice between them, made without comment in the body, is the whole of Proposition \claimref{singularity.p-reduced-metric-level-reading-many}'s antecedent.
__notes__.note.singularity.setting-point-level-tra: What Rule 1 installs instead of a value is the pair $v^2 = (v^*)^2 = 0, \qquad v v^* + v^* v = 1$ itself: the canonical anticommutation relations of one fermionic mode. Nothing commuting satisfies these relations; objects obeying them are irreducibly operators on a two-state space. By the localisation of \cite[Cor.~4.5]{ButlerT4}, in the form the Schwarzschild composite gives it at the black hole \cite[Thm.~8.12]{ButlerT4} (reproduced verbatim, hypotheses included, as Facts \claimref{sheaf.schwarzschild-degeneration-boundary-tame} and \claimref{singularity.imported-one-sided-completion-singularity} in the section “The imported localisation theorems, verbatim”), exactly one such mode is at each point of the blown-up singular locus $E \cong \R \times S^2$, and nowhere else in the physical closure: the composite's corank-one theorem \cite[Thm.~8.7]{ButlerT4} makes the count one pair per point, not one per dying coordinate direction. Quantisation is demanded locally, exactly where the classical description divides by zero, and is output rather than input: no quantisation procedure is imposed anywhere; the strength of ``demanded'' is uniform: barred on the approach by Fact \claimref{singularity.imported-no-c-number-repair} and at the boundary itself by Fact \claimref{singularity.imported-no-equivariant-value-wall}.
__notes__.note.singularity.what-antecedent-stated-: Theorems \claimref{singularity.finite-truncation-meet-big-fibres-equals} and \claimref{singularity.net-assembly-net-it-everything} quantify the two readings of ``the metric level over a region'' and do not decide between them. Both are determined by readings near the region's points; they differ in how the pointwise levels are assembled. The contravariant assembly (the sheaf, a limit: an element must survive every point's descent) gives $\operatorname{range}(\EN)$, the joint-diagonal algebra, and with it the nonzero two-level discrepancy of Steps 5 and 6b. The covariant assembly (the net, a colimit: the algebra generated by what each point's descent retains of the whole mode algebra) gives the whole mode algebra and a discrepancy of zero; it is the assembly an algebraic quantum field theory would adopt for its algebras of regions. The chain adopts the former, and that adoption is Proposition \claimref{singularity.p-reduced-metric-level-reading-many}'s antecedent: the sheaf assembly with the small fibres as stalks is the metric level if and only if the metric level over a region is the meet, so the antecedent is restated by this appendix, not reduced. What the appendix adds is the structural content of the choice: on the sheaf side the reading is a genuine sheaf whose finite truncations are $\operatorname{range}(E_F)$, on the net side it is a net whose finite truncations are the full mode algebras, and the discrepancy of Theorem \claimref{singularity.deficit-theorem-cost-descent-exactly} is precisely the cost of reading a region as a limit rather than a colimit. The choice is made in Definition \claimref{obj.singularity.two-fibres-two-assemblies}, before any sheaf theory runs, and it is a choice about which algebra ``the pointwise metric level'' names: the even part of the mode factor, or the even-in-that-mode part of the boundary mode space.
__notes__.note.singularity.setting-one-temperature: The exact equilibrium condition is stated next, and it is stated in order to be examined rather than assumed: Corollary \claimref{singularity.universality-temperature-under-g} records what it gives, Theorem \claimref{singularity.exact-equilibrium-over-determines-boundary-modes} shows that it gives too much, and the premise the chain actually adopts, (R) below, is imposed mode by mode instead.
__notes__.note.decisions.two-boost-flows:
The series calls two different one-parameter groups ``the boost flow''. Both are generated by the same element, $K = \sigma/2$ for the completed pair with $\sigma = v^{*}v - vv^{*}$ (and $\sum_j \omega_j K_j$ for the boundary modes), and they differ in the parameter.

The \emph{rotor flow} is $\operatorname{Ad}(R_\lambda)$, $R_\lambda = \exp(\lambda\sigma/2)$, a real rotor flow of the atom: it acts by $v \mapsto e^{-\lambda}v$, $v^{*} \mapsto e^{+\lambda}v^{*}$, so it rescales the modes, its adjoint eigenvalues are real, and it has no period. This is the flow of Theorem \claimref{singularity.modular-structure-completed-pair}(2) and (5), the only one-parameter flow implemented by real rotors of the atom, and of the clocks of Lemma \claimref{scrambling.clock-inventory-boundary-modes}, intrinsic flows of the real Clifford boundary-mode algebra with real adjoint eigenvalues. The scrambling law of \claimref{scrambling.spreading-law-chaos-bound-saturated} uses this flow: a quadratic generator containing the boost scales the ladder operators by $e^{\pm\kappa t}$, and that real growth, exponentiated across the window, gives $t_{*} = \kappa^{-1}\ln N$.

The \emph{phase flow} is $\operatorname{Ad}(e^{JtK})$, written with the complex unit of the atom and the boundary modes, $J = e_{2}e_{3}$ (\claimref{synthesis.transverse-bivector-is-the-complex-unit-of-the-radial-atom}), which on the modes is $a_j \mapsto e^{-J\omega_j t}a_j$: a unitary group whose adjoint eigenvalues are imaginary, multiples of $J$, periodic in the parameter for each single mode. This is the flow of Theorem \claimref{singularity.rate-rigidity-temperature-not-algebra-intrinsic}, $\alpha_t = \operatorname{Ad}(e^{JtK})$, and the boost dynamics $\tau_t(a_j) = e^{-J\omega_j t}a_j$ of Definition \claimref{obj.hawking.boundary-mode-algebra-windows-boost-dynamics}. The KMS analysis uses this flow: the descended state of Theorem \claimref{singularity.modular-descent} is KMS for it, the modular flow in its proof being $\operatorname{Ad}(\rho^{Jt})$, and the rigidity theorem, the geometric modular condition and the Hawking paper's I-state are stated for it. Proposition \claimref{singularity.euclidean-rotor-where-it-lies} identifies it as the Euclidean rotation: the boost rotor continued to imaginary rapidity, $R_{J\theta} = \exp(J\theta\sigma/2) = \exp(\theta I_{4}/2)$, whose generator $J\sigma = I_{4}$ is not in the atom's real algebra $\Cl(1,1)$ and which is realised by no real rotor of $\Cl(1,3)$ (the proposition's clause (3) writes the continuation on vectors with the central unit $I_{5} = I_{4}e$ of $\Cl(2,3)$, whose generator $I_{5}\sigma = e_{2}e_{3}e$ lies outside $\Cl(1,3)$).

The two are related by analytic continuation of the parameter, $\lambda = Jt$: $\operatorname{Ad}(e^{JtK}) = \operatorname{Ad}(R_{Jt})$. The rotor flow fixes the orbits and, through the geometric normalisation, the rate $\kappa = 1/4M$ that converts rapidity to Schwarzschild time, $\lambda = \kappa t$; the phase flow carries the period, $2\pi$ in rapidity for the conjugation action on each atom, which under premise (R) is the modular period $\beta = 2\pi/\kappa = 8\pi M$ in Schwarzschild time. The chaos-bound statement compares one with the other: the rotor flow's growth rate $\kappa$ against $2\pi T$, the phase flow's KMS temperature, which are equal. Where the boundary-mode algebra is complex (the Hawking paper) the phase flow acts within it; where it is a real Clifford algebra (the scrambling results) its generator, $J$ times a bivector, is excluded ($J$ is not in that real algebra) and only the rotor flow is intrinsic, which is the dynamical face of the second known limit in the conventions. The Hawking paper's dynamics is the phase flow, while the scrambling assumption runs the window's dynamics on the rotor flow. Which of the two is the physical time evolution of a window, in the one Schwarzschild time $t$ that both papers use, is settled by Proposition \claimref{synthesis.phase-flow-is-time-rotor-flow-kms-continuation}: taking a time evolution to be a group of $*$-automorphisms preserving the states, the phase flow is the window's time evolution and the rotor flow its KMS-strip continuation, so for the quadratic dynamics the scrambling law assumes its growth $e^{\kappa t}$ is an imaginary-time rate on the CAR windows; real-time spreading is left open there.
__notes__.note.singularity.frame-made-explicit:
Which frame carries these statements deserves one sentence each, since the $\hb$-image frame is exactly what degenerates. The bivector $\sigma_r$ is defined in the orthonormal frame of the solution, and Theorem \claimref{singularity.curvature-gauge-field-exact-shape-decoupling}'s invariance display shows the radial \emph{plane} is the same whether computed in the flat background frame or the physical one: the plane is frame-robust precisely where the argument needs it, and no choice is introduced unstated. The sign of $\sigma_r$ (equivalently, which null leg of the plane is called outgoing) is an orientation convention; every appearance of $\sigma_r$ in this paper is either quadratic in it or explicitly sign-convention-flagged, and the verification script fixes one convention and checks every identity in it. The conversion of Proposition \claimref{singularity.plane-rate}, $2\pi$ of rapidity equal to $8\pi M$ of Killing time, is a statement about the Killing flow's boost in this plane; it is the only place in the chain where geometry is converted into a number carrying units, and Theorem \claimref{singularity.modular-descent} is where that number becomes the temperature. One more frame fact, imported, settles the question whether the s-wave structure might exist only in coordinates that degenerate: the radial null dyad of this plane, read as covectors, is carried by the gauge field onto forms with \emph{constant unit} components in the infalling orthonormal frame, at every radius up to the wall \cite[Prop.~8.23, Rem.~8.24]{ButlerT4}.
The structure Steps 4d and 4e run on is exactly finite in the frame of the observer who actually crosses, even though the individual coordinate legs diverge.
__notes__.note.singularity.israels-reading-recover: The natural state satisfying (i)-(iii) is the thermofield double taken across the two ends of the completed pair, which is Israel's 1976 reading of the eternal black hole \cite{Israel1976}, now expressed in the chain's own terms: the global vacuum is entanglement between the element and its adjoined partner, and Hawking radiation is what descent sees of that entanglement. The slogan of Step 4a (the exterior radiation as the shadow of the return map) is hereby made quantitative: the shadow is the partial trace, identified mode by mode with the pinching $E$ by Proposition \claimref{singularity.pinching-against-partial-trace-scope-coincidence}(i) (the coincidence scoped precisely in Step 5, which this identification anticipates), and its output is thermal at exactly $\TH$. What the identification deliberately does not extend to is the full boundary mode space, where the two maps differ (Proposition \claimref{singularity.pinching-against-partial-trace-scope-coincidence}(ii)) and the computation is Theorem \claimref{singularity.deficit-theorem-cost-descent-exactly}'s. The word ``natural'' is made precise in the section “What selects the state”: by Theorem \claimref{singularity.purity-output-partner-commutant} the thermofield double is not one state among those satisfying the hypotheses but the canonical purification of the one-sided state, the partner being the commutant produced by the modular conjugation.
__notes__.note.singularity.three-wrinkles-recorded: First, statistics: the chain's pairs are fermionic, so the directly produced spectrum is Fermi-Dirac, correct for the fermionic sector of Hawking emission; the bosonic Planck sector is Step 4e's task and is derived, not assumed. Second, coherence with the count: at $\omega \sim \TH$ the thermal entropy per fermionic mode is of order $\ln 2$, one bit, exactly the per-mode capacity that converts Step 6a's mode count $N_{\mathrm{6a}}$ into the boundary-mode capacity $C = N_{\mathrm{6a}}\ln 2$ of Proposition \claimref{singularity.area-law-test}: the thermodynamics and the counting cohere. Third, the role of the hyperbolic atom is now complete: $\Cl(1,1)$, the unique self-complete unit of transport (Lemma \claimref{singularity.pseudo-inverse-identities-hyperbolic-atom}), is the horizon's boost plane, matched to the curvature-selected plane by Corollary \claimref{singularity.matching-steps-4b-4c-join-equation}, and its intrinsic structure, the unique rotor flow with its spectral projectors, is the modular structure of black hole thermodynamics. The atom that needs no ascent is the one that carries the temperature.
__notes__.note.singularity.what-was-obtained-what-: Typicality is absent from what the model claims, and the axiom count is correspondingly small: the envelope, the exact rising branch, the quantified falling branch, the turnover and the endpoint follow mechanically from the window identity, saturation of the falling branch remaining typicality's alone (Fact \claimref{singularity.assembled-page-curve-up-typicality}; the one-mode zero-frequency idealisation aside), the envelope and endpoint needing no typicality and no placement rule (Corollary \claimref{singularity.envelope-endpoint-why-boundary-mode-locality}), and the no-attic axiom (A) is a proposition of the model rather than an assumption, its physical force consolidated into the exhaustiveness of (L), which is the no-remnant hypothesis in its correct location: exactly the islands-side choice in the dissonance of Remark \claimref{note.singularity.island-dictionary-one-dissonance}, with its derivation programme aimed at the closure-completeness of the tower \cite[Cor.~6.2]{ButlerT3}. What remains assumed: boundary-mode locality (L$_E$) with its never-return clause (its no-hopping half a theorem within the class of supplied generators, the section “The metric-level sheaf, and the hopping exclusion”), which is what makes the falling branch mechanical (the capacity crossing is the rate-model shadow of the extremal-surface exchange); (I)'s freshness clause, the rate model's own; the capacity postulates (C1)-(C3) of Step 6a feeding (C); the standing hypothesis (U); and, for the Planck sector alone, the joint quasi-freeness (Q) of Step 4e, in its recorded tension with Steps 5 and 6b; the state of Theorem \claimref{singularity.modular-descent} is not a standing hypothesis but is fixed by (P) and (R) (Corollary \claimref{singularity.chains-state-class-stability}), and (L)'s exhaustiveness clause remains the conjectural input. Every premise in the chain is stated, named and quantified; and the two-level discrepancy itself is quantified separately, once and exactly, by Theorem \claimref{singularity.deficit-theorem-cost-descent-exactly}. The division of tasks with the sheaf paper is likewise exact: its Schwarzschild composite proves the kinematics (the carrier module, its uniqueness, the rain-finiteness of the chain's dyad, the localised ladder pair) and poses back to this paper the operator and state level \cite[\S 8.9]{ButlerT4}; that residue is discharged in the section “What selects the state”, down to the single import (R).
__notes__.note.singularity.setting-model:
Qubits stand for modes. At emission event $k$ ($k = 1, \dots, n$) a thermofield pair is created between a radiation qubit $R_k$ and a window qubit $L_k$:
\[
|\psi_k\rangle \;=\; c_k\,|0_{R_k} 0_{L_k}\rangle + s_k\,|1_{R_k} 1_{L_k}\rangle, \qquad c_k = \cos\theta_k, \quad s_k = \sin\theta_k, \quad \tan^2\theta_k = e^{-\omega_k/\TH} ,
\]
the qubit image of Theorem \claimref{singularity.modular-descent}'s state, with rational data (the script uses $(c_k, s_k) = (\tfrac45, \tfrac35), (\tfrac45, \tfrac35), (\tfrac45, \tfrac35), (\tfrac{12}{13}, \tfrac{5}{13})$ for $k = 1, \dots, 4$; every pair has $c_k > s_k$, so every $\omega_k > 0$). The window holds at most $N_{\max} = 2$ qubits; while $|L| \leq N_{\max}$ nothing else happens (Phase I). When an emission would exceed capacity, the model applies a \emph{scrambling unitary} $U$ to the window, diagonal in the number basis (a circuit of controlled-$Z$ gates, entries $\pm 1$, encoding whatever pattern the dynamics carries, including any infalling message), and then \emph{evicts} the oldest window qubit: the evicted qubit is transferred to the radiation as a late quantum (Phase II). This implements the inputs of the section “The eviction theorem: the falling branch without typicality” with a window that fills to $N_{\max} = 2$ over the first two events and then stays full until it is finally emptied: the no-attic property of Proposition \claimref{singularity.no-attic-derived-model} holds because the evicted qubit itself joins $R$, (I) because each pair arrives fresh, and (L$_E$) because the scrambling is diagonal. At the end all window qubits have been evicted and the radiation holds all $2n$ qubits.
__notes__.note.singularity.setting-machine-verific:
Every computational identity in this paper, chain, gauge sector, state selection and model alike, has been checked by computer in exact rational arithmetic, in the manner of the verifications deposited with the earlier papers of the series \cite{ButlerT1, ButlerT3, ButlerT4}. The script \texttt{verify\_T05.py}, deposited with this paper alongside the series' shared exact-arithmetic library \texttt{GA.py} \cite{ButlerVerifyT05}, performs two hundred and thirty-three checks in nine kinds of exact arithmetic: the basis-blade Clifford product over the rationals, which also carries the point-level transport of the section “The point-level transport, instantiated” in $\Cl(2,4)$ with the vector slot represented; rational-function arithmetic over $\mathbb{Q}(r)$ for the Schwarzschild fibre, in which the scalar identities of the point-level transport (the null direction, the dual norms, T04's Gram and its dual) are verified as identities rather than at samples; arithmetic for the field $\mathbb{Q}(r)[\beta]$ with $\beta^2 = 2M/r$, in which the gauge sector is verified as identities rather than at samples; fermionic Fock-space arithmetic on a finite site array for the current algebra; a multi-qubit simulator with rational amplitudes (controlled-$Z$ scrambling contributes only signs) for the finite-mode model; rational-function arithmetic in the radial variable for the appendix, so that the curvature identities are verified as identities of rational functions; formal-logarithm arithmetic, in which the von Neumann entropy of a rational spectrum is an exact vector over the primes, identities between entropies are dictionary equalities, and inequalities are decided by rigorous rational bounds on the logarithms of the primes involved; exact truncated power series over the rationals, for the Hubble-normalised rates of the section “The modular flow of the boundary modes inside, and the entangling half of (L$_E$)”; and Gaussian-rational arithmetic on the Jordan-Wigner Fock module, for the $\mathfrak{so}(2\nu)$ computations of the same section.

__notes__.note.singularity.setting-step-4d-compute: Temperature is a property of a state, and a fixed projector is state-independent: the projection alone provably cannot select a temperature, and this paper does not pretend otherwise. What the descent structure supplies, exactly, is the complete operator structure of thermality: the modular Hamiltonian ($K = N - \tfrac12$, Theorem \claimref{singularity.modular-structure-completed-pair}), its spectral projectors (the descent projectors), the localisation plane and the rate (Proposition \claimref{singularity.plane-rate}), and the uniqueness of the flow. The theorem of the section “The operator structure, and the theorem it supports” is then that any state meeting three physically standard conditions descends to the Hawking thermal matrix, exactly. the section “What selects the state” takes the next question: what selects the state. The answer is that two of the three conditions are theorems, the third is an output, and the whole residue is a single real number whose value is provably not fixable inside the algebra and is fixed by one named premise. One notational warning: from here to the end of Step 6b, $\beta$ is an inverse temperature; the Painlev\'e-Gullstrand velocity $\beta(r)$ of the section “Step 1: locate the failure” reappears only in the appendix and in the verification section.

__notes__.note.singularity.where-descent-acts-hawk: The chain must still supply the reader one sentence of locality, and here it is. The localisation theorem \cite[Thm.~4.4, Cor.~4.5]{ButlerT4}, in the form the Schwarzschild composite gives it at the black hole \cite[Thms 8.7, 8.12]{ButlerT4}, attaches the completed modes, and with them the descent, to the degenerate locus: $\EN$ is the map from the ascended boundary mode space of the singularity to its metric-level shadow, and nothing in the physical closure applies $\EN$ to the exterior radiation, whose observed single-quantum thermality is the coincidence of Proposition \claimref{singularity.pinching-against-partial-trace-scope-coincidence}(i), entanglement seen one mode at a time. Applying $\EN$ to the radiation regardless is, however, a perfectly well-defined operation, and it is precisely what it means to read the radiation at the $\Cl(1,3)$ level: keep the occupation records, erase the coherences, every mode at once. Theorem \claimref{singularity.deficit-theorem-cost-descent-exactly} quantifies that reading exactly: it costs $\rel{\rho}{\EN\rho}$, which by Corollary \claimref{singularity.deficit-carried-quanta-correlations} is exactly the inter-quanta correlation content. One conflation must be avoided here, and the model is what prevents it: the deficit measures how \emph{much} coherent content the metric-level reading destroys, and it is identical in the model's scrambled and unscrambled histories, the accumulated phases squaring away in the diagonal (Proposition \claimref{singularity.two-levels-finite-model}); the \emph{message} is written in which coherences carry it, the dressed correlators of Proposition \claimref{singularity.purity-correlation-transfer-recovery}(3), a pattern that moves phase, not entropy, and to which the deficit is provably insensitive. What descent destroys is the sector where the information lies; what the deficit measures is the size of that destruction, never its content. Hawking's information loss is thereby derived rather than merely undergone, as a \emph{quantity}: it is the deficit of the wrong level, in closed form, the content itself residing in the destroyed sector's pattern, which no function of the deficit recovers. Two more locations must be stated plainly. First, the warrant: reading $\EN$, rather than the single average over $\operatorname{Ad}(\Gamma)$, as the metric-level map is Proposition \claimref{singularity.p-reduced-metric-level-reading-many} below, the composite of the pointwise descents, its definitional antecedent quantified there; under the total-parity grading alone the average fixes every even-total state outright, the model's radiation state included, and the two-level discrepancy would be identically zero. Second, the cost's location: in the rate model the window marginal is joint-diagonal at every stage (Theorem \claimref{singularity.eviction-window-thermal-product-radiation-entropy}(1)), hence a fixed point of $\EN$, so the reading the closure does perform, of the boundary modes, costs nothing; the entire nonzero deficit of the section “The descent, applied: the two levels in numbers” is the cost of the counterfactual reading, of the radiation, at the metric level. the section “The descent, applied: the two levels in numbers” exhibits both in exact numbers.
__notes__.note.singularity.what-curvature-selected: Corollary \claimref{singularity.matching-steps-4b-4c-join-equation} uses the pair $\{\sigma_r, I\sigma_r\}$ to identify the modular bivector by equation, and that use stands: $\pm\sigma_r$ are the members with square $+1$. What the pair does \emph{not} contain is the Euclidean partner of the boost. The rotation whose period fixes the temperature lies in the complexified radial plane, and its $2\pi$ is the periodicity of the Euclidean section (Proposition \claimref{singularity.euclidean-section-period}), a fact about the smooth structure at the bifurcation sphere, not about the eigenplanes of the shape operator. The chain's contribution to the premise is therefore not a location for it inside the curvature but three more modest things: the value of the period, computed from the section (Proposition \claimref{singularity.euclidean-section-period}); the sign of the statistics, located in the algebra (Proposition \claimref{singularity.two-kms-functionals-sign}); and the proof that the premise cannot be replaced by anything internal (Theorem \claimref{singularity.rate-rigidity-temperature-not-algebra-intrinsic}, Proposition \claimref{singularity.why-calibration-cannot-be-internal}).
__notes__.note.singularity.euclidean-reading-sign-: Under continuation to imaginary time the ungraded identity is the antiperiodic boundary condition for the mode's Euclidean two-point function on a circle of circumference $\beta$, and the graded identity the periodic one: this is the Matsubara dichotomy, and it is quoted, not proved. On the smooth Euclidean section a spinor field expressed in the Killing frame, which is the polar frame of the $(\varrho, \tau)$ plane, is multiplied by the boost rotor of Proposition \claimref{singularity.euclidean-rotor-where-it-lies} continued to imaginary rapidity, the Euclidean rotation of the $(\varrho, \tau)$ plane $R_{I_{5}\theta} = \cos(\theta/2) + I_{5}\sigma\sin(\theta/2)$, with $I_{5} = I_{4}e$ the central pseudoscalar of the odd extension $\Cl(2,3)$, the unit of the continuation acting on spacetime vectors (\claimref{std-algebra.complexification-is-the-odd-extension}; not $R_{J\theta}$, which equals $e^{I_{4}\theta/2}$ in $\Cl(1,3)$), relative to a frame regular at the origin, and so reverses sign under one full turn: single-valuedness on the section, in the frame in which the modes are defined, is the antiperiodic condition, and hence the ungraded identity of (R). This is the standard spin-structure argument for the thermal, rather than parity-twisted, character of the Hartle-Hawking and Unruh states of fermions, and it is where $R_{2\pi I_{5}} = -1$ enters. The chain records it as the reason (R) is stated with the ungraded gluing; it does not derive (R) from it, and the dependence of the boundary condition on the choice of frame is exactly why the statement has to be made in the Killing frame.
__notes__.note.singularity.cost-r-dictionary:
(R) is not derived from the transport principle, and Proposition \claimref{singularity.why-calibration-cannot-be-internal} says why it cannot be, so the correct reading is that the chain has localised the last import of its state selection rather than removed it (Step 4e's (Q) is a further import, separately recorded, for the Planck sector alone). It is the same import every derivation of the Hawking temperature makes: Euclidean regularity at the bifurcation point \cite{GibbonsHawking1977, HartleHawking1976}, regularity on the future horizon \cite{Unruh1976}, nonsingularity of the quasi-free state \cite{KayWald1991}, the short-distance condition on the state near the horizon \cite{FredenhagenHaag1990}. What the chain contributes is smaller and exact: the period is computed from the section rather than chosen (Proposition \claimref{singularity.euclidean-section-period}); the premise is imposed on the marginals, mode by mode, because Theorem \claimref{singularity.exact-equilibrium-over-determines-boundary-modes} shows that its joint form destroys the correlations the chain needs; the sign of the statistics is located in the algebra (Proposition \claimref{singularity.two-kms-functionals-sign}); and the premise's irreducibility is a theorem (Theorem \claimref{singularity.rate-rigidity-temperature-not-algebra-intrinsic}). It does not supply the premise with a location inside the curvature: Proposition \claimref{singularity.euclidean-rotor-where-it-lies}(3) shows that the Euclidean rotation is not a member of the curvature-selected pair.

The dictionary against the standard alternatives, now as points of an explicitly parametrised line rather than incommensurable constructions: $\beta_k = \infty$ at every mode is the Boulware analogue \cite{Boulware1975}, unoccupied boundary modes with a pure descended state, zero deficit by Theorem \claimref{singularity.deficit-theorem-cost-descent-exactly} and no flux, excluded by (R); $\beta_k = 2\pi/\kappa$ at every mode is the Hartle-Hawking and Unruh analogue, selected by (R), the product member of that class being the (G) state; $\beta_k$ finite but varying in $k$ is excluded by (R) at the offending modes, and has no geometric modular flow by Corollary \claimref{singularity.universality-temperature-under-g}; $\beta_k = 0$ is the tracial state, excluded with the other boundary case.

One route to a better-placed premise is worth recording, because it is not the one the singular side offers. The Bisognano-Wichmann theorem does not assume the factor $2\pi$: it derives it, from the spectrum condition together with covariance and locality \cite{BW1976, Sewell1982}. The ascent of Step 3 lands in $\Cl(2,4)$, the conformal algebra, whose parabolic stabiliser of $\nInf$ contains exactly the translations such a spectrum condition needs, so the premise could be restated as positivity of the energy of the boundary modes with respect to a generator the ascent itself installed, rather than as smoothness of a Euclidean section. That would still be an import, positivity of energy being no Clifford fact, but it would be stated in the algebra the chain produces. Transcribing the theorem needs an action of the relevant subgroup on the boundary modes, a wedge and locality structure, and analyticity of the state, each of which is genuine work and any of which could fail; the item belongs with the correspondence paper T9 \cite{ButlerT9}, on the conformal spinor space of $\Cl(2,4)$, rather than here.
__notes__.note.state-selection.setting-purity-outp: Hypothesis (i) of \cite[Thm.~7.3]{ButlerT5} asks for a pure state on the doubled system. It need not be asked for.
__notes__.note.state-selection.israels-reading-upg: \cite[Rem.~7.4]{ButlerT5} records that the natural state satisfying (i) to (iii) is the thermofield double, Israel's reading of the eternal black hole \cite{Israel1976}. Theorem \claimref{state-selection.partner-purification-are-canonical} makes the word ``natural'' precise: the thermofield double is not one state among those satisfying the hypotheses, it is the canonical purification of the one-sided state, and the partner is not an extra system but the commutant. In the chain's own terms, the adjoined ladder's ``other end'' is produced by the modular conjugation of the state, so the ascent supplies the algebra and the state supplies the partner.
__notes__.note.transport.setting-one-way-door-what: The asymmetry of transport (total on the way up, lossy on the way down) is now made exact in the matrix picture of Theorem \claimref{transport.rule-1-morita-trivial}. Throughout, $P = f^*f$ and $1 - P = ff^*$ are the \emph{descent projectors}, the diagonal matrix units; they are the spectral projections $\tfrac12(1 \pm \sigma)$ of the involution $\sigma = f^*f - ff^*$, $\sigma^2 = 1$, canonically attached to the completed pair.
__notes__.note.transport.two-sided-reading: Proposition \claimref{transport.pinching-kernel} and Theorem \claimref{transport.door-one-way} split the loose statement that descent is lossy into its two true halves. On transported elements the round trip is not lossy at all: it is the identity in the natural corner identification (the grade involution in Peirce coordinates; either way invertible), and the base algebra passes through the door unchanged in both directions. What cannot descend is the completion's \emph{new} content, the ladder pair and everything it generates off the diagonal, and this impossibility is a theorem about unital homomorphisms, not an artefact of choosing a particular descent map. The statement the computations support is sharper than the original: \emph{descent is invertible on the transported elements and impossible on the elements the ascent adjoined}. Compare the point-level statement of Lemma \claimref{transport.descent-read-out-map}: there the descent is exact on the whole invertible locus and fails only on the ideal points, which are precisely the values the ascent added. Element-level and point-level descent lose different things, and each loses exactly what its ascent supplied.

descent-lift.imported-descent-modes-univ.formal: On the mode algebra the descent is the parity average $\EN(x) = \tfrac12(x + \sigma x\sigma)$, and on $\nu$ modes the composite of the mode-wise averages is the pinching onto the joint-number-diagonal algebra. Physical states are even (P), which is the univalence superselection rule: coherent superpositions of opposite fermion parity are not observable, and the observable algebra is the even subalgebra. The completion attaches one ladder pair to each point of the exceptional set and supplies, as generators of the boundary-mode dynamics, the parity sections and their products, all joint-number-diagonal; the exclusion of pairing terms is premised. On the Fock space of $\nu \geq 2$ modes the hops and pair annihilations stabilise the vacuum ray and the pair creations span the tangent of its orbit; the rotation $\ket{00} \mapsto \tfrac35\ket{00} + \tfrac45\ket{11}$ is the pairing rotation on one pair that the envelope corollary needs. The thermofield pair $c\ket{00} + s\ket{11}$ with $\tan\theta = s/c = e^{-\omega/2T}$ has both marginals equal to the Gibbs state $\operatorname{diag}(c^{2}, s^{2})$; the sample point $e^{-\omega/T} = \tfrac{9}{16}$ gives $(c, s) = (\tfrac45, \tfrac35)$. \emph{Provenance:} \cite[Thm.~5.7, Prop.~9.6, Prem.~7.8, Fact~7.9, Prem.~7.30, Thm.~C.8, Prop.~13.4, Cor.~11.6, Lem.~7.2, Thm.~7.27]{ButlerT5}; the univalence rule \cite{WWW1952}.

This collects the singularity paper's results on which the descent-lift note relies. On one mode the descent is the parity average $\EN(x) = \tfrac12(x + \sigma x\sigma)$, and on $\nu$ modes the composite of the mode-wise averages is the pinching onto the joint-number-diagonal algebra. Under the univalence premise (P) physical states are even and the observable algebra is the even subalgebra. Under the boundary-mode locality premise the completion attaches one ladder pair to each point of the exceptional set and supplies as dynamics the parity sections and their products, all joint-number-diagonal, with pairing terms excluded by premise.

On the Fock space of $\nu \geq 2$ modes the hops and pair annihilations stabilise the vacuum ray and the pair creations span the tangent of its orbit; the rotation $\ket{00} \mapsto \tfrac35\ket{00} + \tfrac45\ket{11}$ is the pairing rotation the envelope corollary needs. The thermofield pair $c\ket{00} + s\ket{11}$ with $s/c = e^{-\omega/2T}$ has both marginals equal to the Gibbs state $\operatorname{diag}(c^{2}, s^{2})$, and the sample point $e^{-\omega/T} = \tfrac{9}{16}$ gives $(c, s) = (\tfrac45, \tfrac35)$.
descent-lift.imported-descent-modes-univ.lay: This entry gathers background results from the earlier black-hole singularity work. Erasing a mode's ladder is the same as averaging over its parity; by the univalence premise (P), physical states are restricted to even fermion parity; and, under the boundary-mode locality premise, the dynamics the framework supplies never creates or destroys pairs of particles, the exclusion of such pairing terms being itself a premise. It also fixes the example used throughout: an entangled pair whose single-mode views are thermal, at amplitudes four fifths and three fifths.

descent-lift.imported-fermionic-operatio.formal: In a fermionic system with the univalence rule, the physically implementable unitaries are those commuting with the total parity, the even ones; an odd operation would carry an even state to an odd one or to a superposition of the two. The reduced state of a subsystem is the restriction of the state to the subsystem's algebra; when the complementary subsystem's states are even, this agrees with the partial trace in the tensor-product basis, and a product state $\omega_{S} \otimes \omega_{R}$ exists whenever one factor is even. \emph{Provenance:} \cite{BravyiKitaev2002}; \cite[Thm.~1]{ArakiMoriya2003}; the univalence rule \cite{WWW1952}, imported by the singularity paper as Fact \claimref{descent-lift.imported-descent-modes-univalence-supplied-class}.
descent-lift.imported-fermionic-operatio.technical:
Under the univalence rule the implementable unitaries of a fermionic system are the even ones, those commuting with the total parity; an odd operation would take an even state to an odd one or to a superposition of the two. The reduced state of a subsystem is the restriction of the state to the subsystem's algebra.

When the complementary subsystem's states are even this restriction agrees with the partial trace in the tensor-product basis, and a product state $\omega_{S}\otimes\omega_{R}$ exists whenever one factor is even.
descent-lift.imported-fermionic-operatio.lay: For fermions, the operations one can actually perform must preserve whether the particle number is even or odd. Looking at part of a fermionic system means restricting attention to the operators on that part, and when the rest has even parity this matches the usual recipe of tracing it out. Two independent subsystems can always be combined when one of them has even parity.

descent-lift.imported-pinching-one-way-d.formal: For the ascent $B = \Cl(p+1, q+1) \cong \Mat_{2}(A)$ of $A = \Cl(p,q)$ with ladder pair $f, f^{*}$ and occupation projector $P = f^{*}f$, the pinching $\EN(x) = PxP + (1-P)x(1-P)$ is an idempotent conditional expectation onto the commutant of $P$; its kernel is the ladder sector. There is no unital algebra homomorphism $B \to A$: every descent is non-multiplicative, and the pinching is the canonical linear surrogate. \emph{Provenance:} \cite[Prop.~7.5, Thm.~7.6]{ButlerT1}.

descent-lift.imported-pinching-one-way-d.lay: Going up one rung of the Clifford tower doubles the algebra by adjoining a ladder pair. Coming back down can only be done by a linear averaging map that keeps what commutes with the occupation and discards the ladder, and no structure-preserving map returns. The way down is a one-way door.

descent-lift.imported-stinespring-kraus-.formal: A completely positive trace-preserving map $\Phi$ on the operators of a finite-dimensional space $H$ has a Kraus form $\Phi(\rho) = \sum_{k} K_{k}\rho K_{k}^{\dagger}$, and a dilation: an isometry $W : H \to H \otimes H_{R}$ with $\Phi(\rho) = \Tr_{R}(W\rho W^{\dagger})$, given by $W\psi = \sum_{k} K_{k}\psi \otimes \ket{k}$ for an orthonormal family $\ket{k}$ of $H_{R}$. The minimal number of Kraus operators, and the minimal dimension of $H_{R}$, is the rank of the Choi matrix $\sum_{ij}\Phi(\ket{i}\bra{j}) \otimes \ket{i}\bra{j}$; every dilation is the minimal one followed by an isometry on the environment, so every dilation has the form $W = \sum_{k} K_{k} \otimes \ket{r_{k}}$ with the $\ket{r_{k}}$ orthonormal and the $K_{k}$ a Kraus family of $\Phi$. \emph{Provenance:} \cite{Stinespring1955, Kraus1983, Choi1975}.
descent-lift.imported-stinespring-kraus-.technical:
A completely positive trace-preserving map $\Phi$ on the operators of a finite-dimensional space $H$ has a Kraus form $\Phi(\rho) = \sum_{k}K_{k}\rho K_{k}^{\dagger}$ and a dilation, the isometry $W\psi = \sum_{k}K_{k}\psi\otimes\ket{k}$ with $\Phi(\rho) = \Tr_{R}(W\rho W^{\dagger})$.

The minimal number of Kraus operators, equal to the minimal environment dimension, is the rank of the Choi matrix $\sum_{ij}\Phi(\ket{i}\bra{j})\otimes\ket{i}\bra{j}$. Every dilation is the minimal one followed by an isometry on the environment, so every dilation has the form $W = \sum_{k}K_{k}\otimes\ket{r_{k}}$ with orthonormal $\ket{r_{k}}$ and a Kraus family $K_{k}$ of $\Phi$.
descent-lift.imported-stinespring-kraus-.lay: Any physically allowed quantum process can be viewed as a reversible interaction with an environment that is afterwards ignored. The smallest environment that does the job is fixed by a single matrix built from the process, and every other way of doing it is that smallest one with extra room added. These are the classical theorems of Stinespring, Kraus and Choi.

descent-lift.imported-thouless-states-wi.formal: For an antisymmetric matrix $A$ the state $\exp(\sum_{i<j}A_{ij}a^{\dagger}_{i}a^{\dagger}_{j})\ket{0}$ is the vacuum of the Witt decomposition obtained from the standard one by the corresponding Bogoliubov rotation; on two modes it is $\ket{00} + A_{12}\ket{11}$, and every even state vector of at most three modes is a Witt vacuum (pure, by Cartan's theorem), of this exponential form exactly when its overlap with $\ket{0}$ is nonzero ($\ket{11}$ on two modes is a Witt vacuum not of this form). \emph{Provenance:} \cite{Thouless1960}; Cartan's theorem as imported by the laboratory paper \cite[Fact~2.10]{ButlerT16}.
descent-lift.imported-thouless-states-wi.technical:
For an antisymmetric matrix $A$, the Thouless state $\exp(\sum_{i<j}A_{ij}a^{\dagger}_{i}a^{\dagger}_{j})\ket{0}$ is the vacuum of the Witt decomposition obtained from the standard one by the corresponding Bogoliubov rotation.

On two modes it is $\ket{00} + A_{12}\ket{11}$, and every even state vector of at most three modes is a Witt vacuum (pure, by Cartan's theorem), of this exponential form exactly when its overlap with $\ket{0}$ is nonzero ($\ket{11}$ on two modes is a Witt vacuum not of this form).
descent-lift.imported-thouless-states-wi.lay: Exponentiating pair creation operators and applying the result to the empty state produces a state that is the empty state of a rotated choice of modes. For two modes this is just a combination of empty and doubly occupied, and for up to three modes every state of even parity is the empty state of some choice of modes, arising from this formula whenever it overlaps the original empty state.

descent-lift.lift-costs-one-rung-per-mod.formal:
Let $\nu \geq 2$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] A lift has the form $W\ket{A} = \ket{A} \otimes r_{A}$ on the even basis states $\ket{A}$, with $r_{A} = \sum_{\kappa}(K_{\kappa})_{AA}\ket{r_{\kappa}}$ for orthonormal record states $\ket{r_{\kappa}}$, one per Kraus operator, and every $\ket{r_{\kappa}}$ even. Hence the record must contain $2^{\nu-1}$ orthonormal even states.
\item[(ii)] The even sector of $k$ rungs has dimension $2^{k-1}$. Hence a lift needs $k \geq \nu$ rungs, one per mode, and one rung never suffices.
\item[(iii)] With $\nu$ rungs a lift exists: $W = \sum_{\kappa_{\nu} = 0}\G^{\kappa} \otimes \ket{r_{\kappa}}$, the $\ket{r_{\kappa}}$ any orthonormal basis of the record's even sector; for the pair, $W = 1 \otimes \ket{00} + \G_{0} \otimes \ket{11}$, up to the normalisation $W^{\dagger}W = 2$.
\item[(iv)] The lift factorises as $W = C\,(\,\cdot \otimes \varphi)$ with $\varphi = \sum_{\kappa}\ket{r_{\kappa}}$ and $C = \sum_{\kappa}\G^{\kappa} \otimes \ket{r_{\kappa}}\bra{r_{\kappa}}$. For the pair, $C = 1 - 2P^{R}_{11}N_{0}$, a polynomial in the parity sections, joint-number-diagonal, even, an involution: an element of the supplied class. And $\varphi = \ket{00} + \ket{11}$ is the Thouless state of the record pair with amplitude $1$, a Witt vacuum of a rotated decomposition.
\item[(v)] Any even unitary $U$ realising a lift from the record vacuum has a generator that does not conserve the total number; among the quadratic generators, those of the Bogoliubov algebra $\mathfrak{so}(2(\nu + k))$, that is a generator with a nonzero pairing component. A unitary generated by number-conserving elements (hops within the record, hops between system and record, Cartan elements, joint-number-diagonal couplings) realises no lift. The pairing may sit on the record, as in (iv), or on the system and be carried to the record by hops.
\end{enumerate}

descent-lift.lift-costs-one-rung-per-mod.lay: The descent throws away part of the information in a set of two or more fermionic modes, and one can ask what it costs to keep that information in an extra record instead. Because physical states must have even fermion parity, the record needs one extra mode for every mode of the system, one more in total than a parity-blind count would give. An explicit way to do it exists: prepare the record in a paired state and apply a coupling the framework already supplies. Starting from an empty record, however, preparing that paired state needs a process that changes the particle number, which no number-conserving dynamics can provide.

descent-lift.pairing-creator-under-trans.formal:
Take two rungs in the root paper's real form, $\Cl(2,2)$ with orthogonal basis $e_{1}, e_{2}$ of square $+1$ and $e_{3}, e_{4}$ of square $-1$, ladder pairs $f_{k} = \tfrac12(e_{k} + e_{k+2})$, $f_{k}^{*} = \tfrac12(e_{k} - e_{k+2})$, number projectors $f_{k}^{*}f_{k}$ and vacuum projector $P_{00} = f_{1}f_{1}^{*}f_{2}f_{2}^{*}$ \cite[Thm.~7.1]{ButlerT1}. Let $n = f_{1}^{*}f_{2}^{*}$ be the pairing creator, $h = f_{1}^{*}f_{2}$ the hop, and $\dagger$ the Fock adjoint, the anti-automorphism that exchanges $f_{k}$ and $f_{k}^{*}$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] $n$ is a nonzero pure bivector with $n^{2} = 0$, the algebra is simple, and $n$ has annihilating idempotents in the sense of Fact \claimref{descent-lift.imported-taxonomy-type-p-rule-algorithm}, both non-central: $e = f_{2}f_{2}^{*}$ on the right, $n(1 - e) = n\,f_{2}^{*}f_{2} = 0$, and $f = f_{1}^{*}f_{1}$ on the left, $(1 - f)n = f_{1}f_{1}^{*}\,n = 0$. Under Step 2, which tests the element's grade first, $n$ is type P and Step 3 adjoins nothing. Both annihilating idempotents are of hyperbolic-pair form, $f_{2}f_{2}^{*} = wv$ for $(v, w) = (f_{2}^{*}, f_{2})$ and $f_{1}^{*}f_{1} = vw$ for $(v, w) = (f_{1}^{*}, f_{1})$, so under the refinement of Fact \claimref{descent-lift.imported-taxonomy-type-p-rule-algorithm} the obstruction is the type-N one carried by the adjoined null vectors $f_{1}^{*}, f_{2}^{*}$ themselves, for which the no-go theorem closes every equivariant element-level repair and the point-level repair is a further $(1,1)$ ascent, which acts on points and not on $n$. On either reading the algorithm returns no element from $n$.
\item[(ii)] The pair annihilation $n^{\dagger} = f_{2}f_{1}$ satisfies the four Penrose equations with $n$: it is the Moore--Penrose inverse for $\dagger$, and its idempotents $nn^{\dagger} = P_{11}$ and $n^{\dagger}n = P_{00}$ are the self-adjoint ones that Fact \claimref{descent-lift.imported-taxonomy-type-p-rule-algorithm} singles out where a definite form is available, the Fock form here. It annihilates the vacuum.
\item[(iii)] The bivector a rung carries, $f \wedge f^{*} = \tfrac12(ff^{*} - f^{*}f)$, squares to $+\tfrac14$ and commutes with the number operator: it is the Cartan element of the mode.
\item[(iv)] The reflection $e_{4} \mapsto -e_{4}$ extends to an automorphism of $\Cl(2,2)$ that fixes $f_{1}$, carries $f_{2}$ to $f_{2}^{*}$, $h$ to $n$, the hop generator $X_{h} = h - h^{\dagger}$ to the pairing generator $X_{p} = n - n^{\dagger}$, and $P_{00}$ to $P_{01}$.
\item[(v)] $X_{p}^{2} = -P_{\mathrm{even}}$ and $X_{h}^{2} = -P_{\mathrm{odd}}$ with $P_{\mathrm{even}} = P_{00} + P_{11}$ and $P_{\mathrm{odd}} = P_{01} + P_{10}$; so $\exp(\theta X) = (1 - P) + \cos\theta\,P + \sin\theta\,X$, and at $(\cos\theta, \sin\theta) = (\tfrac35, \tfrac45)$ both exponentials are rotors of $\mathrm{Spin}(2,2)$, unitary for $\dagger$; the pairing rotor carries $P_{00}$ to $\tfrac35 P_{00} + \tfrac45\,nP_{00}$, the singularity paper's witness state in the Fock ideal, and the hop rotor fixes $P_{00}$.
\item[(vi)] On the even sector $n$ and $n^{\dagger}$ satisfy the root paper's hyperbolic-pair identities, $n^{2} = (n^{\dagger})^{2} = 0$ and $nn^{\dagger} + n^{\dagger}n = P_{\mathrm{even}}$, and $X_{p} = n - n^{\dagger}$; the pairing rotation is the rotation of the plane this pair spans.
\item[(vii)] The root paper's pinching for either rung (Fact \claimref{descent-lift.imported-pinching-one-way-door}) erases $n$, $h$, $X_{p}$ and $X_{h}$ alike and fixes the parity sections $\sigma_{1}, \sigma_{2}, \sigma_{1}\sigma_{2}$.
\end{enumerate}
descent-lift.pairing-creator-under-trans.technical:
In two rungs, $\Cl(2,2)$ with ladder pairs $f_{k} = \tfrac12(e_{k} + e_{k+2})$ and $f_{k}^{*} = \tfrac12(e_{k} - e_{k+2})$, take the pairing creator $n = f_{1}^{*}f_{2}^{*}$, the hop $h = f_{1}^{*}f_{2}$ and the Fock adjoint $\dagger$. The creator is a nonzero pure bivector with $n^{2} = 0$, annihilated on each side by non-central idempotents, so Step 2 of the transport algorithm diagnoses type P and Step 3 adjoins nothing; under the hyperbolic-pair refinement it is instead the type-N obstruction of the adjoined null vectors, whose repair acts on points. On either reading the algorithm returns no element from $n$. Its Moore-Penrose inverse for $\dagger$ is the pair annihilation $n^{\dagger} = f_{2}f_{1}$, with $nn^{\dagger} = P_{11}$ and $n^{\dagger}n = P_{00}$.

The reflection $e_{4}\mapsto -e_{4}$ is an automorphism exchanging $h$ with $n$ and the hop generator $X_{h} = h - h^{\dagger}$ with the pairing generator $X_{p} = n - n^{\dagger}$. Since $X_{p}^{2} = -P_{\mathrm{even}}$ and $X_{h}^{2} = -P_{\mathrm{odd}}$, $\exp(\theta X) = (1 - P) + \cos\theta\,P + \sin\theta\,X$, and at $(\cos\theta, \sin\theta) = (\tfrac35, \tfrac45)$ both are rotors of $\Spin(2,2)$, the pairing rotor producing the singularity paper's witness state. On the even sector $n$ and $n^{\dagger}$ form a hyperbolic pair; each rung's bivector $f\wedge f^{*}$ is the mode's Cartan element; and the root paper's pinching erases $n$, $h$, $X_{p}$ and $X_{h}$ while fixing the parity sections.
descent-lift.pairing-creator-under-trans.lay: The question is whether the transport procedure, run on the operator that creates a pair of particles, produces the pair-creating rotation that the earlier work had to exclude by hand. It does not: on either reading of the procedure's classification step, it returns nothing from the pair creator. The creator's partner, the pair annihilator, is its generalised inverse, a separate fact rather than an output of the procedure. The algebra itself contains the pairing rotation and the ordinary hopping rotation on equal footing, related by a reflection, and the one-way averaging map erases both.

proofs.main: Every clause is a finite identity in the blade basis of $\Cl(2,2)$, and the script checks each (Part H). For (ii) the adjoint is reversion composed with the automorphism $e_{3}, e_{4} \mapsto -e_{3}, -e_{4}$: an anti-automorphism, being an automorphism composed with one, and an involution, since the two commute; the script confirms the anti-automorphism property on random elements and that it exchanges $f_{k}$ with $f_{k}^{*}$. For (iv) the reflection is the automorphism the universal property attaches to the isometry, checked likewise on random elements. For (v), $X^{3} = -X$ and the idempotence of $P = -X^{2}$ are checked, and $XP = X$ follows, which gives the closed form; a rotor is an even element with $R\widetilde{R} = 1$. In the blade basis $X_{p} = \tfrac12(e_{1}e_{2} + e_{3}e_{4})$ and $X_{h} = \tfrac12(e_{1}e_{2} - e_{3}e_{4})$, checked: the two generators are the two combinations of the same two rotation planes, exchanged by reversing the orientation of one of them. descent-lift.parity-alone-forces-second-.formal: For the pair, both one-rung candidates exist as maps: Stinespring's minimal dilation $\psi \otimes \ket{0} + \G_{0}\psi \otimes \ket{1}$ and the occupation copy $P_{00}\psi \otimes \ket{0} + P_{11}\psi \otimes \ket{1}$ each induce the descent on the even sector. Both are odd: the first because its record states $\ket{0} \pm \ket{1}$ mix the parities, the second because it sends the even state $\ket{11}$ to a joint state of odd parity. Neither is an operation the univalence rule allows, and there is no other obstruction.
descent-lift.parity-alone-forces-second-.technical:
For the pair, two one-rung maps do induce the descent on the even sector: Stinespring's minimal dilation $\psi\otimes\ket{0} + \G_{0}\psi\otimes\ket{1}$ and the occupation copy $P_{00}\psi\otimes\ket{0} + P_{11}\psi\otimes\ket{1}$. Both are odd: the first has record states $\ket{0}\pm\ket{1}$ of mixed parity, and the second sends the even state $\ket{11}$ to a joint state of odd parity.

Neither is an operation the univalence rule allows, and parity is the only obstruction: the even two-rung occupation copy $P_{00}\otimes(\ket{00} + \ket{11}) + P_{11}\otimes(\ket{00} - \ket{11})$ is a lift.
descent-lift.parity-alone-forces-second-.lay: For an entangled pair of modes, a single extra record mode would be enough to store what the descent discards if parity did not matter. Both natural one-mode recipes work as maps, but both break the rule that fermion parity is conserved. Restoring parity is the only thing the second record mode is needed for.

descent-lift.partial-lifts-witness-overs.formal: With the record prepared in $\ket{00} + A\ket{11}$ instead of $\varphi$, the same coupling induces the partial descent $\rho \mapsto (\rho + A^{2}\G_{0}\rho\G_{0})/(1 + A^{2})$, which leaves the fraction $(1 - A^{2})/(1 + A^{2})$ of the pair's coherence: all of it at $A = 0$, $\tfrac{7}{25}$ at $A = \tfrac34$, none at $A = 1$, and $-\tfrac{7}{25}$ at $A = \tfrac43$, the amplitude of the singularity paper's witness rotation, which overshoots the descent into a sign flip. The descent is complete if and only if the record is maximally paired.
descent-lift.partial-lifts-witness-overs.technical:
With the record prepared in $\ket{00} + A\ket{11}$ instead of the paired state $\varphi = \ket{00} + \ket{11}$, the lift's coupling $C$ induces the partial descent $\rho\mapsto(\rho + A^{2}\G_{0}\rho\G_{0})/(1 + A^{2})$, which multiplies the pair's coherence by $(1 - A^{2})/(1 + A^{2})$.

This keeps all the coherence at $A = 0$, the fraction $\tfrac{7}{25}$ at $A = \tfrac34$ and none at $A = 1$, and gives $-\tfrac{7}{25}$ at $A = \tfrac43$, the amplitude of the singularity paper's witness rotation, which overshoots the descent into a sign flip. The descent is complete if and only if the record is maximally paired.
descent-lift.partial-lifts-witness-overs.lay: How much of the pair's coherence is erased depends on how strongly the record is paired before the coupling acts. An unpaired record erases nothing, an evenly paired record erases everything, and an over-paired record, such as the one in the earlier black-hole witness, goes past erasure and flips the sign of the coherence.

descent-lift.within-supplied-dynamics-de.formal: Let the admissible generators on the system and any number of rungs be the Hermitian elements of the singularity paper's supplied class together with the Hermitian quadratic elements, in $\mathfrak{so}(2(\nu + k))$, that stabilise the joint vacuum ray: all hops and Cartan elements, on the system, on the rungs and between them. Then no unitary generated by admissible elements realises a lift of the descent from the rungs' vacuum. A lift exists in the ascent by $\nu$ rungs when a pairing rotation is added to the admissible generators, and never without a generator that fails to conserve the total number; the lift of Theorem \claimref{descent-lift.lift-costs-one-rung-per-mode}(iv) places the pairing on the rungs.
descent-lift.within-supplied-dynamics-de.technical:
Take as admissible generators, on the system and any number of rungs, the Hermitian elements of the supplied class together with the Hermitian quadratic elements of $\mathfrak{so}(2(\nu + k))$ that stabilise the joint vacuum ray, namely all hops and Cartan elements. A Hermitian quadratic element that stabilises the vacuum ray has zero pairing part, and the supplied class is joint-number-diagonal, so every admissible generator conserves total number.

Since a lift needs a generator that does not conserve number, no unitary generated by admissible elements realises a lift of the descent from the rungs' vacuum. Adding a pairing rotation gives a lift in the ascent by $\nu$ rungs, with the pairing on the rungs, and no lift exists without some generator that fails to conserve total number.
descent-lift.within-supplied-dynamics-de.lay: The framework supplies a particular set of allowed dynamics, all of which conserve particle number. Within that set, and starting from empty rungs, the information the descent discards can never be stored reversibly. Allowing one extra ingredient, a rotation that creates pairs of particles, makes it possible, so the one-way nature of the descent and the exclusion of pair creation are two views of one fact.
descent-lift.within-supplied-dynamics-de.typing_note: removed the corollary on the second rung, cited only in the closing remark that the quartic counterexample shows the quadratic restriction is needed, which is not part of the statement; added the series' descent fact, since the proof rests on the supplied class being joint-number-diagonal. Levels pass: the lay level now says the no-lift result starts from the rungs' vacuum; the admissible-class condition was already kept.

proofs.main: A Hermitian quadratic element is $X = \sum_{i,j} h_{ij}a^{\dagger}_{i}a_{j} + \sum_{i<j} (p_{ij}a^{\dagger}_{i}a^{\dagger}_{j} + \bar{p}_{ij}a_{j}a_{i}) + \lambda$, and $X\ket{0} = \sum_{i<j} p_{ij}a^{\dagger}_{i}a^{\dagger}_{j}\ket{0} + \lambda\ket{0}$ with the states $a^{\dagger}_{i}a^{\dagger}_{j}\ket{0}$ independent; if $X$ stabilises the vacuum ray then $p = 0$, and $X$ is a combination of hops and Cartan elements, which conserve the total number. (The stabiliser of the ray in the complexified algebra also contains the pair annihilations, which are not Hermitian; the script checks that the Hermitian element $a_{2}a_{3} + a^{\dagger}_{3}a^{\dagger}_{2}$ built from one carries the vacuum to $\ket{11}$.) Every admissible generator therefore conserves the total number, since the supplied class is joint-number-diagonal (\claimref{descent-lift.imported-descent-modes-univalence-supplied-class}), and Theorem \claimref{descent-lift.lift-costs-one-rung-per-mode}(v) excludes a lift; the same theorem gives the necessity clause. Adding the pairing rotation gives Theorem \claimref{descent-lift.lift-costs-one-rung-per-mode}(iii) and (iv). The restriction to quadratic elements is needed: the quartic element $I_{4}N_{0}(a^{\dagger}_{2}a^{\dagger}_{3} - a_{3}a_{2})$ is Hermitian, even, and kills the joint vacuum, but does not conserve the total number, and its rotation at $\pi/2$ is the unitary $(1 - N_{0}) + N_{0}(P^{R}_{\mathrm{odd}} + a^{\dagger}_{2}a^{\dagger}_{3} - a_{3}a_{2})$, which carries $\psi \otimes \ket{00}$ to the two-rung occupation copy of Corollary \claimref{descent-lift.parity-alone-forces-second-rung}, a lift. Here the imaginary unit is $I_{4}$, which commutes with every mode operator of the rungs and with the number operator $N_{0}$, and $I_{4}^{*} = -I_{4}$, so $I_{4}$ times the anti-Hermitian $N_{0}(a^{\dagger}_{2}a^{\dagger}_{3} - a_{3}a_{2})$ is Hermitian. It is a pairing on the rungs conditioned on the system's occupation; the script checks each of these statements, the unitary being entered in closed form. What every lift needs is the non-conservation of number; among quadratic generators that is a pairing.

hawking.gibbs-states-are-kms-conversely-.formal:
Let $\mathfrak{B} = \End(\C^m)$, with scalars $\C = \mathrm{span}\{1, I_4\}$ (the default scalar field of an abstract complex matrix algebra), let $H$ be diagonal in the basis $(\xi_a)$ with eigenvalues $\lambda_a$, all distinct or not, let $\alpha_t = \mathrm{Ad}(e^{I_4tH})$, and $\beta \in \R$. Then the Gibbs state $\omega_G(x) := \tr(e^{-\beta H}x)/\tr(e^{-\beta H})$ satisfies the KMS identity
\[
\omega_G(x\,y) \;=\; \omega_G\bigl(y\,\alpha_{I_4\beta}(x)\bigr), \qquad \alpha_{I_4\beta}(x) := e^{-\beta H}x\,e^{\beta H},
\]
for all $x, y$; and it is the \emph{unique} $\alpha$-KMS state at $\beta$ on $\mathfrak{B}$, degenerate spectrum included.
hawking.gibbs-states-are-kms-conversely-.technical:
Let $\mathfrak{B} = \End(\C^m)$, over $\mathrm{span}\{1, I_4\}$, carry the dynamics $\alpha_t = \mathrm{Ad}(e^{I_4tH})$ for a diagonal $H$ with eigenvalues $\lambda_a$, repeated or not, and fix $\beta \in \R$. The Gibbs state $\omega_G(x) = \tr(e^{-\beta H}x)/\tr(e^{-\beta H})$ satisfies the KMS identity $\omega_G(xy) = \omega_G(y\,\alpha_{I_4\beta}(x))$ with $\alpha_{I_4\beta}(x) = e^{-\beta H}x\,e^{\beta H}$, by cyclicity of the trace.

Conversely, writing a KMS state as $\omega(x) = \tr(\rho x)$ and testing the identity on matrix units forces Gibbs ratios $\rho_{aa} = e^{-\beta(\lambda_a-\lambda_b)}\rho_{bb}$ between the diagonal entries and makes every off-diagonal entry vanish, even where eigenvalues coincide. Hence $\rho = e^{-\beta H}/Z$: the Gibbs state is the unique $\alpha$-KMS state at $\beta$.
hawking.gibbs-states-are-kms-conversely-.lay: In a finite quantum system, the thermal (Gibbs) state at a given temperature satisfies a standard algebraic test of thermal equilibrium, the KMS condition. This result also proves the converse: in finite dimensions the Gibbs state is the only state that passes the test, even when some energy levels coincide.
hawking.gibbs-states-are-kms-conversely-.typing_note: No store references in the statement or proof; the proof is self-contained linear algebra, so no edges.

proofs.main:
The identity is cyclicity of the trace:
\[
\omega_G\bigl(y\,\alpha_{I_4\beta}(x)\bigr) = \tr\bigl(e^{-\beta H}y\,e^{-\beta H}x\,e^{\beta H}\bigr)/Z = \tr\bigl(e^{-\beta H}xy\bigr)/Z = \omega_G(xy),
\]
the trailing $e^{\beta H}$ moved around the trace to cancel the inner factor. Conversely write $\omega(x) = \tr(\rho x)$ and evaluate the KMS identity on matrix units $x = E_{ab}$, $y = E_{cd}$: since $\alpha_{I_4\beta}(E_{ab}) = e^{-\beta(\lambda_a - \lambda_b)}E_{ab}$ and $\tr(\rho\,E_{ab}E_{cd}) = \delta_{bc}\,\rho_{da}$, the identity reads
\[
\delta_{bc}\,\rho_{da} \;=\; e^{-\beta(\lambda_a - \lambda_b)}\,\delta_{da}\,\rho_{bc}
\qquad \text{for all } a, b, c, d.
\]
Taking $c = b$ and $d = a$ gives $\rho_{aa} = e^{-\beta(\lambda_a - \lambda_b)}\rho_{bb}$: Gibbs ratios between all diagonal entries. Taking $c = b$ and $d \neq a$ gives $\rho_{da} = 0$ (the right side carries $\delta_{da} = 0$), for every pair $d \neq a$, degenerate eigenvalues included: $\rho$ is diagonal. So $\rho = e^{-\beta H}/Z$, and the KMS state is unique. The verification script performs the solve symbolically for the mode algebra $\Mat_2$ with $H = \omega N$ and confirms both clauses as identities of rational functions in the Boltzmann factor.

hawking.imported-ideal-fermi-gas-uniquen.formal: For the CAR algebra over a one-particle space with self-adjoint $h$ and the induced quasi-free dynamics, the $\beta$-KMS state is unique and equals the quasi-free state with symbol $(1 + e^{\beta h})^{-1}$. \emph{Provenance:} \cite[Ex.~5.3.2 and \S 5.3]{BratteliRobinson1997}; the quasi-free calculus is \cite{Araki1971}.
hawking.imported-ideal-fermi-gas-uniquen.technical: For the CAR algebra over a one-particle space with self-adjoint one-particle Hamiltonian $h$ and the induced quasi-free dynamics, the $\beta$-KMS state is unique and is the quasi-free state with symbol $(1 + e^{\beta h})^{-1}$, the Fermi-Dirac distribution. This is the ideal-Fermi-gas result of Bratteli and Robinson, with Araki's quasi-free calculus.
hawking.imported-ideal-fermi-gas-uniquen.lay: For a gas of non-interacting fermions with a given energy rule, there is exactly one equilibrium state at each temperature, and its occupation numbers follow the Fermi-Dirac law. This is a textbook result of quantum statistical mechanics.

hawking.imported-kms-passes-inductive-li.formal: Let a C*-algebra be the closure of an increasing union of subalgebras, each globally invariant under a one-parameter dynamics, and let a state be KMS at $\beta$ on each subalgebra for the restricted dynamics. Then the state is KMS at $\beta$ on the whole algebra: the analytic-element requirement is checked on the dense union and passes to the closure. \emph{Provenance:} \cite[Prop.~5.3.25]{BratteliRobinson1997}.
hawking.imported-kms-passes-inductive-li.technical: Suppose a C*-algebra is the closure of an increasing union of subalgebras, each globally invariant under a one-parameter dynamics, and a state is KMS at inverse temperature $\beta$ on each subalgebra for the restricted dynamics. Then the state is KMS at $\beta$ on the whole algebra: the analytic-element requirement is checked on the dense union and passes to the closure. This is a standard result of operator-algebraic statistical mechanics, imported from the literature.
hawking.imported-kms-passes-inductive-li.lay: Thermal equilibrium, in its precise algebraic form, can be checked piece by piece. If a large system is the limit of an increasing chain of smaller subsystems, each preserved by the time evolution, and a state is in equilibrium on every one of them, then it is in equilibrium on the whole system. This is a known result taken from the literature.

imported_from.citation: O. Bratteli and D. W. Robinson, Operator Algebras and Quantum Statistical Mechanics 2, 2nd ed., Springer, Berlin (1997).

hawking.imported-modular-descent-premise.formal: Let the ascended algebra of a horizon pair carry a state that is pure, invariant under the boost flow of Proposition \claimref{hawking.modular-structure-completed-pair}, and entangling across the pair (cyclic and separating for the one-sided subalgebra). Then the descended state is KMS for the phase flow $\operatorname{Ad}(e^{Jt\sigma/2})$ of the same generator, $J = e_{2}e_{3}$ the complex unit of the atom (\claimref{synthesis.transverse-bivector-is-the-complex-unit-of-the-radial-atom}), at \emph{some} inverse temperature $\beta \in \R$ of rapidity, and the hypotheses leave $\beta$ free, its sign included; the Gibbs \emph{form} of the descended state is state-independent. Positivity and the value are supplied by T5's named premises: under (P) univalence and (R) the KMS condition at the geometric period (one modular period equal to one rapidity period $2\pi$, i.e.\ Schwarzschild time $2\pi/\kappa$, the Euclidean period $8\pi M$), the descended state is Fermi-Dirac at $\beta = 2\pi$ of rapidity, which is the physical temperature $\TH = \kappa/2\pi = 1/8\pi M$; the boost plane is the one the shape operator scales by $-2$, and $\kappa = 1/4M$ is proved from the gauge field. Per mode of Schwarzschild frequency $\omega$ the reduced density matrix is the Fermi-Dirac matrix $\mathrm{diag}(1, e^{-\omega/\TH})/Z$. \emph{Provenance:} T5 \cite[Thms.~7.3 and 7.6, Prems.~7.8 and 7.19, Prop.~7.18, Thm.~7.20, Cor.~6.4]{ButlerT5}, with $\kappa = 1/4M$ from the gauge field in \cite[App.~A]{ButlerT5}; premise (R) is proved irreducible there, the temperature being no algebra-intrinsic quantity \cite[Thm.~7.16]{ButlerT5}. The wedge-modular mechanism is Bisognano-Wichmann-Sewell \cite{BisognanoWichmann1976, Sewell1982}, and the thermofield reading is Israel's \cite{Israel1976}.
hawking.imported-modular-descent-premise.technical:
Suppose the ascended algebra of a horizon pair carries a state that is pure, invariant under the boost flow of the completed pair, and entangling across the pair (cyclic and separating for the one-sided subalgebra). Then the descended state is KMS for the phase flow $\operatorname{Ad}(e^{Jt\sigma/2})$ of the same generator, $J = e_2e_3$ the atom's complex unit, at some inverse temperature $\beta\in\R$ of rapidity, with $\beta$ left free, sign included; the Gibbs form of the descended state is state independent.

Under the premises (P) univalence and (R) the KMS condition at the geometric period, the descended state is Fermi-Dirac at $\beta = 2\pi$ of rapidity, the physical temperature $\TH = \kappa/2\pi = 1/8\pi M$, with $\kappa = 1/4M$ proved from the gauge field; per mode of Schwarzschild frequency $\omega$ the reduced density matrix is $\operatorname{diag}(1, e^{-\omega/\TH})/Z$. Premise (R) is irreducible, the temperature being no algebra-intrinsic quantity.
hawking.imported-modular-descent-premise.lay: When a pure state that is entangled across a black-hole horizon and unchanged by the horizon's boost is viewed from one side only, it looks thermal, but the algebra alone does not fix the temperature, not even its sign. Two named premises from the singularity work, one about fermion parity and one about regularity of the geometry, fix it at the Hawking temperature. Each mode then has the Fermi-Dirac occupation expected of fermions at that temperature.

proofs.main:
Let the ascended algebra of a horizon pair carry a state that is pure, invariant under the boost flow of Proposition \claimref{hawking.modular-structure-completed-pair}, and entangling across the pair (cyclic and separating for the one-sided subalgebra). Then the descended state is KMS for the phase flow $\operatorname{Ad}(e^{Jt\sigma/2})$ of the same generator, $J = e_{2}e_{3}$ the complex unit of the atom (\claimref{synthesis.transverse-bivector-is-the-complex-unit-of-the-radial-atom}), at \emph{some} inverse temperature $\beta \in \R$ of rapidity, and the hypotheses leave $\beta$ free, its sign included; the Gibbs \emph{form} of the descended state is state-independent. Positivity and the value are supplied by T5's named premises: under (P, \claimref{singularity.p-univalence}) univalence and (R, \claimref{singularity.r-regularity-fixed-locus}) the KMS condition at the geometric period (one modular period equal to one rapidity period $2\pi$, i.e.\ Schwarzschild time $2\pi/\kappa$, the Euclidean period $8\pi M$), the descended state is Fermi-Dirac at $\beta = 2\pi$ of rapidity, which is the physical temperature $\TH = \kappa/2\pi = 1/8\pi M$; the boost plane is the one the shape operator scales by $-2$, and $\kappa = 1/4M$ is proved from the gauge field. Per mode of Schwarzschild frequency $\omega$ the reduced density matrix is the Fermi-Dirac matrix $\mathrm{diag}(1, e^{-\omega/\TH})/Z$. \emph{Provenance:} T5 \cite[Thms.~7.3 and 7.6, Prems.~7.8 and 7.19, Prop.~7.18, Thm.~7.20, Cor.~6.4]{ButlerT5} (\claimref{singularity.modular-descent}, \claimref{singularity.euclidean-section-period}, \claimref{singularity.rate-discharge-hypothesis-iii}, \claimref{singularity.matching-steps-4b-4c-join-equation}, \claimref{singularity.descended-form-state-independent}), with $\kappa = 1/4M$ from the gauge field in \cite[App.~A]{ButlerT5}; premise (R) is proved irreducible there, the temperature being no algebra-intrinsic quantity \cite[Thm.~7.16]{ButlerT5} (\claimref{singularity.rate-rigidity-temperature-not-algebra-intrinsic}). The wedge-modular mechanism is Bisognano-Wichmann-Sewell \cite{BisognanoWichmann1976, Sewell1982}, and the thermofield reading is Israel's \cite{Israel1976}.

This restates \claimref{hawking.imported-modular-descent-premises-geometric-normalisation-external}, \claimref{singularity.computed}.

hawking.imported-modular-descent-premise.technical: The external ingredients are the Bisognano-Wichmann theorem, that the modular flow of the vacuum on a wedge algebra is the boost; Sewell's extension of this to black-hole spacetimes, which yields states thermal with respect to the horizon's Killing flow; and Israel's thermofield-double reading of the eternal black hole. The series' statement on modular descent and its geometric normalisation draws on them for the mechanism.
hawking.imported-modular-descent-premise.lay: Three classic results stand behind this entry: in flat space the vacuum seen from one wedge looks thermal with respect to boosts, the same mechanism applies near a black-hole horizon, and the eternal black hole can be read as two entangled copies, each of which looks thermal on its own.

hawking.imported-quasi-free-kms-reduces-.formal: For the CAR algebra over a one-particle space with the quasi-free dynamics of a self-adjoint one-particle Hamiltonian, a gauge-invariant quasi-free state is KMS at $\beta$ if and only if its two-point function satisfies the two-point KMS identity: through the Wick-determinant structure, the analytic-continuation requirement for products of generators reduces to the two-point level. \emph{Provenance:} Araki \cite{Araki1971}; \cite[\S 5.3]{BratteliRobinson1997}.
hawking.imported-quasi-free-kms-reduces-.technical: For the CAR algebra over a one-particle space with the quasi-free dynamics of a self-adjoint one-particle Hamiltonian, a gauge-invariant quasi-free state is KMS at $\beta$ if and only if its two-point function satisfies the two-point KMS identity. Through the Wick-determinant structure of quasi-free states, the analytic-continuation requirement on products of generators reduces to the two-point level.
hawking.imported-quasi-free-kms-reduces-.lay: For free fermions in the simplest class of states, checking thermal equilibrium needs only the two-particle correlations, because all higher correlations are built from them. This is a standard result of quantum statistical mechanics.

hawking.kms-restricts-invariant-subalgeb.formal: If $\omega$ is $\alpha$-KMS at $\beta$ on $\mathfrak{B}$ and $\mathfrak{C} \subseteq \mathfrak{B}$ is a unital subalgebra with $\alpha_t(\mathfrak{C}) = \mathfrak{C}$, then $\omega|_{\mathfrak{C}}$ is KMS at $\beta$ for $\alpha|_{\mathfrak{C}}$.
hawking.kms-restricts-invariant-subalgeb.technical:
Let $\omega$ be $\alpha$-KMS at $\beta$ on $\mathfrak{B}$ and let $\mathfrak{C}\subseteq\mathfrak{B}$ be a unital subalgebra with $\alpha_t(\mathfrak{C}) = \mathfrak{C}$. Then the restriction $\omega|_{\mathfrak{C}}$ is KMS at $\beta$ for $\alpha|_{\mathfrak{C}}$.

For $x, y\in\mathfrak{C}$ the correlation function $t\mapsto\omega(y\,\alpha_t(x))$ is the same whether computed in $\mathfrak{C}$ or in $\mathfrak{B}$, so its continuation to the strip and the KMS boundary identity carry over unchanged.
hawking.kms-restricts-invariant-subalgeb.lay: If a system is in thermal equilibrium and one looks only at a set of observables that the time evolution keeps within itself, those observables are also in equilibrium at the same temperature.
hawking.kms-restricts-invariant-subalgeb.typing_note: proved outright with no premises; the paper calls KMS theory standard only in its prior-art paragraph and no imported restriction lemma is in the store, so no standard route.

proofs.main: For $x, y \in \mathfrak{C}$ the correlation function $t \mapsto \omega(y\,\alpha_t(x))$ is computed entirely from elements of $\mathfrak{C}$ (invariance keeps $\alpha_t(x) \in \mathfrak{C}$), and is the same function of $t$ whether $x, y$ are regarded in $\mathfrak{C}$ or in $\mathfrak{B}$. Its continuation to the closed strip is unique (a function analytic on the strip and continuous on its closure is determined by its boundary restriction to the real line, by uniqueness of analytic continuation), so the strip function and the KMS boundary identity transfer verbatim from $\mathfrak{B}$ to $\mathfrak{C}$.

hawking.modular-structure-completed-pair.technical:
For a completed pair $(v, v^{*})$ of null vectors with $vv^{*} + v^{*}v = 1$, set $\sigma = v^{*}v - vv^{*}$. Then $\sigma^{2} = 1$, and in the hyperbolic atom $\Cl(1,1)$ with $v = \tfrac12(e_{0} + e_{1})$ and $v^{*} = \tfrac12(e_{0} - e_{1})$ it is the unit boost bivector $e_{0}e_{1}$. The rotor flow $R_{\lambda} = \exp(\lambda\sigma/2)$ scales $v$ by $e^{-\lambda}$ and $v^{*}$ by $e^{+\lambda}$, the spectral projectors $\tfrac12(1\pm\sigma)$ are the occupation projectors $v^{*}v$ and $vv^{*}$, and in the Fock representation $\tfrac12\sigma = N - \tfrac12$.

Since the bivector space of $\Cl(1,1)$ is one-dimensional, the boost flow is the unique one-parameter rotor flow of the atom up to reparametrisation of the flow parameter and orientation: the algebra fixes the orbits of a rotor-implemented modular flow, but not its speed.
hawking.modular-structure-completed-pair.lay: A single fermionic mode, built from a pair of null directions, carries a natural boost: a flow that stretches one direction and shrinks the other. The two halves of this boost are exactly the empty and occupied states of the mode, and its generator is the particle number shifted by one half. The algebra fixes which flow this is but not how fast it runs, which is the temperature question left open.
hawking.modular-structure-completed-pair.typing_note: proved outright with no premises (the paper says the single-mode modular structure is elementary and proved here); the unresolved reference to the frontier remark is context only.

proofs.main: (1) $\sigma^2 = v^*vv^*v + vv^*vv^* - v^*v\,vv^* - vv^*\,v^*v = v^*v + vv^* - 0 - 0 = 1$, using $vv^*v = v$, $v^*vv^* = v^*$ and the vanishing squares. In $\Cl(1,1)$, by \claimref{std-algebra.vector-squares}: $v^*v = \tfrac14(e_0 - e_1)(e_0 + e_1) = \tfrac14(e_0^2 - e_1^2 + e_0e_1 - e_1e_0) = \tfrac14(1 + 1 + 2e_0e_1) = \tfrac12(1 + e_0e_1)$, so $\sigma = v^*v - vv^* = e_0e_1$ in this orientation; relabelling the pair reverses it. (2) From $vv^*v = v$ and the vanishing squares, $\sigma v = (v^*v - vv^*)v = -vv^*v = -v$ and $v\sigma = v(v^*v - vv^*) = vv^*v = +v$. The first relation gives $e^{\lambda\sigma/2}\,v = v\,e^{-\lambda\sigma/2}$ term by term in the exponential series, so $R_\lambda\, v\, R_\lambda^{-1} = v\,e^{-\lambda\sigma}$. Since $\sigma^2 = 1$, $e^{-\lambda\sigma} = \cosh\lambda - \sigma\sinh\lambda$ (\claimref{std-algebra.bivector-exponential}), and the second relation collapses it on the left factor: $v\,e^{-\lambda\sigma} = v(\cosh\lambda - \sinh\lambda) = e^{-\lambda}v$. The $v^*$ computation is the mirror image, with both signs reversed. (3) $\tfrac12(1 + \sigma) = \tfrac12(1 + v^*v - vv^*) = \tfrac12(v^*v + vv^* + v^*v - vv^*) = v^*v$, and likewise for the complement. (4) In the two-dimensional Fock module ($v^* = $ creation, $v = $ annihilation, $N = v^*v$): $\tfrac12\sigma = \tfrac12(v^*v - vv^*) = \tfrac12(N - (1 - N)) = N - \tfrac12$. (5) The bivector space of $\Cl(1,1)$ is the line $\R\,e_0e_1$, so every one-parameter rotor group is of the form $\lambda \mapsto \exp(c\lambda\sigma/2)$ for some real $c$: the same orbits at a rescaled parameter, which is the reparametrisation the statement reserves. The verification script checks every clause in exact arithmetic, including the finite conjugation of clause (2) at a rational rapidity.
