proofs.main: (1) and (2) are \cite[Lem.~7.1]{ButlerT5} (\claimref{singularity.modular-theory-matrix-factor-proved-outright}) read in the direction of construction rather than of analysis: that lemma computes $\Delta = \rho\otimes\bar\rho^{-1}$ and $J|ij\rangle = |ji\rangle$ for exactly this $\Omega$, and establishes that $\Omega$ is cyclic and separating; the identification $\pi(\Aa)' = J\pi(\Aa)J$ is Tomita's theorem, which in this finite-dimensional case is the content of that lemma's polar decomposition. (3) If $|\Psi\rangle \in \C^2\otimes\mathcal{K}$ purifies $\rho$ then its Schmidt coefficients are the $\lambda_i$, so $|\Psi\rangle = (1\otimes W)\Omega$ for an isometry $W$ carrying one Schmidt basis to the other; two purifications on the same purifying space differ by a unitary there. (4) Substituting $\rho = \operatorname{diag}(1, e^{-\omega_k/T})/Z$ gives $\lambda_1/\lambda_0 = e^{-\omega_k/2T} = \tan\theta$, which is the state of \cite[Lem.~7.2]{ButlerT5}.

synthesis.state-selection-r-and-le-again.technical:
The note folded into T05 states two premises under T05's names. On the boundary-mode algebra the note's (R), regularity of the state's two-point functions continued in rapidity, can be read three ways on a single mode: regularity alone constrains nothing, strict periodicity in imaginary time is satisfied by no state, and the reading T05 uses, with the two operator orderings glued across the cut, fixes the mode's occupancy at its thermal value for the geometric period, and with univalence (P) makes the mode exactly thermal (KMS). Imposed on every two-point function of the window, the glued reading also forces all correlations between different modes' ladders to vanish. It therefore sits strictly between T05's (R), which constrains single modes only, and T05's (R) together with the quasi-free premise (Q); two small even states show both gaps. The single-mode conclusions of the note's rate theorem need only T05's (R) with (P).

The two locality premises (L$_E$) describe the same generators: products of the boost bivectors at each point, which commute with every occupation number, include the cross-point products used for the controlled-$Z$ scrambling, and exclude hopping and pairing between points. The note's wording, taken literally, would also exclude the cross-point products its own proposition uses, so T05's wording is the consistent one.
synthesis.state-selection-r-and-le-again.lay: Two assumptions of the series appear twice, once in the main paper on black-hole states and once in a shorter note later folded into it, under the same names. This result compares them exactly. The two locality assumptions turn out to say the same thing. The two regularity assumptions do not: read in the only way that makes it both meaningful and satisfiable, the note's version asks for everything the main paper's version asks, plus the absence of correlations between different modes, while still asking less than the main paper's version combined with its separate assumption that the state is the simplest (quasi-free) one. Small explicit examples show both differences. What the note actually uses its version for needs only the main paper's, together with the univalence assumption both papers make.

proofs.main:
\emph{(i).} Under the flow, $\alpha_{t}(a^{*}) = e^{J\omega t}a^{*}$ and $\alpha_{t}(a) = e^{-J\omega t}a$, since $[K, a] = -a$ (Proposition \claimref{hawking.modular-structure-completed-pair}(2), (4)). With occupancy $n = \omega(a^{*}a)$ and $\omega(aa^{*}) = 1 - n$, the ladder correlators are $F_{a,a^{*}}(t) = e^{J\omega t}(1 - n)$ and $F_{a^{*},a}(t) = e^{-J\omega t}n$, and $F_{a,a} = F_{a^{*},a^{*}} = 0$ since $a^{2} = 0$. Each is entire, so regularity alone imposes nothing. Strict periodicity gives $(z^{-1} - 1)(1 - n) = 0$ and $(z - 1)n = 0$; for $z \ne 1$ these force $n = 1$ and $n = 0$, so no state satisfies them. The glued reading gives $z^{-1}(1 - n) = n$ (and the same equation from the other ordering), whose one root is $n = 1/(z + 1)$, the occupancy T05's (R) asserts on the mode. The ladder correlators involve only $\omega(aa^{*})$ and $\omega(a^{*}a)$, so they leave $\omega(a)$ free; with $\omega(a) = 0$, which (P) (\claimref{singularity.p-univalence}) supplies, the marginal is $\operatorname{diag}(1 - n, n) = e^{-pK}/\operatorname{tr}e^{-pK}$, the unique KMS state at $\beta = p$ (Theorem \claimref{singularity.kms-uniqueness-factor}). At $z = 1$ both periodicity equations hold for every $n$, and the glued one reads $1 - n = n$. The check runs these equations for $z = 3, \tfrac15, \tfrac72$ with exact density matrices, and at $z = 1$.

\emph{(ii).} For $i \ne j$ the canonical anticommutation relations (Proposition \claimref{scrambling.boundary-mode-space-matrix}) give $b_{j}a_{i} = -a_{i}b_{j}$ for $b_{j} \in \{a_{j}, a_{j}^{*}\}$. The glued condition for $(a_{i}, a_{j}^{*})$ reads $z_{j}^{-1}\omega(a_{i}a_{j}^{*}) = \omega(a_{j}^{*}a_{i}) = -\omega(a_{i}a_{j}^{*})$, so $(1 + z_{j}^{-1})\,\omega(a_{i}a_{j}^{*}) = 0$ and $\omega(a_{i}a_{j}^{*}) = 0$ since $z_{j} > 0$; likewise for $(a_{i}, a_{j})$ with $z_{j}$ in place of $z_{j}^{-1}$, and for the adjoint pairs. Conversely, if every inter-mode two-point function vanishes, the mixed conditions hold trivially, and the single-mode ones are (i).

\emph{(iii).} The two-point clause of (Q) is $\omega(a_{k}^{*}a_{l}) = \delta_{kl}n_{k}$ with gauge invariance, so every inter-mode two-point function vanishes and, with T05's (R), (ii) gives (R$_{\mathrm{reg}}$); (R$_{\mathrm{reg}}$) implies T05's (R) by restriction to single modes. For the counter-models take $z_{1} = 3$, $z_{2} = 5$, $n_{k} = 1/(z_{k} + 1)$, in the Jordan-Wigner basis. Model A is the product state with the coherence $c = \tfrac{1}{50}$ added between $\ket{01}$ and $\ket{10}$: it has trace one, is positive (its $2\times2$ block has determinant $n_{1}(1 - n_{2})\,n_{2}(1 - n_{1}) - c^{2} > 0$), commutes with the total parity, has the Gibbs marginals, and $\omega(a_{1}a_{2}^{*}) = -c$, so the mixed glued condition fails. Model B shifts $p_{11}$ to $n_{1}n_{2} + d$, $d = \tfrac{1}{100}$, with the other diagonal entries fixed by the marginals and no coherence: it is a diagonal, hence even, state with the Gibbs marginals and vanishing inter-mode two-point functions, so (R$_{\mathrm{reg}}$) holds, while $\omega(N_{1}N_{2}) - n_{1}n_{2} = d$, against Wick's factorisation $\omega(N_{1}N_{2}) = n_{1}n_{2}$ for a gauge-invariant quasi-free state with diagonal two-point function. The check confirms each statement exactly.

\emph{(iv).} By (i), (R$_{\mathrm{reg}}$) with (P) makes each marginal the Gibbs state at $\beta = p = 2\pi/\kappa$, with $n = 1/(e^{\omega p} + 1) \in (0, 1)$ for every real $\omega$, so every marginal is faithful; this is the single-mode conclusion of Theorem \claimref{singularity.rate-discharge-hypothesis-iii}, there drawn from T05's (R), and no modular group, hence no geometric modular condition, enters. The single-mode conclusions of the note's Theorem \claimref{state-selection.rate-discharge-hypothesis-iii} are these.

\emph{(v).} Both premises take the generators to be the boost bivector field and its products, so the generated algebra is the one of $\sigma_{1}, \ldots, \sigma_{n}$. The check builds three modes in $\Cl(3,3)$, one hyperbolic atom per mode: the $8$ products of subsets of $\{\sigma_{1}, \sigma_{2}, \sigma_{3}\}$ are linearly independent, each commutes with every $N_{k}$ (so every generator is diagonal in the joint number basis, as Proposition \claimref{singularity.number-diagonal-dynamics-models-scrambling-derived} states), $\sigma_{1}\sigma_{2}$ lies in their span, and the hopping $a_{1}^{*}a_{2}$ and pairing $a_{1}^{*}a_{2}^{*}$ each raise the rank to $9$ and fail to commute with $N_{1}$. T05's premise states the exclusion as no off-diagonal generator, in particular no hopping, with cross-point products allowed; the note's states it as no generator coupling two ladders. Since the note's own Proposition uses the cross-point controlled-$Z$, a product of $\sigma_{j}\sigma_{k}$-type terms, the literal reading that excludes all two-point generators contradicts its first clause, and the reading consistent with it excludes exactly the off-diagonal generators, which is T05's.

synthesis.transverse-bivector-is-the-com.formal:
Work in $\Cl(1,3)$, $e_{0}^{2} = 1$, $e_{k}^{2} = -1$ ($k = 1, 2, 3$), $I_{4} = e_{0}e_{1}e_{2}e_{3}$, with the completed pair of Theorem \claimref{singularity.modular-structure-completed-pair} realised in the hyperbolic atom of the radial plane (Lemma \claimref{singularity.pseudo-inverse-identities-hyperbolic-atom}): $v = \tfrac12(e_{0} + e_{1})$, $v^{*} = \tfrac12(e_{0} - e_{1})$, $\sigma = v^{*}v - vv^{*} = e_{0}e_{1}$, $K = \sigma/2$, $P_{+} = v^{*}v = \tfrac12(1 + \sigma)$, $P_{-} = vv^{*} = \tfrac12(1 - \sigma)$. Let $J = e_{2}e_{3}$, the unit bivector of the transverse plane, and let $x \mapsto x^{*} = e_{0}\rev{x}e_{0}$ be the frame $*$-structure of Theorem \claimref{tower.structure-tower-c-norms} ($e_{0}^{*} = e_{0}$, $e_{k}^{*} = -e_{k}$, an antiautomorphism).
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(The unit.)} $J^{2} = -1$; $J$ commutes with $e_{0}$ and $e_{1}$, hence with $v$, $v^{*}$, $\sigma$ and everything they generate; $J\sigma = \sigma J = +I_{4}$, so $J = I_{4}\sigma$; and $J^{*} = -J$. $J$ is a choice among the units that commute with the atom, fixed as follows: the centraliser of $e_{0}, e_{1}$ in $\Cl(1,3)$ is $\mathrm{span}\{1, J, e_{0}e_{1}e_{2}, e_{0}e_{1}e_{3}\}$, a quaternion algebra; $\pm J$ are its only elements of square $-1$ in the even subalgebra (equivalently, the only ones fixed by the rotations of the transverse plane), and the sign of $J$ is fixed by $J\sigma = +I_{4}$. Odd units such as $\sigma e_{2} = e_{0}e_{1}e_{2}$, which anticommutes with $J$, also square to $-1$, commute with the atom and are sent to their negatives by $*$; they are not identified with $J$.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(The atom over $J$.)} The real algebra $\Aa = \Cl(1,1) \oplus \Cl(1,1)J$ generated by $e_{0}$, $e_{1}$ and $J$ has real dimension $8$ and centre $\mathrm{span}\{1, J\}$, a field isomorphic to $\C$; over that field it is spanned by $1$, $v$, $v^{*}$, $v^{*}v$, so it is the CAR algebra of one mode, a full $2 \times 2$ matrix algebra over $\mathrm{span}\{1, J\}$. The frame $*$ maps $\Aa$ to itself, sends $v$ to $v^{*}$, fixes $\sigma$ and $K$, and is conjugate-linear over the field ($J^{*} = -J$).
\item[(iii)] \emph{(The left unit $I_{4}$ is not a scalar of the atom.)} $I_{4} = J\sigma$ lies in $\Aa$ but is not central: it anticommutes with $e_{0}$, $e_{1}$, $v$, $v^{*}$, and for vectors $a, b$ of the radial plane $(I_{4}a)(I_{4}b) = +ab$, whereas $(Ja)(Jb) = -ab$. On the spectral projectors $I_{4}P_{\pm} = \pm JP_{\pm}$: the two units agree on the image of $v^{*}v$ and are opposite on that of $vv^{*}$, and they are not identified.
\item[(iv)] \emph{(The phase flow.)} $JK = I_{4}/2$ and $(2JK)^{2} = -1$, so $e^{JtK} = \cos\tfrac{t}{2} + 2JK\sin\tfrac{t}{2}$, and for real $t$
\[
\tau_{t}(x) := e^{JtK}\,x\,e^{-JtK}, \qquad \tau_{t}(v) = e^{-Jt}v, \qquad \tau_{t}(v^{*}) = e^{+Jt}v^{*},
\]
infinitesimally $JKv - vJK = -Jv$ and $JKv^{*} - v^{*}JK = +Jv^{*}$. $(e^{JtK})^{*} = e^{-JtK}$, so $\tau$ is a one-parameter group of $*$-automorphisms of $\Aa$. The phase flow of the source on the atom (T05 Thm 7.16, T07 Def 2.7) and the flow of Theorem \claimref{singularity.kms-uniqueness-factor}, written there with a scalar unit, are $\tau_{t}$ with that unit written as $J$; the sign agrees, $v \mapsto e^{-Jt}v$. For $\sin t \neq 0$, $\tau_{t}(v) = v\cos t - Jv\sin t$ is not a vector ($Jv$ is a trivector): $\tau_{t}$ acts on values, and maps no nonzero vector to a vector.
\item[(v)] \emph{(The rotor flow is its continuation.)} For $z$ in the field $\mathrm{span}\{1, J\}$, $\tau_{z} := \operatorname{Ad}(e^{JzK})$ is an automorphism of $\Aa$ with $\tau_{z}(v) = e^{-Jz}v$ and $\tau_{z}(v^{*}) = e^{Jz}v^{*}$, and at $z = -J\lambda$, $\lambda$ real, $e^{JzK} = e^{\lambda K} = R_{\lambda}$, so $\tau_{-J\lambda}(v) = e^{-\lambda}v$ and $\tau_{-J\lambda}(v^{*}) = e^{\lambda}v^{*}$: the rotor flow of Theorem \claimref{singularity.modular-structure-completed-pair}(2) is the phase flow at the parameter $t = -J\lambda$, that is $\lambda = Jt$. The continued boost on the mode operators, $e^{J\theta K} = e^{\theta I_{4}/2}$, and the dual-plane rotor $e^{\theta J/2}$ that the continuation gives when its unit is read as $I_{4}$ acting on values are different objects acting on different things: the second is central in $\Aa$ and acts trivially on it, so the two readings do not contradict each other.
\item[(vi)] \emph{(KMS and the modular flow.)} Let $T(x) = 2\br{x}_{0} - 2J\br{Jx}_{0}$, the trace of $\Aa$ over $\mathrm{span}\{1, J\}$ ($T(1) = 2$, $T(Jx) = JT(x)$, $T(xy) = T(yx)$), and for real $\beta$ let $\omega_{\beta}(x) = T(e^{-\beta K}x)/T(e^{-\beta K})$. Then $\omega_{\beta}$ is a state ($\omega_{\beta}(x^{*}x) > 0$ for $x \neq 0$), $\omega_{\beta}(v^{*}v) = 1/(1 + e^{\beta})$, and it satisfies the KMS condition of $\tau$ at $\beta$ with the unit $J$,
\[
\omega_{\beta}\bigl(x\,\tau_{J\beta}(y)\bigr) = \omega_{\beta}(yx) \quad (x, y \in \Aa), \qquad \tau_{J\beta} = \operatorname{Ad}(e^{-\beta K}),
\]
and, for $\beta \neq 0$, not at $-\beta$; it is the only $\mathrm{span}\{1, J\}$-linear state of $\Aa$ that does (Theorem \claimref{singularity.kms-uniqueness-factor}, for the matrix factor $\Aa$ over the field $\mathrm{span}\{1, J\}$). With $\varrho = e^{-\beta K}/T(e^{-\beta K})$ and $\varrho^{Jt} := e^{Jt\ln\varrho}$, $\operatorname{Ad}(\varrho^{Jt}) = \tau_{-\beta t}$, so $\operatorname{Ad}(\varrho^{Jt})(v) = e^{J\beta t}v$: the flow that is the modular group of $\omega_{\beta}$ in a matrix factor is the phase flow at $-\beta t$, written with $J$.
\end{enumerate}
synthesis.transverse-bivector-is-the-com.technical: The completed pair $v = \tfrac12(e_{0} + e_{1})$, $v^{*} = \tfrac12(e_{0} - e_{1})$ lives in the spacetime radial plane, where the field theory's unit $I_{4}$ anticommutes with both mode operators and cannot serve as their complex scalar: $(I_{4}v)(I_{4}w) = +vw$, not $-vw$. The unit bivector of the orthogonal plane, $J = e_{2}e_{3}$, can: it squares to $-1$, commutes with $e_{0}$, $e_{1}$ and so with the whole atom, is sent to $-J$ by the frame adjoint, and with $1$ spans the centre of the atom's algebra $\Cl(1,1) \oplus \Cl(1,1)J$, which is the one-mode CAR algebra over that field. It is the even such unit: the elements commuting with the atom form a quaternion algebra, whose odd units, such as $\sigma e_{2}$, also square to $-1$ but are not identified with $J$, and $J$ is the one fixed by rotations of the transverse plane, with its sign set by $J\sigma = +I_{4}$. The two units are related by $J\sigma = I_{4}$ with $\sigma = e_{0}e_{1}$: $I_{4}$ equals $J$ on the occupied projector $v^{*}v$ and $-J$ on $vv^{*}$. Written with $J$, the phase flow is $\operatorname{Ad}(e^{JtK})$ with $K = \sigma/2$, and it multiplies $v$ by $e^{-Jt}$ and $v^{*}$ by $e^{+Jt}$; since $JK = I_{4}/2$ it is conjugation by $e^{I_{4}t/2}$, which is not a rotor and maps no nonzero vector to a vector. At the parameter $t = -J\lambda$ it is the real rotor flow $e^{\lambda K}$, $v \mapsto e^{-\lambda}v$. The Gibbs state of $K$, computed with the trace of the atom over $\mathrm{span}\{1, J\}$, gives occupation $1/(1 + e^{\beta})$, satisfies the KMS relation $\omega_{\beta}(x\,\tau_{J\beta}(y)) = \omega_{\beta}(yx)$ and is the only $\mathrm{span}\{1, J\}$-linear state that does, and its modular flow is $\tau_{-\beta t}$. So the store's complex phase flow, its continuation, its KMS states and its modular group on this atom are all written with $J$.
synthesis.transverse-bivector-is-the-com.lay: At a horizon, the graph pairs two fermion modes, one moving outwards and one inwards, and builds them from the two directions of the plane in which the horizon boosts: time and the radial direction. Quantum mechanics needs a square root of minus one that acts on these modes as an ordinary number, and the usual choice in this algebra, the spacetime volume element, does not behave as a number here, because it reverses sign when moved past either direction. The plane of the two remaining directions, the one tangent to the horizon's sphere, supplies one that does, the only one built from the even part of the algebra: it squares to minus one and commutes with everything built from time and the radial direction. This result proves that, and rewrites the modes' time evolution, its thermal state and the link between real and imaginary time with that element in place of the imaginary unit, fixing every sign.

proofs.main:
\emph{Setting.} By Lemma \claimref{singularity.pseudo-inverse-identities-hyperbolic-atom}, $v = \tfrac12(e_{0} + e_{1})$ and $v^{*} = \tfrac12(e_{0} - e_{1})$ satisfy the canonical anticommutation relations $v^{2} = (v^{*})^{2} = 0$, $vv^{*} + v^{*}v = 1$ in $\Cl(1,1) = \mathrm{alg}(e_{0}, e_{1}) \subset \Cl(1,3)$, and by Theorem \claimref{singularity.modular-structure-completed-pair}(1) and (3), $\sigma = v^{*}v - vv^{*} = e_{0}e_{1}$, $\sigma^{2} = 1$, and $\tfrac12(1 \pm \sigma)$ are $v^{*}v$ and $vv^{*}$. Directly, $\sigma v = e_{0}e_{1}\tfrac12(e_{0} + e_{1}) = \tfrac12(-e_{1} - e_{0}) = -v$ and $v\sigma = v$, so $\sigma$ anticommutes with $v$, and likewise $\sigma v^{*} = v^{*} = -v^{*}\sigma$.

\emph{(i).} $J^{2} = e_{2}e_{3}e_{2}e_{3} = -e_{2}^{2}e_{3}^{2} = -1$. Each of $e_{0}$, $e_{1}$ anticommutes with $e_{2}$ and with $e_{3}$ (orthogonal vectors), hence commutes with their product $J$; so $J$ commutes with every element of $\Cl(1,1)$. $J\sigma = e_{2}e_{3}e_{0}e_{1}$: moving $e_{0}$ and then $e_{1}$ to the front past two factors each takes four transpositions, so $J\sigma = e_{0}e_{1}e_{2}e_{3} = I_{4}$, and $\sigma J = I_{4}$ as $J$ and $\sigma$ commute; with $\sigma^{2} = 1$, $J = I_{4}\sigma$. The frame $*$ of Theorem \claimref{tower.structure-tower-c-norms} on the real algebra is the antiautomorphism fixing the frame generator of square $+1$ and negating those of square $-1$; $x \mapsto e_{0}\rev{x}e_{0}$ is an antiautomorphism (reversion is one, conjugation by $e_{0}$ an automorphism) with $e_{0} \mapsto e_{0}$ and $e_{k} \mapsto e_{0}e_{k}e_{0} = -e_{k}$, so it is that $*$. Then $J^{*} = e_{3}^{*}e_{2}^{*} = e_{3}e_{2} = -J$. The centraliser: a blade $B$ commutes with a basis vector $e_{\mu}$ exactly when the number of factors of $B$ other than $e_{\mu}$ is even; requiring this for $e_{0}$ and $e_{1}$ leaves the blades $1$, $e_{2}e_{3}$, $e_{0}e_{1}e_{2}$, $e_{0}e_{1}e_{3}$ (conjugation by a basis vector maps each blade to $\pm$ itself, so the centraliser is spanned by blades). $u_{2} = e_{0}e_{1}e_{2}$ and $u_{3} = e_{0}e_{1}e_{3}$ satisfy $u_{2}^{2} = \sigma e_{2}\sigma e_{2} = \sigma^{2}e_{2}^{2} = -1$ ($e_{2}$ commutes with $\sigma$), likewise $u_{3}^{2} = -1$, $u_{2}u_{3} = \sigma^{2}e_{2}e_{3} = J$ and $u_{2}u_{3} = -u_{3}u_{2}$, so $J, u_{2}, u_{3}$ are anticommuting units of square $-1$ with $u_{2}u_{3} = J$: a quaternion algebra. Its even part is $\mathrm{span}\{1, J\}$, where $(a + bJ)^{2} = a^{2} - b^{2} + 2abJ = -1$ forces $a = 0$, $b = \pm 1$. The rotor $e^{\varphi J/2}$ of the transverse plane fixes $J$ and turns $(u_{2}, u_{3})$ through the angle $\varphi$, so among the units $aJ + bu_{2} + cu_{3}$ ($a^{2} + b^{2} + c^{2} = 1$) it fixes exactly $\pm J$. The odd units are $*$-antihermitian too: $u_{2}^{*} = e_{2}^{*}e_{1}^{*}e_{0}^{*} = -e_{2}e_{1}e_{0} = -u_{2}$.

\emph{(ii).} $\Cl(1,1)$ has basis $1, e_{0}, e_{1}, \sigma$, and the eight products of these with $1$ and $J$ are distinct basis blades of $\Cl(1,3)$, so $\Aa = \Cl(1,1) \oplus \Cl(1,1)J$ has dimension $8$; it is closed under products because $J$ commutes with $\Cl(1,1)$ and $J^{2} = -1$. An element $c = c_{1} + c_{2}J$ ($c_{1}, c_{2} \in \Cl(1,1)$) is central in $\Aa$ exactly when $c_{1}$ and $c_{2}$ are central in $\Cl(1,1)$, whose centre is $\R$ (even dimension), (Theorem \claimref{primer.centre}), so the centre of $\Aa$ is $\mathrm{span}\{1, J\}$, a field isomorphic to $\C$ as in any real algebra $\mathrm{span}\{1, u\}$ with $u^{2} = -1$. Over that field $\Aa$ is spanned by $1, e_{0}, e_{1}, \sigma$, and $e_{0} = v + v^{*}$, $e_{1} = v - v^{*}$, $\sigma = 2v^{*}v - 1$, so also by $1, v, v^{*}, v^{*}v$. Over any field $F$ the algebra presented by $v, v^{*}$ with the canonical anticommutation relations maps onto $\Mat_{2}(F)$ by its Fock representation ($v$ the matrix unit $E_{12}$, $v^{*}$ the matrix unit $E_{21}$), and it is spanned by $1, v, v^{*}, v^{*}v$ (every word in $v, v^{*}$ reduces to these by $v^{2} = 0$ and $vv^{*} = 1 - v^{*}v$); $\Aa$ is a quotient of it of dimension $4$ over $F = \mathrm{span}\{1, J\}$, equal to $\dim \Mat_{2}(F)$, so $\Aa \cong \Mat_{2}(F)$, the CAR algebra of one mode over $F$. The $*$ preserves $\Aa$ ($e_{0}$, $e_{1}$, $J$ are mapped into it), $v^{*} = \tfrac12(e_{0} - e_{1})$ is the image of $v$, $\sigma^{*} = e_{1}^{*}e_{0}^{*} = -e_{1}e_{0} = \sigma$, and $J^{*} = -J$ with $J$ central gives $(zx)^{*} = \bar{z}x^{*}$ for $z = a + bJ$, $\bar{z} = a - bJ$: conjugate-linear. The script checks the dimension, the closure, the centre by solving the linear system for the commutant of $e_{0}, e_{1}, J$ in $\Aa$, the spanning set $\{1, v, v^{*}, v^{*}v\}$ over the field by rank, and the antiautomorphism property of $*$ on all $256$ pairs of blades.

\emph{(iii).} $I_{4} = J\sigma$ lies in $\Aa$. Being the pseudoscalar of the even-dimensional $\Cl(1,3)$, it anticommutes with every vector, in particular with $e_{0}$, $e_{1}$ and their combinations $v$, $v^{*}$, so it is not central in $\Aa$. For vectors $a, b$, $(I_{4}a)(I_{4}b) = -I_{4}^{2}ab = ab$, while $J$ commutes with $a$ and $b$ of the radial plane and $(Ja)(Jb) = J^{2}ab = -ab$. $I_{4}P_{\pm} = J\sigma\tfrac12(1 \pm \sigma) = J\tfrac12(\sigma \pm 1) = \pm JP_{\pm}$. The script checks these on $e_{0}$, $e_{1}$, $v$, $v^{*}$ and $3e_{0} - 2e_{1}$, all pairs.

\emph{(iv).} $JK = \tfrac12J\sigma = \tfrac12I_{4}$ and $(2JK)^{2} = I_{4}^{2} = -1$. For any element $A$ with $A^{2} = -1$ the exponential series collapses as in Theorem \claimref{std-algebra.bivector-exponential} ($A^{2k} = (-1)^{k}$, $A^{2k+1} = (-1)^{k}A$; there for a bivector, the argument uses only the scalar square), so $e^{\theta A} = \cos\theta + A\sin\theta$, and with $A = 2JK$, $\theta = t/2$: $e^{JtK} = \cos\tfrac{t}{2} + 2JK\sin\tfrac{t}{2}$. Since $J$ commutes with $v$ and $\sigma v = -v$, $JKv = -\tfrac12Jv$ and $vJK = \tfrac12Jv$, so $JKv - vJK = -Jv$; likewise $+Jv^{*}$ for $v^{*}$. As $JK$ anticommutes with $v$, $e^{JtK}v = ve^{-JtK}$, so $\tau_{t}(v) = e^{JtK}ve^{-JtK} = e^{2JtK}v = e^{I_{4}t}v$, and $I_{4}v = J\sigma v = -Jv$ with $J$ commuting with $v$ gives $e^{I_{4}t}v = (\cos t - J\sin t)v = e^{-Jt}v$, the exponential $e^{-Jt} = \cos t - J\sin t$ being taken in the field $\mathrm{span}\{1, J\}$. For $v^{*}$, $I_{4}v^{*} = J\sigma v^{*} = Jv^{*}$ and $\tau_{t}(v^{*}) = e^{+Jt}v^{*}$. The $*$ is an antiautomorphism with $(JK)^{*} = K^{*}J^{*} = -KJ = -JK$, so $(e^{JtK})^{*} = e^{-JtK} = (e^{JtK})^{-1}$: $e^{JtK}$ is unitary and $\tau_{t}$ is a $*$-automorphism, $\tau_{t}\tau_{s} = \tau_{t+s}$, and it maps $\Aa$ into itself because $e^{JtK} \in \Aa$. $Jv = \tfrac12(e_{2}e_{3}e_{0} + e_{2}e_{3}e_{1})$ is a trivector, so for $\sin t \neq 0$ the image of a nonzero vector $a = \alpha e_{0} + \beta e_{1}$ of the plane, $e^{I_{4}t}a = a\cos t + I_{4}a\sin t$, has a nonzero trivector part. The script checks the commutators, $JK = I_{4}/2$ and $(2JK)^{2} = -1$, and at three rational points $(c, s) = ((1 - u^{2})/(1 + u^{2}), 2u/(1 + u^{2}))$ of the circle with $U = c + 2sJK$ (that is $c = \cos\tfrac{t}{2}$, $s = \sin\tfrac{t}{2}$): $UU^{-1} = 1$ with $U^{-1} = U^{*} = c - 2sJK$, $UvU^{-1} = (C - SJ)v$ and $Uv^{*}U^{-1} = (C + SJ)v^{*}$ with $C = c^{2} - s^{2}$, $S = 2cs$, against the wrong sign $(C + SJ)v$, and the addition law for two such points.

\emph{(v).} For $z = t + J\theta \in \mathrm{span}\{1, J\}$, $JzK$ commutes with $K$ and with $J$, and the computation of (iv) goes through with $z$ in place of $t$ because $z$ is central in $\Aa$: $JzKv - vJzK = -Jzv$, so $e^{JzK}ve^{-JzK} = e^{-Jz}v$, and $e^{JzK}$ is invertible with inverse $e^{-JzK}$. At $z = -J\lambda$, $Jz = -J^{2}\lambda = \lambda$, so $e^{JzK} = e^{\lambda K} = R_{\lambda}$, the rotor flow of Theorem \claimref{singularity.modular-structure-completed-pair}(2), and $e^{-Jz} = e^{-\lambda}$, $e^{Jz} = e^{\lambda}$, in agreement with $R_{\lambda}vR_{\lambda}^{-1} = e^{-\lambda}v$ and $R_{\lambda}v^{*}R_{\lambda}^{-1} = e^{\lambda}v^{*}$ there. The script checks at two rational values $a = e^{\lambda/2}$ that $R = \tfrac12(a + a^{-1}) + \tfrac12(a - a^{-1})\sigma$ has inverse $\tfrac12(a + a^{-1}) - \tfrac12(a - a^{-1})\sigma$ and gives $RvR^{-1} = a^{-2}v$, $Rv^{*}R^{-1} = a^{2}v^{*}$ (the closed form of $e^{\lambda\sigma/2}$ from Theorem \claimref{std-algebra.bivector-exponential}), and that at $t = -J\lambda$, $-Jt = -\lambda$ and $JtK = \lambda K$; and at the mixed parameter $z = t + J\theta$, with $e^{JzK} = e^{JtK}e^{-\theta K}$ formed from a rational circle point and a rational $e^{\theta/2}$, that $\tau_{z}(v) = e^{-Jz}v = e^{\theta}e^{-Jt}v$ and $\tau_{z}(v^{*}) = e^{Jz}v^{*} = e^{-\theta}e^{Jt}v^{*}$. The continued boost $e^{J\theta K} = e^{\theta I_{4}/2}$ acts on $\Aa$ by (iv); the rotor $e^{\theta J/2}$ is central in $\Aa$, so its conjugation is the identity there, and it is a different element.

\emph{(vi).} Write $x = x_{1} + x_{2}J$ with $x_{1}, x_{2} \in \Cl(1,1)$. Then $\br{x}_{0} = \br{x_{1}}_{0}$ and $\br{Jx}_{0} = -\br{x_{2}}_{0}$, so $T(x) = 2\br{x_{1}}_{0} + 2J\br{x_{2}}_{0}$, which is $T(Jx) = JT(x)$; $T(xy) = T(yx)$ follows from $\br{xy}_{0} = \br{yx}_{0}$ in any Clifford algebra and the centrality of $J$ in $\Aa$ ($\br{Jxy}_{0} = \br{yJx}_{0} = \br{Jyx}_{0}$). Under the isomorphism of (ii) $T$ is the matrix trace, since an $F$-linear functional on $\Mat_{2}(F)$ vanishing on commutators is a multiple of the trace and $T(1) = 2$; so $T(P_{\pm}) = 1$. $e^{-\beta K} = e^{-\beta/2}P_{+} + e^{\beta/2}P_{-}$ (the projectors are the spectral projectors of $\sigma$), so up to the positive factor $e^{-\beta/2}$, which cancels, $\varrho \propto P_{+} + qP_{-}$ with $q = e^{\beta} > 0$, $T(\varrho) \propto 1 + q$ and $\omega_{\beta}(v^{*}v) = \omega_{\beta}(P_{+}) = 1/(1 + q)$. Under the isomorphism with $\Mat_{2}$ over the field, in the Fock basis, $*$ is the conjugate transpose (it is a conjugate-linear antiautomorphism with $v \mapsto v^{*}$, so it agrees with the conjugate transpose on the generators $v$, $v^{*}$ and $J$) and $\varrho$ is diagonal with positive entries, so $\omega_{\beta}(x^{*}x) = T(\varrho x^{*}x)/T(\varrho)$ is the trace of the positive matrix $x\varrho x^{*}$ divided by a positive number: real and positive for $x \neq 0$. KMS: $\tau_{J\beta} = \operatorname{Ad}(e^{J\cdot J\beta K}) = \operatorname{Ad}(e^{-\beta K}) = \operatorname{Ad}(\varrho)$, and $T(\varrho\,x\,\varrho y\varrho^{-1}) = T(x\varrho y) = T(\varrho yx)$ by cyclicity, so $\omega_{\beta}(x\,\tau_{J\beta}(y)) = \omega_{\beta}(yx)$. At $-\beta$ the same computation gives $\omega_{\beta}(x\varrho^{-1}y\varrho) = T(\varrho x\varrho^{-1}y\varrho)/T(\varrho)$, which for $x = v$, $y = v^{*}$ is $q^{2}/(1 + q)$ against $\omega_{\beta}(v^{*}v) = 1/(1 + q)$, so it fails for every $\beta \neq 0$ (at $\beta = 0$ both conditions hold, $\omega_{0}$ being the trace). $\Aa$ is a matrix factor over the field $\mathrm{span}\{1, J\}$, and the flow is $\tau_{t} = \operatorname{Ad}(e^{JtK})$ with $J$ the unit of that field; Theorem \claimref{singularity.kms-uniqueness-factor} uses only the structure of a complex matrix factor, which $\Aa$ is with $J$ as its unit, so $\omega_{\beta}$ is the only $\mathrm{span}\{1, J\}$-linear $(\tau, \beta)$-KMS state (at $\beta = 0$ this is the uniqueness of the normalised trace of a factor). The field-linearity is needed: the real parts $x \mapsto \br{(1 + bJ)\,\omega_{\beta}(x)}_{0}$, $b$ real, are real-linear, normalised, positive and KMS for every $b$, and differ from one another at $x = J$. Finally $\ln\varrho = -\beta K - \ln T(e^{-\beta K})$, so $\varrho^{Jt} = e^{-J\beta tK}e^{-Jt\ln T(e^{-\beta K})}$, the second factor is central in $\Aa$, and $\operatorname{Ad}(\varrho^{Jt}) = \operatorname{Ad}(e^{J(-\beta t)K}) = \tau_{-\beta t}$, with $\tau_{-\beta t}(v) = e^{J\beta t}v$ by (iv). The script checks, at $q = 3$ and $q = 2/7$, that $T$ is $J$-valued on $1$ and $J$ and cyclic on all $64$ pairs of the real basis of $\Aa$; that $\omega_{\beta}(P_{+}) = 1/(1 + q)$; the KMS identity on all $64$ pairs, and its failure for $\operatorname{Ad}(\varrho^{-1})$; positivity of $\omega_{\beta}(x^{*}x)$ on ten elements; that the densities $r \in \Aa$ with $T(rx\varrho y\varrho^{-1}) = T(ryx)$ for all basis $x, y$ form a real space of dimension $2$, the $J$-line of $\varrho$; and, at a rational point $w = C + SJ$ of the unit circle of the field, that $\operatorname{Ad}(P_{+} + wP_{-})$ sends $v$ to $wv$ and $v^{*}$ to $\bar{w}v^{*}$, which is $\operatorname{Ad}(\varrho^{Jt})$ with $w = e^{J\beta t}$ up to a central factor. $\square$

synthesis.univalence-even-extension-spli.formal:
Let $\Aa$ be the boundary-mode algebra of $N$ completed modes with parity automorphism $\alpha = \operatorname{Ad}(\Gamma)$ (Definition \claimref{obj.singularity.grading-parity-automorphism}), even part $\Aev$, odd part $\Aod$, and $E := \tfrac12(\mathrm{id} + \alpha)$. Write (R) for Premise \claimref{singularity.r-regularity-fixed-locus} and (P) for Premise \claimref{singularity.p-univalence}.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(Even extension.)} For every state $\omega$ on $\Aa$, $\omega \circ E$ is an even state equal to $\omega$ on $\Aev$, and it is the only even state with that restriction. So the states of the even subalgebra, the observables of Fact \claimref{singularity.imported-univalence-superselection-rule}, correspond one to one to the even states of $\Aa$, and (P) says exactly that the state on $\Aa$ is the even extension of its restriction to the observables. No expectation value of an even element distinguishes $\omega$ from $\omega \circ E$; what (P) fixes are the odd expectation values, among them the off-diagonal entries $\omega(v_k)$ of the ascended single-mode marginals.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(R) as stated does not give (P).} At a mode of weight $\omega_k$, with $n = (e^{p\omega_k} + 1)^{-1}$ and $0 < c^2 \leq n(1 - n)$, the state $\varrho = \begin{psmallmatrix} 1 - n & c \\ c & n \end{psmallmatrix}$ of the mode factor satisfies the KMS relation of (R) for every pair in the ladder $\{v_k, v_k^{*}\}$, has the Gibbs state as its descended marginal, and has $\omega(v_k) = c \neq 0$.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(Full-factor KMS gives the single-mode part.)} If the marginal at mode $k$ satisfies the KMS relation of (R) for all pairs $a, b$ in the mode factor $\Mat_2(\C)$, it is the Gibbs state of $K_k$, so $\omega(v_k) = 0$; this holds at every weight, and at zero weight the relation is traciality and gives the marginal $\tfrac12$.
\item[(iv)] \emph{(The cross-mode part is not local.)} For $N \geq 2$, single-mode evenness at every mode does not imply (P): on two modes, $\varrho = \varrho_1 \otimes \varrho_2 + c\,(v_1 + v_1^{*})(1 - 2v_2^{*}v_2)$ in the Jordan-Wigner representation, with $\varrho_1, \varrho_2$ diagonal Gibbs states and $c \neq 0$ small, is a state whose two single-mode marginals are $\varrho_1$ and $\varrho_2$ and which gives the odd element $(v_1 + v_1^{*})(1 - 2v_2^{*}v_2)$ the value $4c$.
\item[(v)] \emph{(Graded products.)} If $\omega(xy) = \omega(x)\omega(y)$ for $x$ in the algebra of one set of modes and $y$ in that of a disjoint set, at most one of the two restrictions is non-even.
\end{enumerate}
So (P) is the conjunction of a single-mode part, $\omega(v_k) = 0$ at every $k$, which the full-factor reading of (R) supplies, and a cross-mode part, the vanishing of odd correlations across modes, which no single-mode condition supplies and which no even observable detects.
synthesis.univalence-even-extension-spli.technical: The univalence premise (P) asks every physical state of the boundary modes to be even. The superselection rule it is usually traced to says that only even elements are observable. These are different statements: every state on the even observables has exactly one even extension to the whole algebra, $\omega \circ E$, and agrees with every other extension on all observables, so (P) is the choice of that extension and has no consequence for any even observable. What (P) fixes are odd expectation values, including the off-diagonal entries of the single-mode marginals. Its single-mode part follows if the regularity premise (R) is read on the whole mode factor rather than on the ladder pairs alone: such a marginal is Gibbs, hence diagonal, at every weight. As stated, (R) admits coherent non-even marginals. The cross-mode part, no odd correlation between modes, follows from no single-mode condition, as a two-mode model shows. A product state across disjoint sets of modes can be non-even on one factor at most.
synthesis.univalence-even-extension-spli.lay: The series assumes that the physical states of the boundary modes never mix states with an even and an odd number of particles. A standard rule of quantum theory already says that such mixtures cannot be observed. This result shows the assumption adds nothing that any measurement could see. It is a choice of bookkeeping for quantities nobody can measure. Part of it follows if each mode is required to be thermal in the full sense. The rest, about correlations between different modes, does not follow from anything said about one mode at a time.

proofs.main:
\emph{(i).} $\alpha$ is a $*$-automorphism with $\alpha^2 = \mathrm{id}$, so $E = \tfrac12(\mathrm{id} + \alpha)$ is a positive unital projection onto $\Aev$ fixing $\Aev$ pointwise and killing $\Aod$ (Definition \claimref{obj.singularity.grading-parity-automorphism}). For a state $\omega$, $\omega \circ E = \tfrac12(\omega + \omega \circ \alpha)$ is a convex combination of states, hence a state; it is $\alpha$-invariant because $E \circ \alpha = E$, and it equals $\omega$ on $\Aev$ because $E$ fixes $\Aev$. If $\omega'$ is even and agrees with $\omega$ on $\Aev$, then for every $x$, $\omega'(x) = \omega'(Ex) = \omega(Ex)$, since $Ex \in \Aev$ and an even state satisfies $\omega' = \omega' \circ E$; so $\omega' = \omega \circ E$. Restriction to $\Aev$ and $\eta \mapsto \eta \circ E$ are therefore inverse bijections between the states of $\Aev$ and the even states of $\Aa$. The observable clause of Fact \claimref{singularity.imported-univalence-superselection-rule} makes $\Aev$ the observables; every even element $x$ has $\omega(x) = (\omega \circ E)(x)$, so no observable separates a state from its even part, and (P), $\omega \circ \alpha = \omega$, is the statement $\omega = \omega \circ E$. On one mode $v_k \in \Aod$, so $\omega(v_k)$, the off-diagonal entry of the ascended marginal in the number basis, is among the values (P) fixes. The check \texttt{check\_even\_part\_is\_unique\_even\_extension} verifies on two modes, for a non-even positive $\varrho$, that $\tfrac12(\varrho + \Gamma\varrho\Gamma)$ is positive of trace one, agrees with $\varrho$ on all eight even matrix units, vanishes on the eight odd ones, and is $\Gamma$-invariant, while $\varrho$ itself has a nonzero odd value.

\emph{The flow at imaginary time.} On one mode take the number basis, $v = E_{01}$, $v^{*} = E_{10}$, $v^{*}v = N_k = E_{11}$, and the Killing flow $\alpha_t = \operatorname{Ad}(e^{Jt\omega_k N_k})$, with $J = e_{2}e_{3}$ the complex unit of the completed modes (\claimref{synthesis.transverse-bivector-is-the-complex-unit-of-the-radial-atom}), the scalars of the mode factor being $\mathrm{span}\{1, J\}$ (the generator differs from $\omega_k K_k$ by a multiple of the identity, which does not change $\operatorname{Ad}$). Then $\alpha_{Jp}(E_{ij}) = e^{-p\omega_k N_k} E_{ij} e^{p\omega_k N_k} = r^{\,j - i} E_{ij}$ with $r := e^{p\omega_k} > 0$, and for matrices the analytic continuation in (R) is this substitution, so the KMS relation for a pair $(a, b)$ reads $\omega(a\,\alpha_{Jp}(b)) = \omega(b\,a)$.

\emph{(ii).} For $\varrho = \begin{psmallmatrix} 1-n & c \\ c & n\end{psmallmatrix}$, the four ladder pairs give: $(v^{*}, v)$: $r\,\omega(v^{*}v) = \omega(vv^{*})$, that is $rn = 1 - n$, which is $n = (r+1)^{-1}$; $(v, v^{*})$: $r^{-1}\omega(vv^{*}) = \omega(v^{*}v)$, the same equation; $(v, v)$ and $(v^{*}, v^{*})$: both sides vanish since $v^2 = 0$. The value $c$ enters none of them. $\varrho$ is positive exactly when $c^2 \leq n(1-n)$; its pinching is $\operatorname{diag}(1-n, n)$, the Gibbs state, as Theorem \claimref{singularity.descended-form-state-independent} says it must be for any state; and $\omega(v) = \operatorname{tr}(\varrho E_{01}) = c$. The check \texttt{check\_ladder\_kms\_admits\_coherence} verifies all of this for five values of $r$ (including $r = 1$) and the admissible $c$ among three, and that the same states fail the relation on the whole factor.

\emph{(iii).} Impose the relation for all sixteen pairs of matrix units on an unknown $\varrho = \begin{psmallmatrix} a & b \\ c & d \end{psmallmatrix}$. The pair $(E_{00}, E_{01})$ gives $r\,\omega(E_{01}) = \omega(E_{01}E_{00}) = 0$, so $\omega(E_{01}) = c = 0$ (the entry $\operatorname{tr}(\varrho E_{01})$ is $c$); likewise $(E_{11}, E_{10})$ gives $b = 0$; the pair $(E_{10}, E_{01})$ gives $r\,d = a$. With $a + d = 1$ the solution is unique: $\varrho = \operatorname{diag}(r, 1)/(r + 1)$, the Gibbs state with occupation $(r+1)^{-1}$, which is diagonal, so $\omega(v_k) = 0$. This is the one-mode case of the statement that Gibbs states of even generators are even (filed alongside, synthesis.univalence-from-even-stationary-dynamics, clause (2)); it is computed here because the zero-weight case is needed in the form of traciality. At zero weight $r = 1$ the relation is $\omega(ab) = \omega(ba)$ for all $a, b$, whose only normalised solution on $\Mat_2(\C)$ is the trace state $\tfrac12\operatorname{tr}$, again diagonal, with occupation $\tfrac12$. The check \texttt{check\_full\_kms\_forces\_single\_mode\_evenness} assembles the sixteen linear relations plus normalisation, verifies that they have rank four (a unique solution) and that the Gibbs state solves them, for the same five values of $r$.

\emph{(iv).} In the Jordan-Wigner representation on $\C^2 \otimes \C^2$, $v_1 = v \otimes 1$, $v_2 = P \otimes v$ with $P = \operatorname{diag}(1, -1) = 1 - 2N$, $\Gamma = P \otimes P$; then $\{v_1, v_2\} = \{v_1, v_2^{*}\} = 0$ and $\{v_1, v_1^{*}\} = 1$, and $1 - 2v_2^{*}v_2 = 1 \otimes P$. The element $y := (v_1 + v_1^{*})(1 - 2v_2^{*}v_2) = X \otimes P$, $X = v + v^{*}$, is odd: $\Gamma y \Gamma = (PXP) \otimes P = -y$. Put $\varrho = \varrho_1 \otimes \varrho_2 + c\,y$. Since $\operatorname{tr}(X) = \operatorname{tr}(P) = \operatorname{tr}(XP) = 0$, the term $c\,y$ contributes nothing to the expectation of any $E_{ij} \otimes 1$ (the mode-1 factor) or of $1$, $1 \otimes N$, $v_2 = P \otimes v$, $v_2^{*}$ (the mode-2 factor), so the two marginals are $\varrho_1$ and $\varrho_2$; and $\operatorname{tr}(\varrho\, y) = c\operatorname{tr}(y^2) = 4c$. In the basis ordered by mode 2, $\varrho$ is a direct sum of two $2 \times 2$ blocks $\begin{psmallmatrix} (1-n_1)g & \pm c \\ \pm c & n_1 g\end{psmallmatrix}$, $g$ an eigenvalue of $\varrho_2$, so $\varrho \geq 0$ exactly when $c^2 \leq n_1(1 - n_1)\min(n_2, 1 - n_2)^2$, which leaves room for $c \neq 0$. The check \texttt{check\_cross\_mode\_odd\_correlation\_with\_even\_gibbs\_marginals} verifies the CAR relations, the oddness of $y$, positivity, the marginals and the value $4c$ for three pairs of Gibbs marginals.

\emph{(v).} Let $x$ be odd in the algebra of one set of modes and $y$ odd in that of a disjoint set. Odd elements of disjoint modes anticommute ($v_j$ and $v_k^{(*)}$ do for $j \neq k$, and products of an odd number of them inherit it), so $xy = -yx$. A product state would give $\omega(xy) = \omega(x)\omega(y)$ and $\omega(yx) = \omega(y)\omega(x)$, and $\omega(xy) = -\omega(yx)$ then forces $\omega(x)\omega(y) = 0$. If both restrictions were non-even there would be odd $x$, $y$ with $\omega(x)\omega(y) \neq 0$, a contradiction. One non-even factor is possible: with $\varrho_1$ as in (ii) and $\varrho_2$ even, $\varrho_1 \otimes \varrho_2$ is a state, product across the two modes. The check \texttt{check\_graded\_product\_has\_one\_odd\_factor\_at\_most} verifies $xy = -yx$ for $x = X \otimes 1$, $y = P \otimes X$; that the one-odd-factor state $\varrho_1 \otimes \varrho_2$ (with $\varrho_2$ even) satisfies $\omega(ab) = \omega(a)\omega(b)$ for all sixteen pairs with $a \in \{E_{ij} \otimes 1\}$ and $b \in \{1 \otimes E_{kk},\, P \otimes E_{kl}\}$; and that for two coherent factors the Jordan-Wigner tensor product $\varrho_1 \otimes \varrho_2'$ is a state that is not a product: $\omega(xy) = 0$ while $\omega(x)\omega(y) = 2c_1(1 - 2n_1)\,2c_2 \neq 0$ for $n_1 \neq \tfrac12$.

\emph{Conclusion.} (P) is $\omega(z) = 0$ for every odd $z$. The odd elements of a single mode factor are spanned by $v_k, v_k^{*}$, so (P) contains the single-mode part, supplied by (iii) under the full-factor reading of (R) and not by (R) as stated, by (ii); the remaining odd elements involve two or more modes, and (iv) shows their expectations are not fixed by any condition on single-mode marginals, while (i) shows none of this is visible to an even observable.

synthesis.univalence-from-even-stationar.formal:
Let the boundary modes $a_1, \dots, a_n$ generate the CAR algebra, realised on Fock space as the spinor module of the Clifford algebra of their $2n$ Majorana generators $\mu_{2k-1} = a_k + a_k^*$, $\mu_{2k} = J(a_k^* - a_k)$, with $J = e_{2}e_{3}$ the complex unit of the boundary modes, which commutes with them and squares to $-1$, the Fock space's scalars being $\mathrm{span}\{1, J\}$ (\claimref{synthesis.transverse-bivector-is-the-complex-unit-of-the-radial-atom}), with parity the chirality (Fact \claimref{rungs.imported-fock-representation-bogoliubov-group}), and let $\alpha$ be the grading.
\begin{enumerate}
\item The grading is inner and is the rotation by $\pi$ in every mode plane: with $B_k = \mu_{2k-1}\mu_{2k}$ and $R_k(\theta) = \cos(\theta/2) - B_k\sin(\theta/2)$, $R_k(\pi) = -B_k$ negates the two generators of the $k$-th plane and fixes the others, and $\alpha = \operatorname{Ad}(B_1 \cdots B_n)$, the volume element of the mode space; on Fock space it is implemented by $\Gamma = \prod_k (1 - 2N_k)$.
\item If $H = H^*$ is even, $\alpha(H) = H$, every state with density a function of $H$, in particular every Gibbs state $e^{-\beta H}/Z$ at real $\beta$ ($\beta = 0$ included), is even: $\omega \circ \alpha = \omega$.
\item Every state invariant under the flow $\operatorname{Ad}(e^{JtH})$ of an even $H$ is even if and only if the spectra of $H$ on the even and odd Fock sectors are disjoint. For $H = \sum_k \omega_k N_k$ this holds if and only if no signed sum $\sum_{k \in S} \varepsilon_k\omega_k$, $\varepsilon_k = \pm 1$, over a set $S$ of odd size vanishes. It holds when every weight is an odd multiple of one $\omega_0 \neq 0$ (a common nonzero weight in particular), and then $\alpha$ is the flow itself at time $\pi/\omega_0$.
\item It fails at a zero-weight mode, where $\tfrac12(1 + \tfrac12(a + a^*))$ is stationary and not even, and at an odd resonance: for weights $(1,2,3)$ the state $\tfrac18(1 + \tfrac12(x + x^*))$, $x = a_1a_2a_3^*$, is stationary, positive and not even.
\end{enumerate}
For the boundary modes' boost generator $K_{\mathrm{geo}} = \sum_k \omega_k K_k$ of the geometric modular condition (G) (Definition \claimref{obj.singularity.geometric-modular-condition-g}), with mode-dependent weights $\omega_k$, every stationary state is even if and only if no signed sum of an odd number of the $\omega_k$ vanishes; zero-weight modes violate this, and a common nonzero weight is an example that satisfies it. Every faithful state satisfying (G) is a Gibbs state of the even generator $K_{\mathrm{geo}}$, hence even by (2): (G) implies Premise \claimref{singularity.p-univalence}. Beyond these classes the premise excludes exactly the odd coherences at zero weight and at odd resonances, and it constrains states that are not stationary.
synthesis.univalence-from-even-stationar.technical:
The grading of a fermionic mode algebra is not an outer symmetry that must be postulated: it is the rotation by $\pi$ in every mode plane, implemented by the product of the plane bivectors, which is the volume element of the mode space (on Fock space, the parity operator). Any state invariant under a flow that contains this rotation is therefore even, which is the superselection mechanism of Wick, Wightman and Wigner in an internal form: the symmetry that acts as the grading is part of the dynamics.

Two consequences follow for an even generator $H$, and a corollary for the geometric modular condition (G): a faithful state whose modular flow is the boost generated by $K_{\mathrm{geo}}$ is a Gibbs state of that even generator, so (G) implies (P). Gibbs states, being functions of $H$, commute with the parity and are even at every temperature, including the tracial state at zero weight. Stationary states are even for every such state exactly when the even and odd sectors share no energy; for a weighted number operator this is the absence of a vanishing signed sum of an odd number of weights, and a common nonzero weight suffices (the flow at time $\pi/\omega_0$ is then the grading). The premise adds content only at zero weight, at odd resonances such as $\omega_3 = \omega_1 + \omega_2$, and for non-stationary states; explicit stationary non-even states exist in the first two cases. Because the conditions are on the joint state, they deliver the cross-mode part of (P), the vanishing of odd correlations between modes, which no condition on single-mode marginals can supply.
synthesis.univalence-from-even-stationar.lay: The series assumes that physical states of its boundary modes never mix an even with an odd number of fermions. This result shows that the assumption follows from equilibrium. Flipping the sign of every fermion turns out to be the same as letting each mode's internal clock run half a turn. A state that is unchanged by the modes' own time evolution is therefore unchanged by that sign flip as well, provided no combination of an odd number of mode frequencies cancels out. Thermal states always qualify, and so does any state satisfying the series' geometric modular condition. The assumption still says something new only for modes of exactly zero frequency, for special frequency coincidences, and for states that change in time.

proofs.main:
\emph{(1)} The Majorana generators satisfy $\mu_j^2 = 1$ and anticommute. For $j$ outside the $k$-th plane, $B_k$ commutes with $\mu_j$ (two transpositions); for $j$ in it, $B_k \mu_{2k-1} B_k^{-1} = -\mu_{2k-1}$ and likewise for $\mu_{2k}$, with $B_k^{-1} = -B_k = \tilde B_k$. Since $B_k^2 = -1$, $R_k(\theta) = \exp(-\theta B_k/2) = \cos(\theta/2) - B_k\sin(\theta/2)$, and $R_k(\pi) = -B_k$, whose adjoint action is that of $B_k$: rotation by $\pi$ in the $k$-th plane. The product $B_1 \cdots B_n = \mu_1 \mu_2 \cdots \mu_{2n}$ is the volume element, and its adjoint action negates every generator, hence agrees with $\alpha$ on generators and so on the algebra. On Fock space, $J$ commuting with the mode operators, $-J \mu_{2k-1}\mu_{2k} = -J(a_k + a_k^*)\,J(a_k^* - a_k) = (a_k + a_k^*)(a_k^* - a_k) = a_k a_k^* - a_k^* a_k = 1 - 2N_k$, so $\prod_k(1 - 2N_k) = (-J)^n B_1\cdots B_n$ implements $\alpha$; this is the chirality of the spinor module of Fact \claimref{rungs.imported-fock-representation-bogoliubov-group}. In terms of the mode operators, $\operatorname{Ad}(e^{J\theta N_k})a_k = e^{-J\theta}a_k$, and $e^{J\pi N_k} = 1 - 2N_k$: the phase of a mode operator is the rotation angle of its plane.

\emph{(2)} $\alpha(H) = H$ means $\Gamma H \Gamma^{-1} = H$, so $\Gamma$ commutes with every polynomial in $H$ and, the space being finite dimensional, with every function of $H$ (a function of a diagonalisable matrix is a polynomial in it, the Lagrange interpolant on its spectrum). For $\rho = f(H)$, $\omega(\alpha(x)) = \operatorname{tr}(\rho\,\Gamma x \Gamma^{-1}) = \operatorname{tr}(\Gamma^{-1}\rho\Gamma\, x) = \operatorname{tr}(\rho x) = \omega(x)$.

\emph{(3)} A state $\rho$ is invariant under $\operatorname{Ad}(e^{JtH})$ for all real $t$ iff $[\rho, H] = 0$, iff $\rho$ is block diagonal with respect to the eigenspaces of $H$. Since $\Gamma$ commutes with $H$, each eigenspace $E_\lambda$ splits as $E_\lambda^+ \oplus E_\lambda^-$ into its even and odd parts. If every eigenspace has a definite parity (one part zero), every block-diagonal $\rho$ commutes with $\Gamma$, which is constant on each block, so it is even. If some $E_\lambda$ has both parts nonzero, take unit vectors $u^\pm \in E_\lambda^\pm$ and $\rho = \tfrac12(\lvert u^+\rangle + \lvert u^-\rangle)(\langle u^+\rvert + \langle u^-\rvert)$: it commutes with $H$, and $\operatorname{tr}(\rho\,\lvert u^+\rangle\langle u^-\rvert) = \tfrac12 \neq 0$ on an odd element, so it is not even. Both parts nonzero is exactly a common eigenvalue of $H$ on the two sectors. For $H = \sum_k\omega_kN_k$ the eigenvalues on the occupation basis are $\sum_{k\in T}\omega_k$ with parity $|T| \bmod 2$; a coincidence $\sum_{T}\omega = \sum_{T'}\omega$ with $|T|$, $|T'|$ of opposite parity is the vanishing of $\sum_{T\setminus T'}\omega_k - \sum_{T'\setminus T}\omega_k$, a signed sum over the symmetric difference, of odd size; conversely a vanishing signed sum over odd $S$ gives $T = \{\varepsilon_k = +1\}$, $T' = \{\varepsilon_k = -1\}$. If every $\omega_k = (2m_k+1)\omega_0$, a signed sum of an odd number of them is $\omega_0$ times a sum of an odd number of odd integers, which is odd, hence nonzero; and $e^{J\pi H/\omega_0} = \prod_k e^{J\pi(2m_k+1)N_k} = \prod_k(1-2N_k) = \Gamma$. When the spectra are disjoint, $\Gamma$ is the Lagrange polynomial in $H$ taking the value $\pm 1$ on the eigenvalues of the even and odd sectors, which the check confirms for weights $(1,3,5)$ and $(1,2)$.

\emph{(4)} For one mode of weight zero, $H = 0$ and every state is stationary; $\tfrac12(1 + \tfrac12(a + a^*))$ is positive and has $\omega(a + a^*) = \tfrac12$. For weights $(1,2,3)$, $x = a_1a_2a_3^*$ shifts the eigenvalue of $H$ by $-1-2+3 = 0$, so $X = x + x^*$ commutes with $H$; $X$ is Hermitian with $X^3 = X$ (the check confirms that $P = X^2$ is a projection with $XP = X$), so its eigenvalues lie in $\{-1,0,1\}$ and $\tfrac18(1 + \tfrac12 X)$ is a density matrix; it commutes with $H$ and not with $\Gamma$, and $\omega(X) = \tfrac{1}{16}\operatorname{tr}(X^2) \neq 0$ on the odd element $X$.

\emph{The final sentence.} The boost of the geometric modular condition (Definition \claimref{obj.singularity.geometric-modular-condition-g}) is $K_{\mathrm{geo}} = \sum_k \omega_k K_k$ with $K_k = \tfrac12\sigma_k = N_k - \tfrac12$ in the Fock representation and mode-dependent weights $\omega_k$. It is even, and it differs from $\sum_k\omega_kN_k$ by a constant, so its stationary states and its sector spectra are those of (3): every $K_{\mathrm{geo}}$-stationary state is even iff no signed sum of an odd number of the $\omega_k$ vanishes; a zero weight is such a sum on its own, and a common nonzero weight $\kappa$ is the case $\omega_0 = \kappa$ of (3). For (G): a faithful state $\rho$ on the finite-dimensional factor has modular group $\operatorname{Ad}(\rho^{Jt})$; if this equals $\operatorname{Ad}(e^{JtcK_{\mathrm{geo}}})$ for all $t$ (the constant $c$ absorbing the reparametrisation), then $\rho^{Jt}e^{-JtcK_{\mathrm{geo}}}$ commutes with the whole matrix algebra, so it is a scalar $e^{J t \gamma}$ (a continuous one-parameter group of scalars), and differentiating at $t = 0$ gives $\log\rho = cK_{\mathrm{geo}} + \gamma$: $\rho$ is a Gibbs state of $K_{\mathrm{geo}}$, even by (2). States outside these classes, and stationary states with a zero-weight mode or an odd resonance, are where the premise is an independent input, by (4).

transport.pinching-kernel.formal:
Define the pinching $E : B \to B$, $E(x) = PxP + (1-P)x(1-P)$. Then:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $E$ is an idempotent linear map whose image is the commutant $C = \{x \in B : xP = Px\} = A \oplus A\,ff^*$, on which it restricts to the identity, and $E$ is a $C$-bimodule map: $E(cxc') = c\,E(x)\,c'$ for $c, c' \in C$, with $E(1) = 1$: a conditional expectation onto $C$.
\item Its kernel is exactly the adjoined ladder sector:
\[
\ker E \;=\; PB(1-P) \,\oplus\, (1-P)BP \;=\; A f^* \,\oplus\, A f .
\]
In particular $E(f) = E(f^*) = 0$: the pinching erases precisely the pair the ascent adjoined, and nothing else.
\item The round trip is exact on transported elements: for $a \in A$, $E(a) = a$, and the corner read-out $D(x) = PxP$, identified with an $A$-valued map through the natural corner isomorphism $E_{22}BE_{22} = A\,f^*f \cong A$ ($a \mapsto a\,f^*f$), satisfies $D(a) = a$: ascent-then-descent is the \emph{identity} on the base. (In the Peirce coordinates of Theorem \claimref{transport.rule-1-morita-trivial}, which identify the $(2,2)$ block with the $(1,1)$ corner by conjugating with $E_{12} = f$, the same round trip reads as the grade involution $\hat{a}$; the two corner identifications differ by exactly the grade twist of the embedding $a \mapsto \mathrm{diag}(a,\hat a)$, and either way the map is an automorphism, faithful.) The multiplicative defect of $D$ on general elements is the exact interposition formula
\[
D(xy) - D(x)D(y) \;=\; P\,x\,(1-P)\,y\,P .
\]
\end{enumerate}
transport.pinching-kernel.technical:
In the Rule-1 completion $B \cong \Mat_2(A)$ with descent projector $P = f^*f$, the pinching $E(x) = PxP + (1-P)x(1-P)$ is an idempotent, unital, $C$-bimodule map onto the commutant $C = \{x \in B : xP = Px\} = A \oplus A\,ff^*$: a conditional expectation onto $C$. Its kernel is exactly the adjoined ladder sector $PB(1-P) \oplus (1-P)BP = Af^* \oplus Af$, so in particular $E(f) = E(f^*) = 0$.

On transported elements the round trip is exact: $E(a) = a$, and the corner read-out $D(x) = PxP$ satisfies $D(a) = a$ under the natural corner isomorphism; in Peirce coordinates the same map reads as the grade involution, still an automorphism. On general elements $D$ fails to be multiplicative by exactly $D(xy) - D(x)D(y) = Px(1-P)yP$.
transport.pinching-kernel.lay: After moving up to the completed algebra there is a canonical way to come back down: keep the blocks that commute with a chosen projector and discard the rest. What is discarded is exactly the new ladder pair that the completion added, and every element of the original algebra comes back unchanged under the natural identification of the corner (under the other standard identification it comes back as its grade involution, still faithfully). Coming back down does not respect multiplication in general, and the result gives the exact correction term.
transport.pinching-kernel.typing_note: Kept the Rule-1 Morita theorem, whose matrix picture and Peirce coordinates the statement and proof are built on; no other edges. Levels pass: the lay now says the round trip is the identity under the natural corner identification and the grade involution under the Peirce one.

proofs.main: (1) $E^2 = E$ and $E(1) = P + (1-P) = 1$ are immediate from $P^2 = P$. If $xP = Px$ then the cross-blocks of $x$ vanish ($Px(1-P) = xP(1-P) = 0$ and symmetrically), so $x = PxP + (1-P)x(1-P) = E(x)$; conversely $E(x)$ commutes with $P$ for any $x$; hence $\mathrm{im}\,E = C$ and $E|_C = \mathrm{id}$. The bimodule property follows by moving $c, c'$ through the projectors they commute with. The identification $C = A \oplus A\,ff^*$: $A$ commutes with $P$ (evenness of $f^*f$ in the $H$-factor) and so does $ff^*$, giving $A \oplus A\,ff^* \subseteq C$; and the two diagonal Peirce blocks $PBP \oplus (1-P)B(1-P) = A\,f^*f \oplus A\,ff^*$ span the same $2 \cdot 2^n$-dimensional space, since $a\,f^*f = a - a\,ff^*$. (2) The off-diagonal Peirce blocks contain $Af$ and $Af^*$ ($f = ff^*\cdot f = f \cdot f^*f$ places $f \in (1-P)BP$, symmetrically $f^* \in PB(1-P)$), and the dimensions ($2^n$ each, against Peirce blocks of dimension $2^n$ each in $\Mat_2(A)$) force equality. (3) $E(a) = a$ since $a \in C$. $D(a) = P a P = a\,f^*f$ (as $a$ commutes with $P$ and $P^2 = P$), which is $a$ under the natural corner isomorphism. The Peirce-coordinate reading: the $(2,2)$ entry of $\varphi(a)$ transported to the $E_{11}$ corner is $E_{12}\,a\,E_{21} = f a f^* = \hat{a}\,ff^*$, i.e.\ $\hat{a}$, as computed in Theorem \claimref{transport.rule-1-morita-trivial}. The defect formula is $D(xy) = Px(P + (1-P))yP = D(x)D(y) + Px(1-P)yP$.
